## CHAPTER XVIII. Jesus Read the Book of Isaiah in the Synagogue

**LUKE IV, 16–21.** And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and entered the synagogue according to his custom on the Sabbath day. And he rose to read, and the book of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. And when he had unrolled the book, he found the place where it was written:

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me; for this reason he has anointed me. He has sent me to evangelize the poor, to heal the brokenhearted [Note: [Col. 0266D] These words were lacking in other editions.], to proclaim release to captives and sight to the blind, to set the oppressed free, to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of recompense” (Isaiah LXI, 1–2).

And when he had folded the book, he returned it to the attendant and sat down. And the eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed upon him. And he began to say to them: “Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”

— **MATTHEW IV, 17; MARK I, 15.** From that time Jesus began to preach and say: “For the time has been fulfilled: repent and believe in the Gospel, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near.”

## CHAPTER XIX. Jesus Called Peter and Andrew, James and John [Col. 0266A]

**MATTHEW IV, 18–22.** As he was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen. And he said to them: “Come after me, and I will make you become fishers of men.” And they immediately left their nets and followed him.

And proceeding from there, he saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and John his brother, in a boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets, and he called them. And they immediately left their nets and their father and followed him.

— **LUKE V, 1–11.** Now it came to pass, when the crowd pressed upon him to hear the word of God, and he was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret, that he saw two boats standing beside the lake. But the fishermen had gone down and were washing their nets. And getting into one boat, which was Simon’s, he asked him to put out a little from the shore; and sitting down, he taught the crowds from the boat.

When he ceased speaking, he said to Simon: “Put out into the deep, and lower your nets for a catch.” And Simon answered and said to him: “Master, having labored all night, we caught nothing; but at your word I will lower the net.” And when they had done this, they enclosed a great abundance of fish. Their net was breaking. And they signaled to their companions who were in the other boat to come and help them. And they came and filled both boats, so that they were almost sinking.

When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees, saying: “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord.” [Col. 0266C] For astonishment had seized him and all who were with him, at the catch of fish which they had taken; and likewise James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon’s companions. And Jesus said to Simon: “Do not be afraid; from now on you shall catch men.”

— **JOHN II, 11.** And his disciples believed in him. And when they had brought the boats ashore, they left everything and followed him.

## CHAPTER XX. Jesus Called Matthew the Publican

**MATTHEW IX, 9; MARK II, 14; LUKE V, 27–28.** And as Jesus passed on from there, he saw a man sitting at the tax booth, named Matthew, and he said to him: “Follow me.” And he rose and, leaving everything, followed him.

## CHAPTER XXI. Hearing That John Had Been Imprisoned, Jesus Withdrew into the Territories of Zebulun and Naphtali [Col. 0266D]

**JOHN III, 22–36.** After these things Jesus and his disciples came into the land of Judea, and there he stayed with them and baptized. John also was baptizing at Aenon, near Salim, because there were many waters there; and people came and were baptized. For John had not yet been sent into prison.

Now a dispute arose between John’s disciples and the Jews concerning purification. And they came to John and said to him: “Rabbi, he who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you bore witness—behold, he is baptizing, and everyone is coming to him.”

John answered and said: “A man cannot receive anything unless it has been given to him from heaven. You yourselves bear witness to me that I said: ‘I am not the Christ, but I have been sent before him.’ He who has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices with joy because of the bridegroom’s voice. Therefore this joy of mine has been fulfilled. He must increase, but I must decrease.

“He who comes from above is above all. He who is from the earth is of the earth, and speaks from the earth. He who comes from heaven is above all. And what he has seen and heard, this he testifies; and no one accepts his testimony. He who accepts his testimony has certified that God is true. For he whom God has sent speaks the words of God. For God does not give the Spirit by measure.

“The Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hand. He who believes in the Son has eternal life; but he who is unbelieving toward the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him.”

— **JOHN IV, 1–3.** When Jesus therefore knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John—although Jesus himself did not baptize, but his disciples— [Col. 0267A]

— **MARK I, 14.** and that John had been imprisoned, he left Judea and went again into Galilee.

— **MATTHEW IV, 12–16.** When he had heard that John had been imprisoned, he withdrew into Galilee. And leaving the city of Nazareth, he came and lived in seaside Capernaum, in the territories of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, so that what had been spoken through the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled:

“Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations. The people who were sitting in darkness saw a great light; and for those sitting in the region and shadow of death, light has risen” (Isaiah IX, 1–2).

## CHAPTER XXII. Jesus Went through All the Regions, and Sitting on the Mountain Chose Twelve Disciples and Taught Them About the Blessedness of the Kingdom of Heaven and What Follows

**MATTHEW IV, 23–25.** And Jesus went throughout all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease [Col. 0267D] and every infirmity among the people. And his fame went throughout all Syria; and they brought to him all who were ill, afflicted with various diseases and torments, and those who had demons and epileptics, and he healed them. And great crowds followed him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and from beyond the Jordan.

— **LUKE IV, 42–44.** And they tried to keep him from leaving them. But he said to them: “I must evangelize the kingdom of God to the other cities also, because for this I was sent.”

And when he saw the crowds— **MATTHEW X, 2–4; MARK III, 13–19; LUKE VI, 13–16**—he went up onto the mountain, and when he had sat down he called to himself those whom he wished. And they came to him, and he made them twelve to be with him, whom he also named apostles:

Simon, whom he surnamed Peter; and Andrew his brother; and James son of Zebedee; and John the brother of James, to whom he gave the name Boanerges, which means “sons of thunder”; Philip and Bartholomew; Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus; and Simon who is called the Zealot; and Jude of James; and Judas Iscariot, who was the betrayer.

— **MATTHEW V, 1–12; LUKE VI, 20–23.** And his disciples came to him. And lifting up his eyes toward them, he opened his mouth and taught them, saying:

“Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

“Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the earth.

“Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.

“Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be satisfied.

“Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.

“Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.

“Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God.

“Blessed are those who suffer persecution for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

“Blessed are you when people curse you, hate you, persecute you, and speak every evil against you falsely for my sake; and when they separate you, reproach you, and cast out your name as evil because of the Son of Man. Rejoice on that day and exult, for your reward is great in heaven; for so they persecuted the prophets who were before you, their fathers.”

## CHAPTER XXIII. Rebuke of the Rich

[Col. 0268C] **LUKE VI, 24–26.** “Nevertheless, woe to you who are rich, for you have your consolation. Woe to you who are filled, for you shall hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, for you shall mourn and weep. Woe when people bless you [Note: [Col. 0267D] Other editions read, ‘all people.’]; for their fathers did the same to the prophets. But I say to you who hear:

## CHAPTER XXIV. You Are the Salt of the Earth

**MATTHEW V, 13; MARK IX, 49; LUKE XIV, 34.** “You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt loses its savor, with what will you season it? It is useful for nothing any longer except to be thrown out and trampled underfoot by people.

## CHAPTER XXV. You Are the Light of This World; and Further Comparisons Concerning the Precepts of the Law

[Col. 0268D] **MATTHEW V, 14–16; MARK IV, 21; LUKE VIII, 16; XI, 33.** “You are the light of the world. A city set upon a mountain cannot be hidden. Nor do they light a lamp and place it under a measuring basket, or under a bed, or in a hidden place, or under a vessel, but on a lampstand, so that it may give light to all who are in the house. Thus let your light shine before people, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.”

— **MATTHEW V, 17–20.** “Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I have not come to abolish, but to fulfill. For amen I say to you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke [Col. 0269A] will pass from the Law until everything takes place. Therefore whoever loosens one of these least commandments and teaches people to do so shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven. But whoever does and teaches them shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven. For I say to you, unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter the kingdom of heaven.

## CHAPTER XXVI. Prohibition of Anger

**MATTHEW V, 21–22.** “You have heard that it was said to the ancients: ‘You shall not kill’; and whoever kills shall be liable to judgment [Note: [Col. 0269D] Greek, τῇ κρίσει (*tē krisei*), ‘to judgment.’ The Vulgate has *judicio*, ‘to judgment.’]” (Exodus XX, 13; Deuteronomy V, 17). “But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother shall be liable to judgment. Whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ shall be liable to the council. Whoever says, ‘Fool,’ shall be liable to the fire of Gehenna.

## CHAPTER XXVII. Leaving One’s Gift at the Altar

**MATTHEW V, 23–26.** “Therefore, if you offer your gift at the altar, and there you remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and go first to be reconciled to your brother; then come and offer your gift.

“Be willing to agree quickly with your adversary, while you are on the way with him, lest perhaps your adversary hand you over to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and you be thrown into prison. Amen I say to you, you shall not come out from there until you repay the last quadrans.

## CHAPTER XXVIII. The Adultery of Desire

**MATTHEW VI, 5–15.** “And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, who love to pray standing in the synagogues and at the street corners, so that they may be seen by people. — **LUKE XI, 1–4.** Then one of his disciples said to him: “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.” And he said to them: “When you pray, say:

— **LUKE XI, 34–36.** “The lamp of your body is your eye. If your eye is simple, your whole body will be full of light. But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be dark. Therefore, if the light that is in you is darkness, how great will the darkness be?

## CHAPTER XXXVII. No One Can Serve Two Masters

**MATTHEW VI, 24.** “No one can serve two masters; for either he will hate one and love the other, or he will endure one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.

## CHAPTER XXXVIII. No One Should Be Anxious About Food or Clothing

**MATTHEW VI, 25–34; LUKE XII, 22–31.** “Therefore I say to you: Do not be anxious about your life, what you shall eat, or about your body, what you shall wear. Is not the life more than food, and the body more than clothing? Look at the birds of heaven, for they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns; [Col. 0272B] and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth more than they?

“Which of you, by thinking about it, can add one cubit to his stature? If therefore you cannot do even what is least, why are you anxious about the rest? And concerning clothing, why are you anxious? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they do not labor or spin. But I say to you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these. And if God so clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, you of little faith?

“Therefore do not be anxious, saying: ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘With what shall we be clothed?’ For the nations seek all these things. Your Father knows that you need all these things. But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, [Col. 0272C] and all these things will be added to you. Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow. For tomorrow will be anxious for itself; sufficient for the day is its own trouble.

## CHAPTER XXXIX. No One Should Judge or Condemn

**MATTHEW VII, 1–6; LUKE VI, 37–42.** “Do not judge, so that you may not be judged; for with the judgment with which you judge, you shall be judged. Do not condemn, and you shall not be condemned. Forgive, and you shall be forgiven. Give, and it shall be given to you. They will give into your lap a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and overflowing.

**MARK IV, 24.** “For with the measure with which you measure, it shall be measured back to you.

“Why do you see the speck in your brother’s eye [Col. 0272D] but do not see the beam in your own eye? Or how do you say to your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye,’ while behold, there is a beam in your own eye? Hypocrite, first remove the beam from your own eye, and then you will see to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.

“Do not give what is holy to dogs, and do not throw your pearls before swine, lest perhaps they trample them under their feet, and, turning, tear you apart.

## CHAPTER XL. The Parable of the Friend, or the Three Loaves. Asking, Knocking, Seeking

**LUKE XI, 5–13.** “Which of you will have a friend and go to him at midnight and say: ‘Friend, lend me three loaves, because a friend of mine has arrived at my house from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him’? And he, answering from within, will say: ‘Do not trouble me; the door is already shut, and my children are with me in bed. I cannot get up and give you anything.’

“And if he persists in knocking, I say to you, even if he will not rise and give him because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence he will rise and give him as many as he needs.

“I say to you:— **MATTHEW VII, 7–14.** Ask, and you shall receive; seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives; and whoever seeks finds; and to whoever knocks it shall be opened.

“Or what man is there among you who, if his son asks him for bread, will he perhaps give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, will he perhaps give him a serpent? Or [Col. 0273B] if he asks for an egg, will he perhaps give him a scorpion? Therefore, if you, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him?

“Therefore, everything whatsoever you wish people to do to you, do likewise to them. For this is the Law and the Prophets.

— **LUKE XIII, 24.** “Enter through the narrow gate; for the gate is broad and the way spacious that leads to destruction, and there are many who enter through it. How narrow the gate and constricted the way that leads to life—and there are few who find it!

## CHAPTER XLI. Guarding Against False Prophets

**MATTHEW VII, 15–20; LUKE VI, 43–45.** “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing [Col. 0273C] but inwardly are ravenous wolves. You will know them by their fruits. Do they gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles? Thus every good tree produces good fruits, but a bad tree produces bad fruits. A good tree cannot produce bad fruits, nor can a bad tree produce good fruits.

“A good person brings forth good things from the good treasure of the heart, and an evil person brings forth evil things from the evil treasure; for from the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks. Every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire. Therefore, by their fruits you will know them.

[Col. 0273D] **MATTHEW VII, 21–23; LUKE VI, 46.** “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven will enter the kingdom of heaven. Many will say to me on that day: ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and in your name cast out demons, and in your name perform many mighty works?’ And then I will declare to them: ‘I never knew you. Depart from me, you workers of iniquity.’

## CHAPTER XLIII. A Comparison in All These Matters Concerning Wise and Foolish Builders

**MATTHEW VII, 24–29; LUKE VI, 47–49.** “Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house upon rock. And [Col. 0274A] the rain fell, and the rivers came, and the winds blew, and they beat upon that house, and it did not fall, for it had been founded upon rock.

“And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them will be like a foolish man who built his house upon sand. And the rain fell, and the rivers came, and the winds blew, and they beat upon that house, and it fell, and its fall was great.”

And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, that the crowds were astonished at his teaching. For he was teaching them as one having authority, and not like their scribes and Pharisees.

[Col. 0274B] **MATTHEW 9:36.** But when he saw the crowds, he had compassion on them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.

## CHAPTER 45. In Cana of Galilee Jesus made water into wine.

[Col. 0276A] **JOHN 2:1–11.** And on the third day there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there. Jesus and his disciples were also invited to the wedding. And when the wine ran out, the mother of Jesus said to him: “They have no wine.” And Jesus said to her: “What is there between me and you, woman? My hour has not yet come.” His mother said to the attendants: “Whatever he tells you, do it.”

Now there were six stone water jars placed there for the Jewish rites of purification, each holding two or three measures. Jesus said to them: “Fill the jars with water.” And they filled them to the brim. And Jesus said to them: “Now draw some out and take it to the master of the feast.” And they took it.

[Col. 0276B] When the master of the feast tasted the water that had become wine—and he did not know where it came from, though the attendants who had drawn the water knew—the master of the feast called the bridegroom and said to him: “Everyone serves the good wine first, and when they have become drunk, then the inferior wine; but you have kept the good wine until now.” Jesus performed this beginning of signs in Cana of Galilee and manifested his glory.

## CHAPTER 46. Jesus cleanses a leper.

**MATTHEW 8:1–4; MARK 1:40–45.** When Jesus had come down from the mountain, large crowds followed him. And behold, a leper came, knelt down, and worshiped him, saying: “Lord, if you are willing, you can cleanse me.” And [Col. 0276C] Jesus stretched out his hand, touched him, and said: “I am willing; be cleansed.” And immediately his leprosy was cleansed. And Jesus said to him: “See that you tell no one, but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded (Leviticus 14:2) as a testimony to them.”

But he went out and began to proclaim and spread the report of what had happened, so that Jesus could no longer enter a city openly, but had to remain outside in deserted places. And people came to him from everywhere.

## CHAPTER 47. Jesus healed the centurion’s paralyzed servant.

**MATTHEW 8:5–13; LUKE 7:1–10.** When he had entered Capernaum, a centurion approached him, asking [Col. 0276D] him and saying: “Lord, my servant lies paralyzed at home and is suffering terribly.” And Jesus said to him: “I will come and heal him.”

And the centurion replied: “Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof, but only say the word, and my servant will be healed. For I too am a man under authority [Note: [Col. 0275D] Thus in the Greek, Matthew 8:9: ἄνθρωπός εἰμι ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν, ‘I am a man under authority.’ Ammonius expressed this passage here. But in Luke 7:8: ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν τασσόμενος, ‘placed under authority.’ Hence the Vulgate in both places: ‘placed under authority.’] and have soldiers under me. I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”

When Jesus heard this, he marveled, and said to those following him: “Truly I say to you, I have not found such faith in Israel. I say to you that many will come from the east and the west and will recline with Abraham, [Col. 0277A] Isaac [Note: [Col. 0277D] ‘and Jacob’ has dropped out of the printed editions; the Greek text and the Vulgate contain it. I would judge that the error should be attributed not to Ammonius or his translator, but rather to scribes or typesetters.], and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven. But the sons of the kingdom will be cast into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”

And Jesus said to the centurion: “Go; let it be done for you as you have believed.” And the servant was healed in that hour. And the centurion returned to his house and found the servant who had been ill in good health.

## CHAPTER 48. Jesus healed Peter’s mother-in-law of her fever.

**MATTHEW 8:14–15.** When Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw his mother-in-law lying sick with a fever. And he touched her hand, and the fever left her; and she rose and served them.

## CHAPTER 49. He raised a dead man in the city of Nain.

[Col. 0277B] **LUKE 7:11–17.** And afterward he went to a city called Nain, and his disciples and a large crowd were going with him. As he drew near the gate of the city, behold, a dead man was being carried out, the only son of his mother; and she was a widow, and a large crowd from the city was with her.

When the Lord saw her, he was moved with compassion for her and said to her: “Do not weep.” And he came near and touched the bier. Those carrying it stopped. And he said: “Young man, I say to you, arise.” And the dead man sat up and began to speak, and he gave him to his mother.

Fear seized everyone, and they glorified God, saying: “A great prophet has arisen among us,” and, “God has visited his people.” And this report about him went out throughout all Judea and the surrounding region.

## CHAPTER 50. He heals all illnesses, so that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.

[Col. 0277C] **MATTHEW 8:16–18.** When evening came, they brought him many who had demons, and he cast out the spirits by a word and healed all who were sick, so that what had been spoken through the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled: “He himself took our infirmities and bore our diseases” (Isaiah 53:4). When Jesus saw large crowds around him, he ordered them to go across the lake.

## CHAPTER 51. To one who wished to follow him he said: “Foxes have dens.”

**MATTHEW 8:19–22; LUKE 9:57–62.** A certain scribe approached and said to him: “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.” And Jesus said to him: “Foxes have dens and [Col. 0277D] birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”

And he said to another: “Follow me.” But he said: “Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father.” Jesus said to him: “Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead; but you go and announce the kingdom of God.”

And another said: “I will follow you, Lord, but first permit me to say farewell to those who are at home.” Jesus said to him: “No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”

## CHAPTER 52. While sailing, he commands the storm, and it immediately ceased.

[Col. 0278A] **MATTHEW 8:23–27; MARK 4:37–40; LUKE 8:22–25.** When he had boarded the boat, his disciples followed him. And behold, a great storm arose on the sea, so that the boat was covered by the waves; but he was sleeping in the stern on a cushion.

They approached and woke him, saying: “Lord, save us, for we are perishing.” And he said to them: “Why are you afraid, you of little faith?” Then he rose and commanded the winds and the sea, and the wind ceased. And he said: “Be silent; be still.” And there was a great calm.

The people marveled, saying: “Who—or what sort of man—is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?”

## CHAPTER 53. Across the lake he healed the demon-possessed man who lived among the tombs.

[Col. 0278B] **MATTHEW 8:28–34; 9:1; MARK 5:1–21; LUKE 8:26–39.** When he had come across the lake to the region of the Gerasenes, which lies opposite Galilee, and had gone ashore, two demon-possessed men came to meet him from the tombs, exceedingly violent, so that no one could pass along that road.

For one of them had been possessed by demons for a long time; he wore no clothing and lived not in a house but among the tombs. No one could any longer bind him, not even with chains, because he had often been bound with shackles and chains, but had broken the chains and shattered the shackles, and no one could subdue him.

[Col. 0278C] Night and day he was always among the tombs and in the mountains, crying out and cutting himself with stones. When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran to him [Note: [Col. 0278D] Greek: ἔδραμε, ‘he ran’; Vulgate: cucurrit, ‘he ran.’ And shortly afterward: ‘You have come here.’ Greek: ἦλθες ὧδε, ‘you came here.’] and worshiped him.

And crying out with a loud voice, he said: “What have you to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? Have you come to torment us before the time?”

Jesus was saying to him: “Come out, unclean spirit, from the man.” And he asked him: “What is your name?” But he said: “Legion,” because many demons had entered him.

And they begged him not to drive them out of the region and not to command them to go into the abyss. Now a large herd of pigs was grazing not far from them. The demons begged him, saying: “If you cast us out, send us into the herd of pigs.” And he said to them: “Go.”

They came out and entered the pigs; and the herd rushed violently down into the sea—about two thousand of them—and they were drowned in the sea. Those who had been tending them fled and reported everything in the city and in the countryside, including what had happened to the demon-possessed men.

And behold, the whole city came out to meet Jesus. When they saw the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting there clothed and in his right mind at his feet, they were afraid. And they begged him to leave their territory.

As he was boarding the boat, the man from whom the demons had gone out begged him to let him be with him. But he did not permit him, saying: “Go to your house and your own people, and tell them how much the Lord has done for you and how he had mercy on you.”

And he went away, proclaiming throughout the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him; and everyone marveled. And he boarded the boat, crossed over, and came to his own city.

## CHAPTER 54. He healed the paralytic whom they lowered through the roof.

[Col. 0279A] **MATTHEW 9:2–8; MARK 2:3–12; LUKE 5:18–26.** And behold, four men were carrying on a bed a man who was paralyzed, and they sought to bring him in and place him before Jesus. When they could not find a way to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up onto the roof and lowered him, with his bed, through the tiles into the middle, before Jesus.

When he saw their faith, he said to the paralytic: “Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven.” And the scribes and Pharisees began to think, saying: “Who is this man who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins [Col. 0279B] except God alone?”

When Jesus knew their thoughts, he answered and said to them: “Why are you thinking evil in your hearts? Which is easier to say: ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say: ‘Rise and walk’? But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralytic—“I say to you, rise, take up your bed, and go to your house.”

And he immediately rose before them, picked up the bed on which he had been lying, and went to his house glorifying God. Amazement seized them all, and they glorified God and were filled with fear, saying: “We have seen extraordinary things today.” And they glorified God, who had given such authority to human beings.

## CHAPTER 55. He healed the royal official’s absent son.

[Col. 0279C] **JOHN 4:46–53.** He came again to Cana of Galilee, where he had made water into wine. And there was a certain royal official whose son was ill at Capernaum. When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea into Galilee, he went to him and begged him to come down and heal his son, for he was beginning to die.

Jesus therefore said to him: “Unless you see signs and wonders, you will not believe.” The royal official said to him: “Lord, come down before my son dies.” Jesus said to him: “Go; your son lives.”

The man believed the word that Jesus had said to him, and he went. As he was already going down, his servants met him and reported that his son was alive. He asked them at what hour he had begun to improve, and they said to him: “Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.” Therefore the father knew that it was at that very hour when Jesus had said to him: “Your son lives.” And he himself and his entire household believed.

## CHAPTER 56. Levi the tax collector prepared a banquet for him. And the scribes and Pharisees said to his disciples: “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

[Col. 0279D] **MATTHEW 9:9–17; LUKE 5:29–39; MARK 2:16–22.** And Levi prepared a great banquet for him in his house. And while he was reclining at table in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and reclined with Jesus and his disciples. For there were many who also followed him.

When the scribes and Pharisees saw that he was eating with sinners and tax collectors, they said [Col. 0280A] to his disciples: “Why does your teacher eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”

When Jesus heard this, he said to them: “Those who are well do not need a physician, but those who are sick. Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice’ (Hosea 6:6). For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

They said to him: “Why do the disciples of John fast frequently and offer prayers, and likewise those of the Pharisees, while yours eat and drink and do not fast?”

He said to them: “Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast. But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them; then they will fast in those days.”

He also gave them an analogy: “No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment; otherwise the new patch takes away from the old garment, and a worse tear results. And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the new wine will burst the wineskins, and the wine will spill out, and the wineskins will be ruined. Rather, new wine must be put into new wineskins, and both are preserved. And no one who has drunk old wine immediately desires new, for he says: ‘The old is better.’”

## CHAPTER 57. The scribes ask him for a sign, and he says many things to them.

[Col. 0280B] **MATTHEW 12:38–45.** Then certain scribes and Pharisees answered him, saying: “Teacher, we wish to see a sign from you.” He answered them:

**LUKE 11:29–32.** “This evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given it except the sign of the prophet Jonah. [Col. 0280C] For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea creature for three days and three nights, so will the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights.

The men of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the preaching of Jonah. And behold, something greater than Jonah is here.

The queen of the South will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon. And behold, something greater than Solomon is here.”

**LUKE 11:24–26.** “When an unclean spirit has gone out from a person, it travels through dry places, seeking rest, and does not find it. Then it says: ‘I will return to my house from which I came.’ And when it comes, it finds it vacant, swept clean, and put in order.

Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they enter and dwell there. And the final condition of that person becomes worse than the first. So it will also be with this most wicked generation.”

## CHAPTER 58. A certain woman from the crowd cried out to Jesus: “Blessed is the womb that bore you.”

[Col. 0280D] **LUKE 11:27–28.** As he was saying these things, a certain woman from the crowd raised her voice and said to him: “Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breasts that nursed you.”

But he said: “Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it.”

## CHAPTER 59. Jesus is told: “Your mother and your brothers wish to see you.”

**MATTHEW 12:46–50; MARK 3:31–35; LUKE 8:19–21.** While he was still speaking to the crowds, behold, his mother and his brothers were standing outside, seeking to speak with him. Someone said to him: “Behold, your mother and your brothers are standing outside, seeking you.”

But he answered the one who told him and said: “Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?” And stretching out his hand toward his disciples, he said: “Behold, my mother and my brothers. For whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven is my brother, sister, and mother.”

## CHAPTER 60. Jesus healed the woman who suffered from a flow of blood and raised Jairus’s daughter, the ruler of the synagogue, from the dead.

[Col. 0281A] **MATTHEW 9:18–26; MARK 5:22–43; LUKE 8:41–56.** While he was saying these things to them, behold, one of the rulers of the synagogue, named Jairus, approached and worshiped him, saying: “My daughter has just died; but come, lay your hand on her, and she will live.”

Jesus rose and followed him, as did his disciples. And behold, a woman who had suffered from a flow of blood for twelve years, and had endured much at the hands of many physicians and spent all she had, yet could be healed by no one, but had grown worse, came up behind him in the crowd and touched the fringe of his garment.

For she was saying within herself: “If I only touch his garment, I will be saved.” And immediately the flow of blood stopped, and she felt in her body that she had been healed from the affliction.

And immediately Jesus, knowing in himself the power that had gone out from him, turned toward the crowds and said: “Who touched me?” When everyone denied it, Peter and those who were with him said: “Master, the crowds press in and crowd around you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”

And Jesus said: “Someone touched me, for I too know that power has gone out from me.” And he looked around to see the woman who had done this.

When the woman saw that she had not escaped notice, she came trembling and fell before his feet. In the presence of all the people she declared why she had touched him and how she had been healed immediately. And he said to her: “Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace and be healed of your affliction.”

While he was still speaking, someone came from the ruler of the synagogue’s house and said to him: “Your daughter is dead; why trouble the teacher any further?” When Jesus heard this message, he said to the ruler of the synagogue: “Do not fear; only believe, and she will be saved.”

And he did not permit anyone to follow him except Peter, James, and John, the brother of James. [Col. 0281D] When he came to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, he saw flute players and a crowd making a commotion, weeping and wailing loudly.

When he entered, he said: “Go away; the girl is not dead, but sleeping.” And they mocked him, knowing that she was dead.

But after putting everyone out, he took the girl’s father and mother and those who were with him and entered where the girl was lying. And holding her hand, he said to her: “Talitha, cumi”—which is translated: “Girl—I say to you—arise.”

And her spirit returned. Immediately the girl rose and walked. She was twelve years old. And everyone was overcome with great astonishment. And he strictly ordered them that no one should know this. And he commanded that she be given something to eat. And this report spread throughout that entire land.

## CHAPTER 61. He healed two blind men and cast out a deaf and mute demon.

[Col. 0282A] **MATTHEW 9:27–33.** As Jesus was passing on from there, two blind men followed him, crying out and saying: “Have mercy on us, Son of David.” When he had come into the house, the blind men approached him. And Jesus said to them: “Do you believe that I can do this for you?” They said to him: “Yes, Lord.”

Then he touched their eyes, saying: “Let it be done for you according to your faith.” And their eyes were opened. And Jesus sternly warned them, saying: “See that no one knows.” But they went out and spread his fame throughout that entire land.

When they had gone out, behold, they brought him a mute man who had a demon. And when the demon had been cast out, the mute man spoke. And the crowds marveled, saying: “Such a thing has never appeared in Israel.” [Col. 0282B]

**MATTHEW 12:23.** “Can this be the Son of David?”

## CHAPTER 62. The Pharisees say about Jesus: “He casts out demons by Beelzebub, the prince of demons.”

**MATTHEW 12:24–37; MARK 3:22–30; LUKE 11:17–22.** The Pharisees were saying: “This man casts out demons by Beelzebub, the prince of demons.”

But when he saw their thoughts, he said to them: “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and every city divided against itself will not stand. If Satan is also divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? It cannot stand, but has an end, because you say that I cast out demons by Beelzebub.

And if I cast out demons by Beelzebub, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges. But if I cast out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has certainly come upon you.

Or how can someone enter the strong man’s house and plunder his goods in which he trusted, unless he first binds the strong man? Then he will plunder his house.

Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters. Therefore I say to you: every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven people, but blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.

Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the age to come.

Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad, for the tree is known by its fruit. Brood of vipers, how can you speak good things when you are evil? For the mouth speaks from the abundance of the heart.

A good person brings good things out of a good treasure, and an evil person brings evil things out of an evil treasure. But I say to you: for every idle word that people speak, they will give an account on the day of judgment. For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”

## CHAPTER 63. Martha received Jesus into her house.

[Col. 0282C] **LUKE 10:38–42.** As they were traveling, Jesus entered a certain village, and a woman named Martha welcomed him into her house. And she had a sister named Mary, who also sat at the feet of the Lord Jesus and listened to his word.

But Martha was busy with much serving. She came and said: “Lord, is it no concern to you that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her, therefore, to help me.”

The Lord answered and said to her: “Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things. But one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the better portion, and it will not be taken away from her.”

## CHAPTER 64. John sent from prison to Jesus to question him.

[Col. 0283A] **MATTHEW 11:2–19; LUKE 7:18–35.** When John heard in prison about the works of Christ, he summoned two of his disciples and sent them to Jesus, saying: “Are you the one who is to come, or should we expect another?”

(At that very hour he healed many people of illnesses and afflictions and evil spirits, and he granted sight to many blind people.)

He answered them: “Go and report to John what you have seen and heard: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear (Isaiah 35:5), the dead are raised, and the poor are evangelized. And blessed is whoever is not offended because of me.”

When they had departed, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind? But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Behold, those who are in splendid clothing and luxury are in royal houses.

But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet. This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I am sending my angel before your face, [Col. 0283C] who will prepare your way before you’ (Malachi 3:1).

Truly I say to you: among those born of women no prophet has arisen greater than John the Baptist. But the one who is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

And all the people who heard, including the tax collectors, justified God, having been baptized with John’s baptism. But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected God’s purpose for themselves, not having been baptized by him.

From the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and the violent seize it. For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.

And if you are willing to accept it, he is Elijah who is to come. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.

But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplace, calling to their companions and saying: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a lament, and you did not mourn.’

For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say: ‘He has a demon.’ The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say: ‘Behold, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.’ Yet wisdom has been justified by her children.”

## CHAPTER 65. He reproaches the cities in which most of his miracles had been performed.

[Col. 0283D] **MATTHEW 11:20–24; LUKE 10:12–15.** Then he began to reproach the cities in which most of his miracles had been performed, because they had not repented.

“Woe to you, Corazin [Note: [Col. 0283D] Chorazin: in the Greek of Matthew 11:21, Χοραζίν; in Luke 10:13, Χωραζίν. Eusebius, in *On the Situation and Names of the Places in Sacred Scripture*, has Χωραζέιν. Nevertheless, the Vulgate reading Corozain or Chorozain is confirmed by other Greek manuscripts, whether handwritten or printed. So too does Jerome have it in *On Hebrew Names*.]; woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would long ago have repented in sackcloth and ashes.

Nevertheless I say to you: it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.

And you, Capernaum, will you be exalted to heaven? You will descend to the underworld. For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Sodom, it might have remained to this day. Nevertheless I say to you: it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom on the day of judgment than for you.”

## CHAPTER 66. The apostles return to Jesus from preaching.

[Col. 0284A] **MARK 6:30–31; LUKE 9:10.** When the apostles came to Jesus, they reported to him everything they had done and taught. And he said to them: “Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest for a little while.” For many were coming, and they did not even have time to eat.

## CHAPTER 67. Jesus chose another seventy-two disciples. He adds the parable of the person building a tower and of a king preparing for battle.

[Col. 0284B] **LUKE 10:1, 16–23.** After this the Lord appointed another seventy-two and sent them in pairs ahead of him into every city and place where he himself was about to go. And he said to them: “Whoever hears you hears me, and whoever rejects you rejects me. But whoever rejects me rejects him who sent me.”

The seventy-two returned with joy, saying: “Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name.” And he said to them: “I was watching Satan fall like lightning from heaven. Behold, I have given you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you.

Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you; rejoice instead that your names are written in heaven.”

At that very hour he rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said:

**MATTHEW 11:27–30.** “I confess to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and intelligent and revealed them to little ones. Yes, Father, because this was pleasing before you.

Everything has been handed over to me by my Father. And no one knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son wishes to reveal him.”

And turning to his disciples, he said: “Come to me, all who labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you. Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, because I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”

[Col. 0284D] **LUKE 14:20–33; MATTHEW 10:37–39.** “If anyone comes to me and does not hate his father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters, and even his own life, he cannot be my disciple. And whoever does not carry his cross and come after me cannot be my disciple.

For which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the cost required, to see whether he has enough to complete it? Otherwise, after he has laid the foundation and is unable to finish, all who see it will begin to mock him, saying: ‘This man began to build and was unable to finish.’

Or what king, going to wage war against another king, does not first sit down and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one who comes against him with twenty thousand? Otherwise, while he is still far away, he sends a delegation and asks for terms of peace.

So therefore, every one of you who does not renounce all that he possesses cannot be my disciple.”

## CHAPTER 68. The Pharisees accused his disciples.

[Col. 0285B] **MATTHEW XII, 1–6; MARK II, 23–28; LUKE VI, 1–5.** And it came to pass on the second-first Sabbath, as Jesus was passing through the grainfields, that his disciples, being hungry, plucked the ears of grain and ate them, rubbing them in their hands. But some of the Pharisees said to them: “Why are you doing what is not lawful on the Sabbaths?” And he answered them: “Have you not even read what David did when he was hungry, he and those who were with him: how he entered the house of God, took the bread of the Presence, ate it, and gave it to those who were with him—bread which it was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those with him, but only for the priests?” And he said to them: “The Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.” Or have you not read in the Law that on the Sabbaths the priests in the temple violate the Sabbath and are without blame? But I tell you that here there is one greater than the temple. The Sabbath was made for man, and not man for the Sabbath.

**CHAPTER LXIX. He healed a withered hand in the synagogue on the Sabbath.**

**LUKE VI, 6–11; MATTHEW XII, 10–12; MARK III, 1–5.** It came to pass also on another Sabbath that he entered the synagogue and taught. And there was a man there whose right hand was withered. The scribes and Pharisees were watching whether he would heal on the Sabbath, so that they might find grounds for accusing him. But he knew their thoughts. And he said to the man who had the withered hand: “Rise and stand in the midst.” And he rose and stood. Then Jesus said to them: “I ask you whether it is lawful on the Sabbaths to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?” But they were silent. And, looking around at them all, he said to the man: “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched it out; and his hand was restored to health, just like the other. And he said to them: “What man among you, having one sheep, if it falls into a pit on the Sabbaths, will not take hold of it and lift it out? How much better is a man than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbaths.” But they were filled with folly and discussed with one another what they might do to Jesus.

Jesus, therefore, knowing this, withdrew from there; and many followed him, and he healed them all. And he charged them not to make him known, so that what had been spoken through the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled:

“Behold, my servant whom I have chosen,  
my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased.  
I will put my Spirit upon him,  
and he will announce judgment to the nations.  
He will not contend, nor cry out,  
nor will anyone hear his voice in the streets.  
He will not break a bruised reed,  
nor extinguish a smoldering wick,  
until he brings judgment forth to victory.  
And in his name the nations will hope” (Isaiah XLII, 1–4).

**CHAPTER LXX. Jesus prays on the mountain and, beside the sea, speaks many things in parables to the crowds and his disciples.**

**LUKE VI, 12–13.** Now it came to pass in those days that he went out onto the mountain to pray, and he spent the night in prayer to God. And when day came, he called his disciples.

---**MATTHEW XIII, 1–3.** And leaving the house, he sat beside the sea; and great crowds gathered to him, [Col. 0286B] so that he entered a boat and sat down. And the whole crowd stood on the shore, and he spoke many things to them in parables, saying:

**CHAPTER LXXI. Behold, the sower went out to sow.**

**MATTHEW XIII, 3–9; MARK IV, 3–9; LUKE VIII, 5–8.** “Behold, the sower went out to sow his seed. And as he sowed, some fell beside the road, and were trampled; and the birds of the air came and ate them. Others fell upon rocky ground, and they did not have much soil; and immediately they sprang up, because they had no depth of soil. But when the sun rose, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered. Others fell among thorns; and the thorns grew up and choked them. But others fell upon good soil and yielded fruit: one a hundredfold, another sixtyfold, another thirtyfold.” Saying this, he cried out: “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”

**CHAPTER LXXII. Concerning the one who sows good seed in his field, and concerning the weeds.**

**MATTHEW XIII, 24–30; MARK IV, 26–29.** He set before them another parable, saying: “The kingdom of heaven has become like a man who sowed good seed in his field. But while the men were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat, and went away. And when the grass had grown and produced fruit, then the weeds also appeared. The servants of the master of the household came and said to him: ‘Lord, did you not sow good seed in your field? Where then did it get weeds?’ And he said to them: ‘An enemy has done this.’ The servants said to him: ‘Do you want us to go and gather them?’ But he said: ‘No, lest while gathering the weeds you uproot the wheat along with them. Let both grow until the harvest, and at harvest time I will say to the reapers: Gather the weeds first and bind them into bundles to burn; but gather the wheat into my barn.’”

**CHAPTER LXXIII. Concerning the mustard seed.**

**MATTHEW XIII, 31–32; MARK IV, 30–32; LUKE XIII, 18–19.** He set before them another parable, saying: “To what is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it? Or to what parable shall we compare it? It is like a mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his garden. It is the smallest of all vegetables, yet it becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and dwell in its branches.”

**CHAPTER LXXIV. Concerning the leaven that a woman hid; and many other things he explains to the disciples.**

**MATTHEW XIII, 33–35; MARK IV, 33; LUKE XIII, 21.** He spoke another parable to them: “The kingdom of heaven is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until the whole was leavened.”

Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables. And with many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear; and without parables he did not speak to them, so that what had been spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying (Psalm LXXVII, 2): “I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.”

---**MATTHEW XIII, 10–17; MARK IV, 10–12; LUKE VIII, 9–10; X, 23–24.** And his disciples came and said to him: “Why do you speak to them in parables?” He answered them: “Because it has been given to you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.” Apart from them, he explained everything to his own disciples.

“Therefore I speak to them in parables: because, though seeing, they do not see; and though hearing, they do not hear, nor do they understand. And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of the prophet Isaiah, which says:

‘You will hear with hearing and will not understand;  
and seeing, you will see and will not see.  
For the heart of this people has grown fat,  
and they have heard heavily with their ears,  
and they have closed their eyes,  
lest at some time they should see with their eyes,  
understand with their heart,  
be converted, and I heal them’” (Isaiah VI, 9–10).

“But blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear. For truly I tell you that many prophets and righteous people desired to see what you see, and did not see it; and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it.”

**CHAPTER LXXV. He explains the parable of the sower to the disciples.**

**MATTHEW XIII, 18–23; MARK IV, 13–20; LUKE VIII, 11–15.** “You, therefore, hear the parable of the sower. Everyone who hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it: the evil one comes and snatches away what has been sown in his heart. This is the one sown beside the road.

“The one sown upon rocky ground is the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy; but he has no root in himself and is temporary. When tribulation and persecution arise because of the word, he is immediately scandalized.

“The one sown among thorns is the one who hears the word; but the anxiety of this age and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and it becomes fruitless.

“But the one sown upon good soil is the one who hears the word and understands it, and bears fruit and produces, in one case a hundredfold, in another sixtyfold, and in another thirtyfold.”

**CHAPTER LXXVI. The one who sows seed and goes to sleep or rises; and he explains to the disciples the parable of the weeds of the field.**

**MARK IV, 26–29.** “So is the kingdom of God: as if a man casts seed upon the earth, and sleeps and rises, night and day, while the seed germinates and grows, though he does not know how. For the earth bears fruit of itself: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear. And when it has produced the fruit, he immediately puts in the sickle, because the harvest has arrived.”

---**MATTHEW XIII, 36–43.** Then, having dismissed the crowds, he came into the house; and his disciples came to him, saying: “Explain to us the parable of the weeds of the field.” He answered: “The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man. The field is the world. The good seed—these are the children of the kingdom. The weeds are the children of the evil one. The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the completion of the age, and the reapers are angels.

“Therefore, just as the weeds are gathered and burned with fire, so will it be at the completion of the age. The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather from his kingdom all offenses and those who commit iniquity, and they will cast them into the furnace of fire; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”

**CHAPTER LXXVII. Concerning the treasure hidden in the field and the trading in pearls; concerning the net cast into the sea; and concerning the master of the household who brings forth new and old things from his treasure.**

**MATTHEW XIII, 44–53.** “The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden in a field. When a man finds it, he hides it; and for joy over it he goes and sells everything he has and buys that field.

“Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant seeking good pearls. When he found one precious pearl, he went away and sold everything he had and bought it.

“Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net cast into the sea, gathering fish of every kind. When it was full, they drew it out and, sitting beside the shore, selected the good into their vessels [Note: In the Latin Vulgate, in accordance with the Greek, *sua* (‘their own’) is lacking.], but threw the bad outside.

“So will it be at the completion of the age. The angels will go out and separate the wicked from among the righteous, and cast them into the furnace of fire; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

“Have you understood all these things?” They said to him: “Yes.” He said to them: “Therefore every learned scribe in the kingdom of heaven is like a master of a household who brings forth from his treasure new things and old.”

And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these parables, that he departed from there.

**CHAPTER LXXVIII. His fellow citizens were indignant against Jesus, saying: “Where did this man get such knowledge?”**

**MATTHEW XIII, 54–58; MARK VI, 1–6.** And coming into his own country, he taught them in their synagogues, so that they were astonished and said: “Where did this man get this wisdom and such mighty works, which are performed through his hands? Is this not the craftsman’s son? Is not his mother called Mary, and his brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas? And are not all his sisters with us? Where, then, did this man get all these things?” And they were scandalized by him.

---**LUKE IV, 23–30.** And he said to them: “Certainly you will say to me this proverb: ‘Physician, heal yourself. The things we have heard were done in Capernaum, do here also in your own country.’” But he said—

---**JOHN IV, 44.** “Truly I tell you that no prophet is accepted in his own country and in his own house.”

And he did not perform many mighty works there because of their unbelief, except that he healed a few sick people by laying his hands upon them. And he marveled because of their unbelief.

“Truly I tell you: there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when heaven was shut up for three years and six months, when a great famine occurred throughout the whole land; and Elijah was sent to none of them except to a widow woman at Zarephath of Sidon” (3 Kings XVII, 9). “And there were many lepers in Israel under the prophet Elisha (4 Kings V, 14), and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.”

And everyone in the synagogue was filled with anger when they heard this. They rose up and drove him outside the city, and led him to the brow of the mountain upon which their city had been built, in order to throw him down. But he, passing through the midst of them, went away.

**CHAPTER LXXIX. Concerning Herod’s banquet and the killing of John.**

**MATTHEW XIV, 3–12; MARK VI, 17–29; LUKE III, 19–20.** At that time Herod the tetrarch sent for John, seized him, and bound him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother, because he had married her. For John was saying to Herod: “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”

Herodias was plotting against him and wanted to kill him, but could not; for she feared the people, because they regarded him as a prophet. Herod likewise, wishing to kill him, was afraid, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man; and he protected him. And after hearing him, he did many things and gladly listened to him.

When a suitable day arrived, Herod made a dinner on his birthday for the rulers and tribunes and the leading men of Galilee. And when the daughter of Herodias herself had entered, danced, and pleased Herod and those reclining with him, the king said to the girl: “Ask me for whatever you wish, and I will give it to you.” And he swore to her: “Whatever you ask, I will give you, even half of my kingdom.”

When she had gone out, she said to her mother: “What shall I ask for?” And she said: “The head of John the Baptist.”

And when she had immediately entered the king with haste, she asked, saying: “I want you to give me at once the head of John the Baptist on a platter.” The king was grieved because of the oath and because of those reclining with him, but he did not wish to sadden her. He sent an executioner and beheaded John in prison. His head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, and she gave it to her mother.

His disciples came, took his body, and buried it in a tomb. And they came and reported it to Jesus.

---**MATTHEW XIV, 1–2; MARK VI, 14–16; LUKE IX, 7–8.** Herod heard the report about Jesus and everything that was being done by him, and he was perplexed, because some were saying that John had risen from the dead, others that Elijah had appeared, and still others that one of the ancient prophets had risen. And Herod said: “I beheaded John; but who is this man about whom I hear such things?” And he sought to see him.

---**MATTHEW XIV, 13–14.** When Jesus heard this, he withdrew from there in a boat to a deserted place apart. And when the crowds heard, they followed him on foot from the cities. And going out, he saw a great crowd, had compassion on them, and healed their sick.

**CHAPTER LXXX. [Col. 0290B] In the desert Jesus fed five thousand men with five loaves and two fish.**

**MATTHEW XIV, 15–23; MARK VI, 35–46; LUKE IX, 12–17; JOHN VI, 5–15.** When evening had come, the twelve approached him and said: “Dismiss the crowds, so that they may go to the villages and hamlets nearby, turn aside, and find food, because we are here in a deserted place.” But Jesus said to them: “They do not need to go; you give them something to eat.”

Philip answered him: “Two hundred denarii worth of bread would not be enough for them, so that each might receive even a little.” And he said to them: “How many loaves do you have?” One of his disciples, Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, said to him: “There is one boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish. But what are these among so many? Unless perhaps we ourselves should go and buy food for all this crowd.”

He said to them: “Bring them here to me.” And he ordered them to make everyone recline in groups upon the green grass. And they reclined in sections, by hundreds and by fifties.

Having taken the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke them, and distributed them to his disciples; and the disciples distributed them to the crowds. And they all ate and were satisfied. And they took up the leftovers: twelve baskets full of fragments.

The number of those who had eaten was five thousand men, apart from women and children. And immediately he ordered the disciples to get into the boat [Note: Both Matthew XIV, 22, and Mark VI, 45, have the Greek *ēnagkase* (ἠνάγκασε), “he compelled, forced.” But Ammonius, who chiefly follows Matthew, rightly read in his copy *tous mathētas embēnai* (τοὺς μαθητὰς ἐμβῆναι), “the disciples to embark,” rather than, as all published Greek texts have it, *tous mathētas autou* (τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ), “his disciples.” Origen likewise read with Ammonius in volume I of his *Commentary*, p. 240. Hence the Vulgate reading, “he compelled the disciples to embark,” is confirmed; the Persian translation also agrees with it, while the remaining Greek witnesses perhaps imitate the current text restored from Mark. See Huet, the distinguished editor of the Origenian exegetical works, in the notes, p. 33.] and go ahead of him across the strait to Bethsaida, until he dismissed the crowds.

Those men, when they had seen the sign that he had performed, were saying: “This is truly the prophet who is to come into the world.” Therefore Jesus, when he realized that they were about to come and seize him and make him king, fled. And having dismissed the crowd, he went up onto the mountain alone to pray.

**CHAPTER LXXXI. Jesus walked upon the sea and rescued Peter as he was sinking.**

**MATTHEW XIV, 23–33; MARK VI, 47–51; JOHN VI, 16–21.** When evening had come, he was there alone. But the boat was being tossed in the middle of the sea by the waves, for the wind was contrary. During the fourth watch of the night, seeing them laboring, he came to them, walking upon the sea. And he wanted to pass them by.

When they saw him walking upon the sea, they were troubled, saying: “It is a phantom,” and out of fear they cried out. Immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying: “Take courage; it is I. Do not be afraid.”

Peter answered and said: “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you upon the waters.” He said: “Come.” And Peter, descending from the boat, walked upon the water to come to Jesus. But when he saw the strong wind, he was afraid. And when he began to sink, he cried out, saying: “Lord, save me!”

And immediately Jesus stretched out his hand, took hold of him, [Col. 0291B] and said to him: “You of little faith, why did you doubt?” And when he had * entered the boat, the wind ceased. And immediately the ship was at the land to which they were going.

Those who were in the boat came and worshiped him, saying: “Truly you are the Son of God.”

**CHAPTER LXXXII. Crossing over, they came to the land of Gennesaret; and the crowds followed him across the sea.**

**MATTHEW XIV, 34–36; MARK VI, 53–56.** And when they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret [Note: The Vulgate has *Genesar*. Millius gives the reading *Gennasar*, with two n’s.]. And when the men of that place recognized him, they sent throughout that entire region and brought to him all who were ill. And they begged him that they might touch even the fringe of his garment. And as many as touched it were made whole.

---**JOHN VI, 22–72.** The next day, the crowd that stood across the sea saw that there was no other boat there except one, and that Jesus had not entered the boat with his disciples, but that his disciples alone had departed. Other boats, however, had come from Tiberias, near the place where they had eaten the bread after giving thanks to the Lord.

When the crowd therefore saw that Jesus was not there, nor his disciples, they got into the boats and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus. And when they had found him across the sea, they said to him: “Rabbi, when did you come here?”

Jesus answered them and said: “Truly, truly I tell you: you seek me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate from the loaves and were satisfied. Work not for food that perishes, but for food that remains unto eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you; for God the Father has sealed him” [Col. 0291D] (Matthew III, 17; XVII, 5).

Therefore they said to him: “What shall we do, so that we may perform the works of God?” Jesus answered and said to them: “This is the work of God: that you believe in him whom he has sent.”

Therefore they said to him: “What sign, then, do you perform, so that we may see and believe you? What do you work? Our fathers ate manna in the desert, as it is written: ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat’” (Exodus XVI, 14).

Therefore Jesus said to them: “Truly, truly I tell you: Moses did not give you bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven. For the bread of God is the one who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.”

Therefore they said to him: “Lord, always give us this bread.”

Jesus said to them: “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not hunger, and whoever believes in me will never thirst” (Ecclesiasticus XXIV, 29). “But I told you that you have both seen me and have not believed” [Note: The Vulgate has *et non creditis*, “and you do not believe.” Nor does the Greek differ: *kai ou pisteuete* (καὶ οὐ πιστεύετε), “and you do not believe.”].

“All that the Father gives me will come to me; and whoever comes to me I will not cast out, because I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me. This is the will of the Father who sent me: that of all that he has given me, I should lose nothing, but raise it up on the last day. For this is the will of my Father who sent me: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life; and I will raise him up on the last day.”

Therefore the Jews murmured about him because he had said: “I am the bread that came down from heaven.” And they said—

---**MATTHEW XIII, 55; MARK VI, 3.** “Is this not the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How, then, does he say: ‘I have come down from heaven’?”

Therefore Jesus answered: “Do not murmur among yourselves. No one can come to me unless my Father [Note: The Greek has *ho Patēr ho pempsas me* (ὁ Πατὴρ ὁ πέμψας με), “the Father who sent me”; so also the Vulgate: “the Father who sent me.”] draws him; and I will raise him up on the last day.

“It is written in the prophets: ‘And they will all be taught by God’” (Isaiah LIV, 13). “Everyone who has heard from the Father and learned comes to me. Not that anyone has seen the Father, except the one who is from God; he has seen the Father.

“Truly, truly I tell you: whoever believes in me has eternal life. I am the bread of life. Your fathers ate manna in the desert and died. This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that if anyone eats of it, he may not die. I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. And the bread that I will give is my flesh for the life of the world.”

Therefore the Jews argued among themselves, saying: “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?”

Therefore Jesus said to them: “Truly, truly I tell you: unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you will not have life in yourselves. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day. For my flesh is truly food, and my blood is truly drink. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in him. Just as the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, so whoever eats me will himself live because of me.

“This is the bread that came down from heaven. It is not as your fathers ate manna and died: whoever eats this bread will live forever.”

He said these things while teaching in the synagogue at Capernaum.

Therefore many of his disciples, hearing this, said: “This is a hard saying; who can hear it?”

But Jesus, knowing in himself that his disciples were murmuring about this, said to them: “Does this scandalize you? What, then, if you see the Son of Man ascending where he was before? It is the Spirit who gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words that I have spoken to you are spirit and life.

“But there are some among you who do not believe.” For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were who did not believe [Note: In other editions the negative particle was missing. We have restored it in accordance with the Greek and the Latin Vulgate.], and who would betray him.

And he said: “Therefore I told you that no one can come to me unless it has been granted to him by my Father.”

From that time many of his disciples went back and no longer walked with him. Therefore Jesus said to the twelve: “Do you also want to go away?”

Simon Peter answered: “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life. And we have believed and have come to know that you are the Christ, the Son of God.”

Jesus answered them: “Did I not choose you twelve? And one of you is a devil.” He was speaking of Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon; for he was about to betray him, though he was one of the twelve.

**CHAPTER LXXXIII. A certain Pharisee invited Jesus to lunch and wondered why he had not been baptized.**

**LUKE XI, 37–41.** A certain Pharisee invited him to dine with him. And he entered and reclined. But the Pharisee began to reason within himself, saying why he had not been baptized before lunch. And the Lord said to him: “Now you Pharisees cleanse what is outside the cup and the dish, but what is within you is full of robbery and wickedness. Fools! Did not the one who made what is outside also make what is within? Nevertheless, give what remains as alms, and behold, everything will be clean for you.”

**CHAPTER LXXXIV. Concerning the Apostles, why they ate without washing their hands.**

**MATTHEW XV, 1–20; MARK VII, 1–23.** The Pharisees and some of the scribes, coming from Jerusalem, saw some of his disciples eating bread with common hands—that is, unwashed hands—and they found fault, saying: “Why do your disciples transgress the traditions of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread.”

But he answered them: “Why do you also transgress the commandment of God because of your tradition? For God said: ‘Honor your father and your mother’ (Exodus XX, 12; Deuteronomy V, 16); and: ‘Whoever curses father or mother shall die the death’ (Exodus XXI, 17; Leviticus XX, 20).

“But you say: ‘Whatever gift is from me will benefit you’; and he does not honor his father or his mother. Thus you have invalidated the commandment of God because of your tradition.

“For the Pharisees and all the Jews, unless they wash their hands frequently, do not eat, holding to the traditions of the elders; and when they return from the marketplace, unless they wash themselves, they do not eat. And there are many other things handed down to them to observe: the washings of cups, pitchers, bronze vessels, and beds, and many other similar things they do.

“You have invalidated the commandment of God because of your tradition. Hypocrites, Isaiah prophesied well concerning you, saying: ‘This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me’ (Isaiah XXIX, 13). ‘In vain do they worship me, teaching doctrines and commandments of men.’

“For abandoning the commandment of God, you hold the tradition of men.”

And calling the crowds to himself, he said to them: “Hear and understand: it is not what enters the mouth that defiles a person.”

Then his disciples approached and said to him: “Do you know that the Pharisees, when they heard this saying, were scandalized?”

But he answered: “Every plant that my heavenly Father has not planted will be uprooted. Leave them; they are blind guides of the blind. And if the blind leads the blind, both will fall into a pit.”

And when he had entered the house away from the crowd, Peter asked him: “Explain this parable to us.”

But he said: “Are you also still without understanding? Do you not understand that everything that enters the mouth goes into the stomach and is discharged into the latrine? But the things that proceed from the mouth come out of the heart, and these defile a person.

“For from the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false testimonies, greed, wickedness, deceit, indecency, an evil eye, blasphemies, pride, foolishness. These are the things that defile a person. But to eat with unwashed hands does not defile a person.”

**CHAPTER LXXXV. Concerning the Syrophoenician woman who asked on behalf of her daughter.**

**MATTHEW XV, 21–28; MARK VII, 24–30.** And rising from there, he went away into the region of Tyre and Sidon. And behold, a Gentile Canaanite woman, Syrophoenician by race, cried out, saying: “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is grievously tormented by a demon.”

But he did not answer her a word. And his disciples approached and begged him, saying: “Send her away, because she cries out after us.”

But he answered: “I was not sent except to the sheep that have perished from the house of Israel.”

But she came and worshiped him, saying: “Lord, help me.”

He said to her: “Let the children be satisfied first; for it is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”

But she said: “Yes, Lord; for even the little dogs eat from the crumbs that fall from their masters’ table.”

Then Jesus answered and said to her: “O woman, great is your faith; let it be done for you as you wish.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.

**CHAPTER LXXXVI. Jesus healed a deaf and mute man.**

**MARK VII, 31–37.** And again, going out from the region of Tyre, he came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the midst of the region of the Decapolis. And they brought him a deaf and mute man, and they begged him to lay his hand upon him.

And taking him aside from the crowd, he put his fingers into his ears, and, spitting, touched his tongue. And looking up to heaven, he groaned and said to him: “Ephphatha” [Note: The Greek has *Ephphatha* (Ἐφφαθά). Therefore the translator or copyist ought to have written *Ephphatha*. Nevertheless, the Vulgate reading *Ephpheta* is confirmed by the Cantabrigian manuscript.], which means, “Be opened.”

And immediately his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosened, and he spoke correctly. And he ordered them not to tell anyone. But the more he ordered them, the more abundantly they proclaimed it, and they were astonished all the more, saying: “He has done all things well; he makes the deaf hear and the mute speak.”

**CHAPTER LXXXVII. Jesus spoke to the Samaritan woman beside Jacob’s well.**
JOHN 4:4–42. Now he* had to pass through Samaria. So he came to a city of Samaria called Sychar [Note: [Col. 0295D] According to the literal text, Συχάρ, “Sychar.”], near the estate which Jacob gave to Joseph his son (Gen. 48:22). Jacob’s spring was there. Jesus therefore, weary from the journey, sat thus by the spring. It was about the sixth hour. A woman of Samaria came to draw water.
