Jesus said to her: “Give me a drink.” For his disciples had gone into the city to buy food. Therefore that Samaritan woman said to him: “How is it that you, being a Jew, ask a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.

Jesus answered and said to her: “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ perhaps you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.” The woman said to him: “Sir, you have nothing with which to draw, and the well is deep; whence, then, do you have living water? Surely you are not greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and himself drank from it, as did his sons and his livestock?” Jesus answered and said to her: “Everyone who drinks from this water will thirst again; but whoever drinks from the water that I shall give him will never thirst. Rather, the water that I shall give him will become in him a spring of water leaping up into eternal life.” The woman said to him: “Sir, give me this water, so that I may not thirst or come here to draw water.” Jesus said to her: [Col. 0295C] “Go, call your husband, and come here.” The woman answered and said: “I have no husband.” Jesus said to her: “You have spoken well in saying, ‘I have no husband’; for you have had five husbands, and the one whom you now have is not your husband. In this you have spoken truly.”

The woman said to him: “Sir, I see that you are a prophet. Our fathers worshipped on this mountain, and you say that Jerusalem is the place where one ought to worship” (Deut. 12:15). Jesus said to her: “Woman, believe me: the hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem. You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, because salvation is from the Jews. But the hour is coming—and now is—when true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth. For indeed the Father seeks such people to worship him. God is spirit, and those who [Col. 0295D] worship him must worship in spirit and truth.” The woman said to him: “I know that the Messiah is coming, who is called Christ. When he comes, he will announce everything to us.” Jesus said to her: “I am he who speaks with you.”

Immediately his disciples came, and they marvelled that he was speaking with a woman. Yet no one said, “What do you seek?” or, “Why are you speaking with her?” The woman therefore left her water jar, went away into the city, and said to the people: “Come and see a man who told me everything that I have done. Surely he is not [Col. 0296A] the Christ?” They went out [Note: [Col. 0296D] The Vulgate, with the Greek, has: “Therefore the Jews said.” Mill observed that the particle οὖν, “therefore,” is absent in the Cantabrigian and Arabic [versions].] from the city and came to him.

Meanwhile the disciples were asking him, saying: “Rabbi, eat.” But he said to them: “I have food to eat which you do not know.” Therefore the disciples said to one another: “Surely someone has not brought him something to eat?” Jesus said to them: “My food is to do the will of him who sent me, to complete his work. Do you not say that there are still four months and then the harvest comes? Behold, I say to you: lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are already white for harvest. And the reaper receives wages and gathers fruit for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together. For in this the saying is true: one sows and another reaps. I sent you to reap what you did not labour for; [Col. 0296B] others laboured, and you entered into their labours.”

Now many Samaritans from that city believed in him because of the woman’s testimony: “He told me everything that I did.” When the Samaritans came to him, they asked him to remain with them, and he remained there two days. And many more believed because of his word. They said to the woman: “We now believe not because of your account, for we ourselves have heard and know that this man is truly the Saviour of the world.”

## CHAPTER LXXXVIII. Jesus healed at Jerusalem an infirm man who had lain in his infirmity for thirty-eight years; and on that occasion disputed much with the Jews.

JOHN 5:1–47. After this there was a feast day of the Jews, [Col. 0296C] and Jesus went up to Jerusalem. Now at Jerusalem there is a sheep-gate pool, called in Hebrew Bethsaida, having five porticoes. In these lay a great multitude of sick people—blind, lame, and withered—waiting for the movement of the water. For an angel of the Lord descended into the pool at a certain time, and the water was stirred. Whoever first went down after the stirring of the water [Note: [Col. 0295D] After “went down,” it omits “into the pool,” which the Vulgate and Armenian have. Thus the Greek: ἐμβὰς μετὰ τὴν ταραχήν, “having entered after the stirring.”] was made well, whatever illness held him.

There was a certain man there who had been in his infirmity thirty-eight years. When Jesus saw him lying there and knew that he had already been so for a long time, he said to him: “Do you wish to become well?” The sick man answered him: “Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water has been stirred; for while I am coming, [Col. 0296D] another goes down before me.” Jesus said to him: “Rise, take up your pallet [Note: [Col. 0295D] Thus also in what follows the common Greek text, κράββατον. The Alexandrian and Cantabrigian [texts have] κράβαττον.] and walk.” Immediately the man was made well; he took up his pallet and walked. Now that day was the Sabbath.

The Jews said [Note: [Col. 0296D] The Vulgate, with the Greek, has: “Therefore the Jews said.” Mill observed that the particle οὖν, “therefore,” is absent in the Cantabrigian and Arabic [versions].] to the man who had been healed: “It is the Sabbath; you are not permitted to carry your pallet.” He answered them: “The one who made me well said to me, ‘Take up your pallet and walk.’” They therefore asked him: “Who is the man who said to you, ‘Rise, take up [Note: [Col. 0296D] The former word is lacking either in the text or in the versions.] your pallet and walk’?” But the man who had been made well [Col. 0297A] did not know who he was, for Jesus had withdrawn himself* from the crowd gathered in that place.

Afterward Jesus found him in the temple and said to him: “Behold, you have become well; sin no more, lest something worse happen to you.” The man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well. Therefore the Jews persecuted Jesus because he did these things on the Sabbath. But Jesus answered them: “My Father works until now, and I work.” Therefore the Jews sought all the more to kill him, because he not only broke the Sabbath but also called God his own Father, making himself equal to God.

Jesus therefore answered and said to them: “Amen,* I say to you: the Son can do nothing from himself, except what he sees the Father doing. For whatever that one does, [Col. 0297B] these things the Son likewise does. For the Father loves the Son and shows him everything that he himself does; and he will show him greater works, so that you may marvel. For as the Father raises the dead and gives life, so also the Son gives life to whom he wishes. For neither does the Father judge anyone, but he has given all judgment to the Son, so that all may honour the Son as they honour the Father. Whoever does not honour the Son does not honour the Father who sent him.

“Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life. He does not come into judgment, but will pass [Note: [Col. 0297D] The Vulgate has transiit, “has passed.” The Greek agrees: μεταβέβηκε, “has passed.” Ammonius, however, read μεταβήσεται, “will pass,” with Nonnus. So too some manuscripts cited by Mill.] from death into life. Amen, amen, I say to you: the hour is coming, and now is, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live. For as the Father has life in himself, so he also gave the Son to have life [Col. 0297C] in himself. And he gave him authority to execute judgment, because he is the Son of Man. Do not marvel at this, because the hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear his voice [Note: [Col. 0297D] The present text agrees: φωνῆς αὐτοῦ, “his voice.” The Vulgate has “the voice of the Son of God,” a reading certainly confirmed by other Greek manuscripts. See Mill.] and will come forth: those who have done good to the resurrection of life, but those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.

“I can do nothing from myself. As I hear, I judge; and my judgment is just, because I do not seek my own will but the will of him who sent me [Note: [Col. 0298D] These words, “because I do not seek … him who sent me,” have dropped out of the printed editions.]. If I bear witness concerning myself, my witness is not true. There is another who bears witness concerning me, and I know that the witness which he bears concerning me is true. You sent to John, and he bore witness to the truth. But I do not receive testimony from a human being; rather, I say these things so that you may be saved.

[Col. 0297D] “He was a burning and shining lamp, and you wished to rejoice for an hour in his light. But I have testimony greater than John’s. For the works which the Father gave me to complete—the very works which I do—bear witness concerning me that the Father sent me. And the Father who sent me has himself borne witness concerning me. Yet you have neither heard his voice [Note: [Col. 0298D] The Vulgate has “have ever heard.” The Greek: ἀκηκόατε πώποτε, “have ever heard.” This final word is absent from the Cantabrigian manuscript and seems to have been absent from Ammonius’s copy.] (Matt. 3:17; 17:5) nor seen his form (Deut. 4:12). And his word does not remain in you, because you do not believe him whom he sent. [Col. 0298A] Search the Scriptures, because you think that in them you have eternal life; and they are the ones which bear witness concerning me. Yet you are unwilling to come to me that you may have life.

“I do not receive glory from human beings. But I have known you: you do not have love in yourselves. I came in my Father’s name, and you did not receive me. If another comes in his own name, you will receive him. How can you believe, receiving glory from one another, while you do not seek the glory which is from God alone? Do not think that I shall accuse you before the Father; there is one who accuses you—Moses, in whom you hope. For if you believed Moses, perhaps you would also believe me, for he wrote concerning me (Gen. 3:15; 12:3; 18:18; 22:18; 26:4; 28:14; 49:10; Deut. 18:15). But if you do not believe his [Col. 0298B] writings, how will you believe my words?”

## CHAPTER LXXXIX. Jesus fed four thousand people with seven loaves and a few fish, and instructed the apostles to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees.

MATTHEW 15:32–39; MARK 8:1–10. Having left them, in those days, when there was again a great crowd, he summoned his disciples and said: “I have compassion on the crowd, because, behold, they have already remained with me three days and have nothing to eat; and I do not wish to dismiss them fasting, lest they fail on the way.” His disciples said to him: “Where then shall we find in the wilderness enough bread to satisfy so great a crowd?” Jesus said to them: “How many loaves do you have?” They said: “Seven, and a few little fish.” He instructed the crowd to recline on the ground. And taking [Col. 0298C] the seven loaves and the fish, giving thanks, he broke them and gave them to his disciples, and the disciples gave them to the people. They all ate and were satisfied. What remained of the fragments they took up: seven full baskets. Those who had eaten were four thousand men, apart from children and women. And he dismissed them. Immediately he entered the boat with his disciples and came into the district of Dalmanutha.

—MATTHEW 16:5–12; MARK 8:14–21. When his disciples had crossed the strait, they forgot to take loaves, and they had no more than one loaf with them in the boat. He instructed them, saying: “Look, and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, and of the leaven of Herod.” They reasoned among themselves, saying: “Because we have no loaves.” But Jesus, knowing this, said: “Why do you reason [Col. 0298D] among yourselves, you of little faith, because you have no bread? Do you not yet understand or remember? Do you still have your heart blinded? Having eyes, do you not see, and having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember when I broke the five loaves for the five thousand? How many baskets full of fragments did you take up?” They said to him: “Twelve.” “And when [I broke] the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many baskets of fragments did you take up?” They said to him: “Seven.” “Why do you not understand that [Col. 0299A] I did not speak to you of bread: ‘Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees’?” Then they understood that he had not said that they should beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

## CHAPTER XC. Jesus asks the apostles, “Who do people say that I am?”; what follows; and he says to Peter, “You are a stumbling block to me.”

MATTHEW 16:13–27. Jesus came into the district of Caesarea Philippi and questioned his disciples, saying: “Who do people say the Son of Man is?” They said: “Some say John the Baptist, others Elijah, others Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.” Jesus said to them: “But who do you say that I am?” Simon Peter answered: “You are the Christ, the Son [Col. 0299B] of the living God.” Jesus answered and said to him: “Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but my Father who is in heaven. And I say to you: you are Peter, and upon this rock I shall build my Church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. I shall give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you bind on earth shall be bound also in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed also in heaven.” Then he instructed his disciples to tell no one that he was the Christ.

From then on Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem, suffer many things from the elders, scribes, and chief priests, be killed, and rise on the third day. Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him, saying: [Col. 0299C] “May it be far from you, Lord; this shall not happen to you.” But he turned and said to Peter: “Get behind me, Satan; you are a stumbling block to me, because you do not relish the things of God, but those of human beings.” Then, summoning the crowd with his disciples, he said to them: “If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me. For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for my sake will find it. For what does it profit a person if he gains the whole world but suffers loss of his own life? Or what will a person give in exchange for his life? For the Son of Man is about to come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will repay each person according to his work.”

## CHAPTER XCI. [Col. 0299D] Jesus says: “There are some standing here who shall not taste death.” And on the mountain he is transfigured.

MATTHEW 16:28; 17:1–13; MARK 9:1–15; LUKE 9:28–36. “Amen, I say to you: there are some standing here who shall not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.” Six days later Jesus took Peter, James, and John his brother, and led them apart up a high mountain to pray; and he was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and his garments became white as snow, shining exceedingly white, such as no fuller on earth [Col. 0300A] can make white. And behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, speaking with him in majesty. They spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem. Peter answered and said to Jesus: “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you wish, let us make three tents here: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them. And behold, a voice from heaven said: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him.” When the disciples heard this, they fell on their faces and were greatly afraid. Jesus came up, touched them, and said to them: “Rise, and do not be afraid.” Raising their eyes, they saw no one except Jesus alone.

As they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus instructed them: “Tell no one of the vision until [Col. 0300B] the Son of Man rises from the dead.” The disciples asked him: “Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?” He answered and said*: “Elijah indeed is coming, and he will restore all things” (Mal. 4:5). “But I say to you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did with him whatever they wished. So also the Son of Man is about to suffer at their hands.” Then the disciples understood that he had spoken to them about John the Baptist. When he came to the crowd, he saw scribes disputing with them. Immediately all the people, seeing Jesus, were astonished and alarmed; and they ran up and greeted him. He asked them: “What are you disputing among yourselves?”

## CHAPTER XCII. The Pharisees say to Jesus: “Leave here, because Herod [Col. 0300C] wishes to kill you”; and he healed a lunatic.

LUKE 13:31–33. On that day certain Pharisees came to him and said: “Go out and leave here, because Herod wishes to kill you.” He said to them: “Go and tell that fox: ‘Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am brought to completion. Nevertheless, I must travel today, tomorrow, and the following day, for it is not possible for a prophet to perish outside Jerusalem.’”

—MATTHEW 17:14–20; MARK 9:16–28; LUKE 9:38–44. On the following day a man came to him, fell on his knees, and cried out, saying: “Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is my only son, and he is lunatic. When the spirit seizes him, it throws him down; he foams, gnashes his teeth, and withers away, and suffers grievously. For he often falls into fire and frequently into water, [Col. 0300D] suddenly cries out, convulses him, and scarcely leaves him after tearing him. I asked your disciples to cast it out, and they could not heal him.”

Jesus answered and said: “O faithless and perverse generation, how long* shall I be with you? Bring him here to me.” As he came near and saw him, immediately the spirit convulsed him; thrown to the ground, he rolled about foaming. Jesus asked his father: “How long is it since this happened to him?” He said: “From childhood; and it has often thrown him both into fire and into water in order to destroy him. But if you can do anything, help us, having compassion on us.” Jesus said to him: “If you can believe, all things are possible for the one who believes” [Note: [Col. 0299] The Vulgate inserts sunt, “are.” Greek: πάντα δυνατὰ τῷ πιστεύοντι, “all things [are] possible for the one who believes.”]. Immediately [Col. 0301A] the child’s father cried out with tears, saying: “I believe, Lord; help my unbelief.”

When Jesus saw a crowd running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it: “Deaf and mute spirit, I command you: come out of him, and enter him no more.” Crying out and violently tearing him, it came out of him. He became like a dead person, so that many said, “He is dead.” But Jesus took his hand, raised him, and he stood up. The boy was healed from that hour, and he gave him back to his father. All were astonished at the greatness of God. Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and said: “Why were we unable to cast it out?” He said to them: “Because of your unbelief. For amen, I say to you, if you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you will say [Col. 0301B] to this mountain, ‘Move from here,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you. But this kind of demon is not cast out except by prayer and fasting.”

## CHAPTER XCIII. Jesus discloses to his disciples his passion, and at Capernaum paid the didrachma collectors for himself and Peter.

MATTHEW 17:21–26; MARK 9:30, 31; LUKE 9:44, 45. While they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said to them: “The Son of Man is to be delivered into the hands of people; they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise.” But they did not understand the saying and were afraid to ask him; and they were deeply grieved. When they came to Capernaum, those who received the didrachma came to Peter and said: “Does your teacher not pay [Col. 0301C] the didrachma?” He said: “Yes.” When he had entered the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying: “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth receive tribute or tax—from their sons or from strangers?” He said: “From strangers.” Jesus said to him: “Then the sons are free. But lest we cause them to stumble, go to the sea, cast in a hook, and take the first fish that comes up; when you open its mouth, you will find a stater. Take it and give it to them for me and you.”

## CHAPTER XCIV. Jesus, asked by his disciples who will be greatest in the kingdom of heaven, instructs them by these examples to humble themselves like a little child.

MATTHEW 18:1–6; MARK 9:32–36; LUKE 9:46–48. At that hour, while he was at home, he asked them: [Col. 0301D] “What were you discussing on the way?” But they were silent, for on the way they had disputed among themselves which of them was greater. The disciples came to Jesus, saying: “Who do you think is greater in the kingdom of heaven?” Jesus called a little child, placed him in their midst, and said: “Amen, I say to you: unless you turn and become like little children, you shall not enter the kingdom of heaven. Whoever therefore humbles himself like this little child is greater in the kingdom of heaven. If anyone wishes to be greater [Note: [Col. 0301D] The Vulgate has primus, “first,” in Mark 9:34, whence this is taken. Nor does the Greek differ.], he shall be last of all and servant of all. Whoever receives one such little child in [Col. 0302A] my name receives me. But whoever causes one of these little ones* who believe in me to stumble, it is expedient for him that a millstone turned by an ass be hung around his neck and that he be drowned in the depth of the sea.”

## CHAPTER XCV. Those who perform signs in Jesus’ name should not be prohibited.

MARK 9:37–39; LUKE 9:49–50. John answered and said: “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we prohibited him because he does not follow us.”

But Jesus said: “Do not prohibit him, for there is no one who performs a mighty work in my name and can soon speak evil of me. For whoever is not against you is for you.”

—MATTHEW 18:7–9; MARK 9:41–48; LUKE 17:1–2. [Col. 0302B] “Woe to the world because of stumbling blocks. For it is necessary that stumbling blocks come; nevertheless, woe to the person through whom the stumbling block comes.

“But if your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you. It is good for you to enter life maimed or lame rather than, having two hands or two feet, to be thrown into eternal fire.

“And if your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it away from you. It is good for you to enter life one-eyed rather than, having two eyes, to be thrown into the Gehenna of fire, where their worm does not die and the fire is not extinguished.

“For every person will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt” [Note: [Col. 0301D] This comma, Mark 9:48, is expressed thus in Greek: Πᾶς γὰρ πυρὶ ἁλισθήσεται, καὶ πᾶσα θυσία ἁλὶ ἁλισθήσεται, “For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.” The Vulgate has: “For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.”].

## CHAPTER XCVI. We must not despise one of the little ones; the parable of the lost sheep and the drachma is added.

[Col. 0302C] MATTHEW 18:10–14; LUKE 15:3–10. “See that you do not despise one of these little ones. For I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father who is in heaven. For the Son of Man came to save what had perished.

“And he told them this parable: ‘What do you think? If someone has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, would he not leave the ninety-nine on the mountains or in the wilderness and go in search of the one that went astray? And if it happens that he finds it, he places it on his shoulders, rejoicing. And when he comes home, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them: “Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that had perished.”

“‘Amen, I say to you, he will rejoice over it more than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray and do not need repentance. So it is not the will before your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.

“‘Or what woman, having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp, sweep the house, and search carefully until she finds it? And when she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying: “Rejoice with me, because I have found the drachma that I had lost.”

“‘So I tell you, there will be joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents more than over ninety-nine righteous people who have no need of repentance.’”

## CHAPTER XCVII. Concerning the son who squandered his father’s substance.

LUKE 15:11–32. He said: “A certain man had two sons. And the younger* said to his father: ‘Father, give me the share of the property that falls to me.’ And he divided the property between them.

“Not many days later, after gathering everything together, the younger son departed for a distant region; and there he squandered his property by living extravagantly. When he had consumed everything, a severe famine arose in that region, and he began to be in need.

“And he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that region. He sent him into his estate to feed pigs. And he longed to fill his stomach with the pods that the pigs were eating, but no one gave him any.

“Then, coming to himself, he said: [Col. 0303B] ‘How many hired servants in my father’s house have an abundance of bread, while I am perishing here from hunger! I will rise and go to my father and say to him: “Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son; make me like one of your hired servants.”’

“And rising, he came to his father. While he was still far away, his father saw him and was moved with compassion. He ran and fell upon his neck and kissed him. And the son said to him: ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you; I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’

“But the father said to his servants: ‘Quickly, bring out the first robe and clothe him, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet. Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let us eat and celebrate, because this son of mine was dead and has come to life again; he was lost and has been found.’ And they began to celebrate.

“Now his older son was in the field. When he came and drew near the house, he heard music and dancing. He called one of the servants and asked what this meant. He said to him: ‘Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe.’

“But he became angry and was unwilling to enter. Therefore his father went out and began to plead with him. He answered and said to his father: ‘Behold, for so many years I have served you, and I have never disobeyed your command; yet you never gave me a young goat so that I might celebrate with my friends. But when this son of yours came, who has devoured his property with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him.’

“But he said to him: ‘Son, you are always with me, and everything I have is yours. But it was necessary to celebrate and rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and has come to life again; he was lost and has been found.’”

## CHAPTER XCVIII. Concerning forgiving one’s brothers from the heart.

MATTHEW 18:15–22; LUKE 17:3–4. “Pay attention to yourselves. If your brother sins against you, go and rebuke him between you and him alone. If he listens to you and repents, forgive him, and you will have gained your brother.

“But if he does not listen to you, take with you one or two more, so that every word may stand by the mouth of two or three (Deut. 19:13). But if he does not listen to them, tell it to the church. And if he does not listen even to the church, let him be to you as a gentile and a tax collector.

“Amen, I say to you: whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.

“Again I say to you: if two of you agree on earth about any matter that they ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven. For where two or three are gathered in my name, there I am in the midst of them.”

Then Peter approached him and said: “Lord, how often will my brother sin against me and I forgive him? Up to seven times?”

Jesus said to him: “I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven.”

## CHAPTER XCIX. The parable of the king who settled accounts with his servants.

MATTHEW 18:23–35. “Therefore the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wished to settle accounts with his servants.

“When he began to settle the accounts, one was brought to him who owed ten thousand talents. Since he had nothing with which to repay, the master ordered him to be sold, together with his wife, his children, and everything he had, and payment to be made.

“Then that servant fell down and pleaded with him, saying: ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything.’

“Moved with compassion, the master of that servant released him and forgave him the debt.

“But when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii. He seized and choked him, saying: ‘Pay what you owe.’

“Then his fellow servant fell down and begged him, saying: ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything.’

“But he was unwilling. Instead, he went away and had him thrown into prison until he repaid the debt.

“When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly saddened. They came and reported to their master everything that had taken place.

“Then his master summoned him and said to him: ‘Wicked servant, I forgave you all that debt because you begged me. Should you not therefore also have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had mercy on you?’

“And his master, becoming angry, handed him over to the torturers until he repaid the entire debt.

“So also my heavenly Father will do to you, if each of you does not forgive his brother from your hearts.”

## CHAPTER C. Jesus is asked by the Pharisees whether it is lawful to divorce one’s wife for any reason.

MATTHEW 19:1–12; MARK 10:1–12. And it happened that when Jesus had finished these sayings, he departed from Galilee and came into the territory of Judea beyond the Jordan. And great crowds followed him, and he healed them there.

And Pharisees approached him, testing him and saying: “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?”

He answered and said to them: “Have you not read that the one who made them from the beginning* made them male and female (Gen. 1:27)? And he said: ‘For this reason a man will leave father and mother and cling to his wife, and the two will be one flesh’ (Gen. 2:24). Therefore they are no longer two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, let no human being separate.”

They said to him: “Why, then, did Moses command that a document of divorce be given (Deut. 24:1) and that she be dismissed?”

He said to them: “Because of the hardness of your hearts Moses permitted you to divorce your wives; but from the beginning it was not so. I say to you: whoever divorces his wife, except on account of fornication, and marries another commits adultery. And whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.”

His disciples said to him: “If such is the situation of a man with his wife, it is not advantageous to marry.”

He said [Note: [Col. 0305D] The Greek and the Vulgate add illis, “to them.” I would rather suppose that this word dropped out of Ammonius’s copy through scribal error.]: “Not everyone accepts this saying, but only those to whom it has been given. For there are eunuchs who were born so from their mother’s womb. And there are eunuchs who were made so by human beings. And there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let the one who is able to accept it accept it.”

## CHAPTER CI. Jesus laid his hands on children. And the Pharisees murmur against Jesus because he receives sinners.

MATTHEW 14:13–15; MARK 10:13–16. Then children were brought to him so that he might lay his hands on them and pray. But the disciples rebuked them.

Jesus, however, said to them: “Let the children come, and do not prevent them from coming to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.”

And when he had laid his hands on them, he departed from there.

—LUKE 15:1–2. Now many tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to him to hear him. And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying: “This man receives sinners and eats with them.”

—JOHN 7:1. After these things Jesus was walking about in Galilee, for he did not wish to walk about in Judea, because the Jews were seeking to kill him.

## CHAPTER CII. Jesus instructs those who reported to him about the Galileans whom Pilate killed, adding the parable of the fig tree in the vineyard.

[Col. 0305C] Luke 13:1–9. At that time some people were present, telling him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices. And he answered and said to them: “Do you think that these Galileans were sinners above all other Galileans, because they suffered such things? No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish. Or those eighteen upon whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think that they also were debtors beyond all the people dwelling in Jerusalem? No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish.”

And he told this parable: “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it but found none. Then he said to the vinedresser: ‘Behold, it is three years since I have come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and I find none. Cut it down, therefore; why should it even occupy the ground?’ But he, answering, said to him: ‘Lord, leave it this year also, until I dig around it and apply manure; and if indeed it bears fruit—otherwise, you shall cut it down in the future.’”

## CHAPTER CIII. [Col. 0306A] Jesus healed in the synagogue a woman who was withered and bent over.

Luke 13:10–17. Now he was teaching in one of their synagogues on the Sabbaths. And behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years; she was bent over and could not look upward at all. When Jesus saw her, he called her to himself and said to her: “Woman, you are released from your infirmity.” And he laid his hands upon her; and immediately she was made straight and glorified God.

But the ruler of the synagogue, indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, answered and said: “There are six days on which one ought to work; on those days come and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day.”

But the Lord answered him and said:

[Note: [Col. 0305D] The present text of Luke 13:15 is somewhat different: “Then the Lord answered him” (Ἀπεκρίθη οὖν αὐτῷ ὁ Κύριος). Apart from the word αὐτῷ (“to him”), however, several other Greek manuscripts cited by Mill uphold the Ammonian reading.]

“Hypocrites! Does not each one of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the manger and lead it away to drink? And this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has bound—behold, for eighteen years—ought she not to be released from this bond on the Sabbath day?”

And as he said these things, all his adversaries were put to shame. And all the people rejoiced in all the things that were being done by him.*

## CHAPTER CIV. Jesus went up to Jerusalem on the feast of Booths.

John 7:2–31. Now the Jewish feast, the feast of Booths, was near. Therefore his brothers said to him: “Leave here and go into Judea, so that your disciples also may see the works that you do. For no one does anything in secret while seeking himself to be known publicly. If you do these things, manifest yourself to the world.” For even his brothers did not believe in him.

Therefore Jesus said to them:

[Col. 0306C] “My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready. The world cannot hate you, but it hates me, because I testify concerning it that its works are evil. Go up to this feast yourselves; I am not going up to this feast,* because my time has not yet been fulfilled.”

[Note: [Col. 0305D] On this passage, John 7:8, Mill discusses several matters learnedly; there he also cites from the Velesian manuscripts a reading twice corresponding to the Ammonian one: “For I will not go up” (ἐγὼ γὰρ οὐκ ἀναβήσομαι). And rightly so. For, as the distinguished Lamy says in his *Harmony*, the Lord did not in fact go up for the feast itself, since he did not come to Jerusalem until part of the celebration had already passed.]

When he had said these things, he remained in Galilee. But when his brothers had gone up, then he too went up to the feast, not openly but as if in secret. The Jews, therefore, were looking for him at the feast and saying: “Where is that man?” And there was much murmuring about him among the crowd. For some were saying: “He is good.” Others were saying: “No, but he deceives the crowds.” Yet no one spoke openly about him, because of fear of the Jews.

Now, when the feast was already halfway over, Jesus went up into the temple [Col. 0306D] and was teaching. And the Jews were amazed, saying: “How does this man know letters, since he has not studied?”

Jesus answered them and said: “My teaching is not mine, but his who sent me. If anyone wishes to do his will, he will know concerning the teaching* whether it is from God, or whether I speak from myself.”

[Note: [Col. 0306D] The final word is absent both from the Greek and from the Vulgate, and seems to have been repeated from what immediately precedes.]

“He who speaks from himself seeks his own glory. But he who seeks the glory of him who sent him is truthful, and there is no injustice in him. Did not Moses give you the law (Exodus 24:3), and yet none of you observes the law? Why do you seek to kill me?”

The crowd answered and said: “You have a demon. Who is seeking to kill you?”

Jesus answered and said to them: “I did one work, and you are all amazed. For this reason Moses gave you circumcision (Leviticus 12:3)—not because it is from Moses, but from the patriarchs—and you circumcise a man on the Sabbath. If a man receives circumcision on the Sabbath, so that the law of Moses may not be broken, why are you angry with me because I made a whole man well on the Sabbath?*

[Note: [Col. 0307D] “With me” was lacking in the printed editions. I have no doubt that Ammonius both read it and translated it.]

“Do not judge according to appearance, but judge a just judgment.”

Therefore some of the people of Jerusalem were saying: “Is this not the man whom they seek to kill? And behold, he speaks openly, and they say nothing to him. Can it be that the rulers have truly recognized that this is the Christ? But we know where this man is from; when the Christ comes, no one knows where he is from.”

Therefore Jesus cried out while teaching in the temple and said: “You both know me and know where I am from. And I have not come from myself, but he who sent me is true, whom you do not know. I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me.”

—John 8:55. “And if I should say that I do not know him, I would be like you, a liar.”

Therefore they sought to seize him, and no one laid hands on him, because his hour had not yet come. But many from the crowd believed in him and said: “When the Christ comes, will he perform more signs than this man has performed?”

## CHAPTER CV. [Col. 0307C] Concerning the rich man whose field produced an abundant harvest.

Luke 12:13–21. Then someone from the crowd said to him: “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.” But he said to him: “Man, who appointed me judge or divider over you?”

And he said to them: “See and beware of all greed, because a person’s life does not consist in the abundance of what he possesses.”

And he told them a parable, saying: “The field of a certain rich man produced an abundant harvest. And he was reasoning within himself, saying: ‘What shall I do? For I have no place where I may gather my crops.’ And he said: ‘I will do this: I will pull down my barns and build larger ones; and there I will gather all that has grown for me and my goods. And I will say to my soul: “Soul, you have many good things stored up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, feast.”’”

But God said to him: “Fool, this night they demand your soul* from you. And the things you have prepared—whose will they be?”

[Note: [Col. 0308D] Greek: ἀπαιτοῦσιν (“they demand”); Vulgate: repetent (“they will demand”).]

“So is the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.”

## CHAPTER CVI. Concerning the man who, although possessing many estates, went away sorrowful when he heard the word: “Go, sell everything you have.”

Matthew 19:16–30; Mark 10:17–31; Luke 18:18–30. And when he had gone out onto the road, a certain man ran up, knelt before him, and asked him: “Good Teacher, what good thing shall I do so that I may have eternal life?”

He said to him: “Why do you ask me about the good? [Col. 0308A] No one is good except God alone. But if you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments.”

He said to him: “Which ones?”

And Jesus said: “You shall not kill; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness. Honor your father and mother; and, You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

The young man said to him: “I have kept all these things from my youth. What do I still lack?”

Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him: “One thing you lack: if you wish to be perfect, go, sell what you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”

When the young man heard the word, he went away sorrowful, for he was very rich and possessed many estates.

And Jesus, looking around, said to his disciples: “How difficult it will be for those who have money to enter the kingdom of God! Amen, [Col. 0308B] I tell you: a rich man will enter the kingdom of heaven with difficulty. And again I tell you: it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven.”

When the disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished, saying: “Who, then, can be saved?”

But Jesus looked at them and said: “With human beings this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”

Then Peter answered and said to him: “Behold, we have left everything and followed you. What, then, will there be for us?”

But Jesus said to them: “Amen, I tell you: you who have followed me, in the regeneration, when the Son of Man sits on the throne of his majesty, you also will sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. Amen, I tell you: everyone who has left a house, or parents, or brothers [Col. 0308C] or sisters, or father or mother, or wife or children, or lands, for the sake of the kingdom of heaven, and my name, and the Gospel, will receive a hundredfold: now, in this time, houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the age to come, he will possess eternal life. But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”

—Luke 16:14–15. Now the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all these things, and they ridiculed him. And he said to them: “You are those who justify yourselves before human beings, but God knows your hearts; for what is exalted among human beings is an abomination before God.”

## CHAPTER CVII. [Col. 0308D] Concerning the rich man and Lazarus.

Luke 16:19–31. Again he said: “There was a certain rich man, and he dressed in purple and fine linen and feasted splendidly every day. And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, who lay at his gate, full of sores, desiring to be filled with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table; and no one gave them to him. But even the dogs came and licked his sores.

“Now it happened that the beggar died and was carried by angels into Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried in hell. And when he lifted up his eyes while he was in torments, he saw Abraham from afar, and Lazarus in his bosom. And he himself cried out and said: ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am suffering in this flame.’

“And Abraham said to him: ‘Son, remember that you received good things during your life, and Lazarus likewise evil things. But now he is comforted here, while you are suffering. And in all these matters a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that those who wish to cross from here to you cannot, nor can they cross from there to us.’

“And he said: ‘Then I ask you, father, to send him to my father’s house. For I have five brothers, so that he may testify to them, lest they too come to this place of torment.’

“And Abraham said to him: ‘They have Moses and the prophets; let them listen to them.’

“But he said: ‘No, father Abraham; but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’

“And he said to him: ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not believe even if someone rises from the dead.’”

## CHAPTER CVIII. Concerning the dishonest steward.

Luke 16:1–12. And he said to his disciples: “There was a certain rich man who had a steward, and this man was accused before him of wasting his property. And he called him and said to him: ‘What is this I hear about you? Give an account of your stewardship, for you can no longer be steward.’

“But the steward said within himself: ‘What shall I do, since my master is taking the stewardship away from me? I cannot dig; I am ashamed to beg. I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.’

“Therefore, summoning each of his master’s debtors, he said to the first: ‘How much do you owe my master?’ And he said: ‘A hundred jars of oil.’ He said to him: ‘Take your bond, sit down, and quickly write fifty.’

“Then he said to another: ‘And you, how much do you owe?’ He said: ‘A hundred measures of wheat.’ He said to him: ‘Take your written account and write eighty.’

“And the master praised the dishonest steward, because he had acted shrewdly; for the children of this age are shrewder in their generation than the children of light. And I tell you: make friends for yourselves from the mammon of iniquity, so that when you fail, they may receive you into the eternal dwellings.

“He who is faithful in the least is faithful also in much; and he who is unjust in a little is unjust also in much. Therefore, if you have not been faithful with the unrighteous mammon, who will entrust to you what is true? And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is true?”

—Luke 12:47–50. “But that servant who knew his master’s will and did not prepare himself and did not act according to his will will be beaten with many blows; but the one who did not know and did things deserving of blows will be beaten with few. Everyone to whom much has been given, much will be required of him; and from the one to whom much has been entrusted, they will demand more from him. Do you not know that I have come to cast fire upon the earth? And what do I desire except that it be kindled? But I have a baptism with which I must be baptized, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!”

## CHAPTER CIX. Concerning the master of a household who went out at dawn to hire workers for his vineyard.

Matthew 20:1–16. “The kingdom of heaven is like a master of a household [Col. 0310A] who went out at dawn to hire workers for his vineyard. And after reaching an agreement with the workers for a denarius per day, he sent them into his vineyard.

“And going out around the third hour, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace, and he said to them: ‘You also go into the vineyard, and whatever is just I will give you.’ And they went.

“Again he went out around the sixth and ninth hours, and did likewise. But around the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing there, and he said to them: ‘Why do you stand here idle all day?’ They said to him: ‘Because no one has hired us.’ He said to them: ‘You also go into the vineyard.’

“When evening came, the master of the vineyard said to his steward: ‘Call the workers and pay them their wage, beginning with the last and ending with the first.’

“Therefore, when those who had come at the eleventh hour arrived, they received a denarius each. When the first also came, they thought that they would receive more; but they too received a denarius each. And when they had received it, they murmured against the master of the household, saying: ‘These last have worked one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who bore the burden of the day and the heat.’

“But he answered one of them and said: ‘Friend, I am not doing you an injustice. Did you not agree with me for a denarius? Take what is yours and go. But I wish to give this last one the same as to you. Or is it not lawful for me to do what I wish? Or is your eye evil because I am good?’

“Thus the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.”

## CHAPTER CX. Jesus healed a man with dropsy in the house of a Pharisee and instructed [Col. 0310C] those who chose the chief places at banquets.

Luke 14:1–15. And it happened that, when he entered the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on the Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him. And behold, a certain man with dropsy was before him.

And Jesus answered the lawyers and Pharisees, saying: “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”

But they remained silent. Then he took him, healed him, and dismissed him. And answering them, he said: “Which of you, if his donkey or ox falls into a well, will not immediately pull it out on the Sabbath day?”

And they could not answer him concerning these things.

And he also told those who had been invited a parable, observing how they chose the chief places, and said to them: “When you are invited to a wedding, do not recline in the first place, lest someone more honored than you have been invited by him. And the one who invited you and him may come and say to you: ‘Give this man your place’; and then you will begin, with shame, to occupy the last place.

“But when you are invited, go and recline in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he may say to you: ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will have glory before all your fellow guests. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted.”

And he also said to the one who had invited him: “When you make a luncheon or dinner, do not invite your friends, or your brothers, or your relatives, or rich neighbors, lest they also invite you in return and repayment be made to you. But when you hold a banquet, invite the poor, the weak, the lame, and the blind; and [Col. 0311A] you will be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you. For you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”

When one of those reclining at table heard this, he said to him: “Blessed is the one who will eat bread in the kingdom of heaven.”

## CHAPTER CXI. Jesus cleansed ten lepers.

John 6:1–4. After this, the Passover, the Jewish feast, was near.

—Luke 17:11–19. And it happened that, as he was going to Jerusalem, he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee. And as he entered a certain village, ten leprous men met him. They stood at a distance and raised their voices, saying: “Jesus, master, have mercy on us.”

When he saw them, he said: “Go, show yourselves to the priests.” And it happened that, as they went, they were cleansed.

But one of them, when he saw that he had been cleansed, returned, glorifying God with a loud voice. And he fell on his face at his feet, giving thanks; and he was a Samaritan.

Then Jesus answered and said: “Were not ten cleansed? And where are the nine? Was no one found to return and give glory to God except this foreigner?”

And he said to him: “Rise, go; your faith has saved you.”

## CHAPTER CXII. Jesus again foretold his passion to his disciples, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee makes a request for her sons.

Matthew 20:17–28; Mark 10:32–45; Luke 18:31–34; 22:25. Taking the Twelve again, he said [Col. 0311C] to them: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything that has been written through the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be fulfilled. For he will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they will hand him over to the Gentiles; and he will be mocked, scourged, spat upon, and crucified, and on the third day he will rise.”

Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee approached him with her sons, worshiping and asking something of him. He said to her: “What do you want?”

She said to him: “Say that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom.”

But Jesus answered and said to them: “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I am going to drink, or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?”

They said to him: “We can.”

He said to them: “You will indeed drink my cup, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you will be baptized; but to sit at my right hand and left is not mine to give you, but it belongs to those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.”*

[Note: [Col. 0311D] In Mark 10:38 the pronoun is absent both from the Greek and from the Vulgate. Immediately afterward comes “to give you.” Therefore Ammonius read ὑμῖν (“to you”) with the common translator, although this word is now absent from the Greek manuscripts. See Luke of Bruges in his notes on Matthew 20:23.]

When the ten heard this, they were indignant at the two brothers. But Jesus called them to himself and said: “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those who are greater exercise authority over them. It shall not be so among you. Rather, whoever wishes to become great among you shall be your servant; and whoever wishes to be first among you shall be your slave, just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

## CHAPTER CXIII. [Col. 0312A] Jesus answers the one who said to him: “Lord, are there few who will be saved?”

Luke 13:23–30; Matthew 7:13–14, 23. And someone said to him: “Lord, are there few who are being saved?”

But he said to them: “Strive to enter through the narrow gate, because I tell you that many will seek to enter and will not be able. But when the master of the household has entered and shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying: ‘Lord, open to us,’ he will answer and say to you: ‘I do not know where you are from.’

“Then you will begin to say: ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’

“And he will say to you: ‘I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity, into the eternal fire. There will be weeping [Col. 0312B] and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets entering the kingdom of God, while you are cast outside. And they will come from the East and the West, from the North and the South, and will recline in the kingdom of God. And behold, there are last who were first, and there are first who were last.”

## CHAPTER CXIV. Concerning Zacchaeus the tax collector.

Luke 19:1–10. And entering, he was passing through Jericho. And behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich. And he was seeking to see Jesus, who he was, but he could not because of the crowd, for he was short in stature.

And running ahead, he climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, because he was about to pass that way. And when he came to the place, Jesus looked up and saw him and said to him: “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, because today I must remain in your house.”

And he hurried down and welcomed him joyfully. And when everyone saw this, they murmured, saying that he had turned in to a sinful man.

But Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord: “Behold, Lord, I give half of my possessions to the poor; and if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I repay fourfold.”

Jesus said to him: “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham. For the Son of Man came to seek and to save what had perished.”

## CHAPTER CXV. Jesus healed two blind men again.

Matthew 20:29–34; Mark 10:46–52; Luke 18:35–43. [Col. 0312D] And as they were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed him. And behold, two blind men, one of whom was Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, were sitting beside the road. When they heard that Jesus the Nazarene was passing by, they cried out, saying: “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.”

But the crowd rebuked them so that they would be silent. Yet they cried out all the more, saying: “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.”

And Jesus stopped and called them and said: “What do you want me to do for you?”

They said to him: “Lord, that our eyes may be opened.”

And Jesus, having compassion on them, touched their eyes. And immediately they saw, and they followed [Col. 0313A] him, magnifying the Lord.*

[Note: [Col. 0313D] In the Greek of Luke 18:43 we read δοξ. τὸν Θεόν (“glorifying God”). So also in the Vulgate: *magnificantes Deum* (“magnifying God”).]

And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.

## CHAPTER CXVI. Jesus enters Jerusalem seated on a donkey.

Matthew 21:1–9; Mark 11:1–11; Luke 19:29–38. And when he drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, at the Mount of Olives, Jesus then sent two disciples, saying to them: “Go into the village opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt tied with it, on which no human being has ever sat. Untie it and bring it to me. And if anyone says anything to you, say to him: ‘The Lord has need of it’; and immediately he will let them go.”

[Col. 0313B] And the disciples went and did as Jesus had commanded them. As they were untying the colt, its owners said to them: “Why are you untying the colt?”

They said: “Because the Lord needs it.” And they let them go.

And they brought the colt to Jesus; and throwing their garments over the colt, they made him sit upon it.

Now this happened* [Note: [Col. 0313D] Vulgate: “Now all this happened.” *Totum* (“all”) is added in agreement with the Greek and Syriac, although certain good books omit it, according to Luke of Bruges. The word ὅλον (“all”) is likewise absent from the Cantabrigian manuscript and from several versions, as may be seen in Mill.]

so that what had been spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:

“Tell the daughter of Zion: Behold, your king comes to you, meek, sitting upon the colt of a submissive donkey” (Isaiah 62:11; Zechariah 9:9).

—John 12:16. His disciples did not understand these things at first; but when Jesus had been glorified, then they remembered that these things had been written about him, and that they had done these things for him.

As he went along, many spread their garments on the road; others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading them on the road. And when he was already approaching the descent of the Mount of Olives, all the crowds of those descending began joyfully to praise God with a loud voice.

And the crowds that went before and those that followed cried out, saying: “Hosanna to the Son of David; blessed is the one who comes, the king, in the name of the Lord; peace in heaven and glory in the highest; blessed is the kingdom of our father David that comes. Hosanna in the highest.”

—John 12:12–14. On the following day, the great crowd that had come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem, took palm branches and went out to meet him, and cried out: “Hosanna; blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord, the king of Israel.”

—Luke 19:39–44. And some of the Pharisees from the crowds said to him: “Teacher, rebuke your disciples.”

But he said to them: “I tell you, if these were silent, the stones would cry out.”

And when he drew near to Jerusalem and saw the city, he wept over it, saying: “If only you too had known—and indeed on this your day—the things that belong to your peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes. For days will come upon you, and your enemies will surround you with a rampart,* [Col. 0313D] hem you in on every side, throw you and the children* who are in you to the ground, and not leave a stone upon a stone within you, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation.”

## CHAPTER CXVII. [Col. 0314A] He drives out those buying and selling from the temple and answers the Pharisees who exalt themselves.

Matthew 21:10–16; Mark 11:15–18; Luke 19:45–46; John 2:14–21. And when he had entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred, saying: “Who is this?”

But the people were saying: “This is the prophet Jesus from Nazareth of Galilee.”

And Jesus entered the temple of God. And having made something like a whip from cords, he drove out all those selling and buying in the temple, as well as sheep and oxen. He poured out the money-changers’ coins and overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those selling doves.

And he said to them: “Take these things away from here, and do not make my Father’s house a house of commerce. It is written: ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations’ (Isaiah 56:7; Jeremiah 7), but you have made it a den of thieves.”

And he did not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple. His disciples remembered that it was written: “Zeal for your house has consumed me” (Psalm 68:10).

And the blind and the lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them. But when the chief priests and scribes saw the wonders that he performed, and the children crying out in the temple and saying: “Hosanna to the Son of David,” they were indignant and said to him: “Do you hear what these are saying?”

Jesus said to them: “Certainly. Have you never read: ‘From the mouth of infants and nursing children you have perfected praise’ (Psalm 8:3)?”

Therefore the Jews answered and said to him: “What sign do you show us, since you do these things?”

Jesus answered and said to them: “Destroy this temple, [Col. 0314C] and in three days I will raise it up.”

Therefore the Jews said: “This temple was built over forty-six years, and you will raise it up in three days?”

But he was speaking about the temple of his body.

## CHAPTER CXVIII. Jesus preferred a widow to the others because of her two small coins, adding the parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector against those who exalt themselves.

Mark 12:41–44; Luke 21:1–4. Looking up, he saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury. He also saw a certain poor widow putting in two small copper coins, which is a quadrans.

And calling his disciples to himself, he said to them: “Truly I tell you: this poor widow has put in more than all the others. For all these gave from their abundance as gifts to God; [Col. 0314D] but she, from what she lacked, put in all the means of living that she had.”

—Luke 18:9–14. And he told this parable to some who trusted in themselves as righteous and despised others:

“Two men went up into the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector. The Pharisee stood and prayed this within himself: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like the rest of humanity—robbers, unjust, adulterers—or even like this tax collector. I fast twice a week; I give tithes of everything I possess.’

“But the tax collector, standing far off, was unwilling even to lift his eye,* but was striking [Col. 0315A] his breast, saying: ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner.’

“I tell you: this man went down to his house justified rather than the other, because everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted.”

—Matthew 21:17; Mark 11:11. And leaving them, when it was already evening, he went out of the city to Bethany, and remained there.

—Luke 9:11. And when the crowd learned that he had gone outside the city, they followed him. And he received those who needed care and healed them.

## CHAPTER CXIX. Concerning Nicodemus, who came to Jesus by night.

John 3:1–21. Now there was a man from the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews. He came to him by night and said to him: “Rabbi, we know that you have come from God as a teacher; for no one can perform these signs that you perform unless God is with him.”

Jesus answered and said to him: “Amen, amen, I tell you: unless someone has been born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

Nicodemus said to him: “How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb and be born?*”

Jesus answered: “Amen, amen, I tell you: unless someone has been born again of water and Spirit,* he cannot enter the kingdom of God. What has been born of flesh is flesh, and what has been born of Spirit is spirit. Do not be astonished that I said to you: You must be born again.

“The Spirit breathes where it wills; you hear its voice, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone who has been born of the Spirit.”

Nicodemus answered and said to him: “How [Col. 0315C] can these things happen?”

Jesus answered and said to him: “You are a teacher in Israel, and you do not know these things? Amen, amen, I tell you: we speak what we know and testify to what we have seen, yet you do not accept our testimony. If I told you earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?

“And no one has ascended into heaven except the one who descended from heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven. And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness (Numbers 21:9), so must the Son of Man be lifted up, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but have eternal life.

“For God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, so that everyone who believes in him* may not perish but have eternal life. For God did not send his Son into the world to judge the world, but so that the world might be saved through him.

“The one who believes in him is not judged. But the one who does not believe has already been judged, because he has not believed in the name of the only-begotten Son of God.

“And this is the judgment: that light has come into the world, and people loved darkness more than light, for their works were evil. For everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his works may not be exposed. But the one who does the truth comes to the light, so that his works may be revealed, because they have been done in God.”

—John 7:53; 8:1–2. And each returned to his own house. But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives; and at dawn [Col. 0316A] he came again into the temple. And all the people came to him, and he sat and taught them.

## CHAPTER CXX. Concerning the woman caught in adultery by the Jews.

John 8:3–11. The scribes and Pharisees brought a woman caught in adultery, set her in the midst, and said to him: “Teacher, this woman has just been caught in adultery. Now in the law Moses commanded us to stone such women (Leviticus 20:10). What, then, do you say?”

They were saying this to test him, so that they might be able to accuse him. But Jesus, bending down, was writing with his finger on the ground. And when they persisted in questioning him, he straightened up and said to them: “Let the one among you who is without sin cast the first stone at her.”

And again bending down, he was writing on the ground.

When they heard this [Note: [Col. 0315D] Luke of Bruges had advised that this pronoun should not be included. Indeed, it is absent from the Greek and from the Vulgate.], they went out one by one, beginning with the elders. And Jesus was left alone, with the woman standing in the midst.

[Note: [Col. 0315D] We have added *se* (“himself”) with the Vulgate; it is absent from the printed editions. Greek: ἀνακύψας, “having raised himself” or “raising himself”; nor would Victor have translated it otherwise. Immediately afterward: “No one has condemned you, woman?” But the final word is lacking in our Greek and Latin manuscripts.]

Then Jesus, raising himself, said to her: “Woman, where are those who accused you? Has no one condemned you, woman?”

She said: “No one, Lord.”

And Jesus said: “Neither will I condemn you. Go, and from now on do not sin anymore.”

## CHAPTER CXXI. Jesus cursed the fig tree, and it withered.

## Matthew 21:18–22; Mark 11:11, 12, 19–25; Luke 17:5, 6

Now, returning to the city in the morning, he was hungry. And seeing a fig tree beside the road, he came to it; but he found nothing on it except leaves, for it was not yet the season for figs. And he said to it: “May no fruit ever come from you again.” And the fig tree immediately withered. Seeing this, the disciples marveled, saying: “How did it wither immediately?” When evening came, he went out of the city. And as they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from its roots. Peter remembered and said to him: “Rabbi, look: the fig tree that you cursed has withered.”

But Jesus answered and said to them: “Have faith in God. Amen, I say to you: if you have faith and do not doubt in your heart, you will do not only this to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ it will happen. And the apostles said to him: ‘Lord, increase our faith.’ And Jesus said: ‘Whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you will receive it, and it will come to you. And whenever you stand to pray, forgive, if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father who is in heaven may also forgive you your sins.”

## CHAPTER CXXII. Jesus tells his disciples a parable about persistence in prayer, concerning a harsh judge and a widow

### Luke 18:1–8

He also told them a parable, because they ought always to pray and not lose heart, saying:

“There was a certain judge in a certain city who did not fear God and had no regard for man. Now there was a widow in that city, and she kept coming to him, saying: ‘Vindicate me against my adversary.’ For a long time he was unwilling. But afterward he said to himself: ‘Although I do not fear God and have no regard for man, nevertheless, because this widow is troubling me, I will vindicate her, lest, coming at last, she wear me out.’

“And the Lord said: ‘Hear what the unjust judge says. And will God not vindicate his elect, who cry out to him day and night, and will he be patient with them? I tell you that he will swiftly vindicate them. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, do you suppose he will find faith on the earth?’”

## CHAPTER CXXIII. The chief priests ask: “By what authority do you do these things?” He adds the parable of the two sons sent into the vineyard

[Col. 0317B] **Matthew 21:23–32; Mark 11:27–33; Luke 20:1–8**

When he had come into the temple and was teaching and proclaiming the gospel to the people, the chief priests and the elders of the people approached him, saying: “By what authority do you do these things? And who gave you this authority?”

Jesus answered and said to them: “I also will ask you one question; if you answer me, I will also tell you by what authority I do these things. The baptism of John—where was it from, heaven or men?”

But they considered the matter among themselves, saying: “If we say, ‘From men,’ we fear the crowd, for they all regarded John as a prophet.” And they answered Jesus: “We do not know.”

He also said to them: “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things. But what do you think? A certain man had two sons. Approaching the first, he said: ‘Son, go and work today in my vineyard.’ But he answered: ‘I will not.’ Yet afterward, moved by repentance, he went. Approaching the other, he spoke in the same way. But he answered: ‘I am going, lord,’ and did not go. Which of the two did the father’s will?”

They said, * “The last.”

Jesus said to them: “Amen, I say to you: tax collectors and prostitutes will go before you into the kingdom of God. For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him; but the tax collectors and prostitutes believed him. Yet you, seeing this, did not afterward repent so as to believe him.”

## CHAPTER CXXIV. The parable of the householder who leased his vineyard to tenant farmers

[Col. 0317D] **Matthew 21:33–46; Mark 12:1–12; Luke 20:9–19**

“Hear another parable. There was a householder who planted a vineyard, surrounded it with a fence, dug a winepress in it, built a tower, leased it to tenant farmers, and went abroad. When the season of fruits approached, he sent servants to the tenant farmers to collect its fruits. But the tenant farmers seized his servants: they beat one, killed another, and stoned another. Again he sent other servants, more numerous than the first, and they treated them in the same way. Finally, he sent his son to them, saying: ‘Perhaps they will respect my son.’

“But when the tenant farmers saw the son, they said among themselves: ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and we shall have his inheritance.’ So they seized him, threw him outside the vineyard, and killed him. Therefore, when the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?”

They said to him: “He will destroy those evil men miserably and lease his vineyard to other tenant farmers who will give him the fruit in its seasons.”

Jesus said to them: “Have you never read in the Scriptures:

> ‘The stone which the builders rejected,  
> this has become the cornerstone;  
> this was done by the Lord,  
> and it is marvelous in our eyes’  
> (Psalm 117:22–23)?

“Therefore I say to you: the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a nation producing its fruits. Everyone who falls upon this stone will be shattered; but upon whomever it falls, it will crush him.”

When the chief priests and Pharisees heard his parables, they understood that he was speaking about them. Seeking to seize him, they feared the crowds, because they regarded him as a prophet.

—**Matthew 22:1.** And Jesus answered and again spoke to them in parables, saying:

## CHAPTER CXXV. The kingdom of heaven is like a king who made a wedding feast for his son

**Matthew 22:2–14; Luke 14:16–24**

“The kingdom of heaven has become like a king who made a wedding feast for his son. And he invited many. At the supper hour he sent his servants to call those invited to the wedding, but they were unwilling to come. And they all began together to make excuses.

“The first said to him: ‘I have bought a farm, and I must go out and see it. I ask you to excuse me.’ Another said: ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to test them. I ask you to excuse me.’ Another said: ‘I have taken a wife, and therefore I cannot come.’

“Again he sent other servants, saying: ‘Tell those invited: “Look, I have prepared my meal; my bulls and fattened animals have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding.”’

“But they disregarded it and went away, one to his farm and another to his business. The rest seized his servants, insulted them, and killed them. When the king heard this, he became angry; and sending his armies, he destroyed those murderers and burned their city.

“Then he said to his servants: ‘The wedding is indeed ready, but those who were invited were not worthy. Go therefore to the crossroads, into the streets and lanes and cities, and invite to the wedding whomever you find who are poor and weak, blind and lame.’

“And the servant said: ‘It has been done, lord, as you commanded, and there is still room.’

“And the lord said to the servant: ‘Go out onto the roads and among the hedges, and compel them to enter, so that my house may be filled. But I tell you that none of those men who were invited will taste my supper.’

“And his servants went out onto the roads and gathered all whom they found, bad and good, and the wedding hall was filled with those reclining at table.

“But the king entered to see those reclining at table, and he saw there a man who was not dressed in a wedding garment. And he said to him: ‘Friend, how did you enter here without a wedding garment?’ But he was speechless.

“Then the king said to the attendants: ‘Bind his feet and hands and throw him into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth there.’ For many are called, but few are chosen.”

## CHAPTER CXXVI. The Pharisees deceitfully send people to Jesus to ask whether it is permitted to pay tribute to Caesar

[Col. 0319A] **Matthew 22:15–22; Mark 12:13–17; Luke 20:20–26**

Then the Pharisees went away and took counsel to trap him in his speech. And they sent their disciples to him with the Herodians, saying:

“Teacher, we know that you are truthful, teach the way of God in truth, and are not concerned about anyone, for you do not look at the status of men. Tell us, therefore: What do you think? Is it permitted to pay the census tax to Caesar, or not?”

But Jesus, knowing their wickedness, said: “Why are you testing me, hypocrites? Show me the coin of the census tax.”

They offered him a denarius. And Jesus said to them: “Whose image and inscription is this?”

They said to him: “Caesar’s.”

Then he said to them: “Give back, therefore, to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”

When they heard this, they marveled, and leaving him, went away.

## CHAPTER CXXVII. Concerning the Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, and who ask about seven brothers who had one wife

**Matthew 22:23–33; Mark 12:18–27; Luke 20:27–39**

On that day the Sadducees approached him—those who say that there is no resurrection—and questioned him, saying:

“Teacher, Moses said: ‘If someone dies without having children, his brother is to marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’ Now there were seven brothers among us. The first, having taken a wife, died; and because he had no offspring, he left his wife to his brother. Likewise the second died without a son, and the third took her, and so all seven, and they left no offspring. Last of all, the woman also died. In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife will she be? For they all had her.”

Jesus said to them: “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures or the power of God. The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage; but those who are considered worthy of that age and of the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor take wives. For they cannot die any longer, but are like the angels of God in heaven, and are sons of God, since they are sons of the resurrection.
