“But that the dead rise, have you not read in the book of Moses, at the bush, how God spoke to him, saying: ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’ (Exodus 3:6)? He is not the God of the dead but of the living, for all live to him. Therefore you are greatly mistaken.”

When the crowds heard this, they marveled at his teaching. But some of the scribes answered and said: “Teacher, you have spoken well.”

[Note: The Vulgate has in Luke 20:35, “those who will be considered worthy.” Greek καταξιωθέντες, “having been considered worthy.”]

## CHAPTER CXXVIII. A scribe asks Jesus which commandment is greatest in the law

**Matthew 22:34–40; Mark 12:28–34; Luke 10:25–37**

When the Pharisees heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together. And one of the scribes, a teacher of the law, approached him, testing him and saying: “Teacher, which is the great commandment in the law?”

Jesus said to him: “The first commandment of all is: ‘Hear, Israel: the God of all of us is one God; and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind’ (Deuteronomy 6:4). This is the first and greatest commandment.

[Note: Who can tell me whence either Ammonius or the translator drew this reading? Greek: “the Lord our God” (Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν). The Vulgate: “the Lord your God.” But the better of our books, says Lucas Brugensis, in agreement with the Greek and Syriac and with the Hebrew law itself, write: “the Lord our God.”]

“The second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ On these two commandments the whole law and the prophets depend.”

And the scribe said to him: “Well said, Teacher; you have spoken truthfully, for he is one and there is no other besides him; and to love him with all the heart, with all the understanding, with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love one’s neighbor as oneself, is greater than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.”

When Jesus saw that he had answered wisely, he said to him: “You have answered correctly. Do this, and you will live.”

But wishing to justify himself, he said to Jesus: “And who is my neighbor?”

Jesus took up the question and said:

“A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers. They also stripped him and, after inflicting wounds, went away, leaving him half dead. It happened that a certain priest was going down the same road; and seeing him, he passed by. Likewise a Levite, when he was near the place and saw him, passed by.

“But a certain Samaritan, traveling, came near him; and when he saw him, he was moved with compassion. Approaching him, he bound his wounds, pouring wine and oil on them. Then he placed him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and cared for him. The next day he brought out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper, saying: ‘Take care of him, and whatever more you spend, I, when I return, will repay you.’

“Which of these three seems to you to have been a neighbor to the man who fell among robbers?”

He said: “The one who showed mercy to him.”

And Jesus said to him: “Go, and you do likewise.”

## CHAPTER CXXIX. While Jesus teaches in the temple, the Pharisees send to arrest him

**Luke 19:47–48**

He was teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests, scribes, and leaders of the people were seeking to destroy him, and they could not find what to do to him. For the whole people hung upon his words, listening to him.

—**John 7:32–52.** The Pharisees heard the crowd murmuring these things about him. And the chief priests and Pharisees sent officers to seize him.

Therefore Jesus said to them: “I am with you for a little while longer, and I am going to him who sent me. You will seek me and will not find me; and where I am, you cannot come.”

The Jews therefore said among themselves: “Where is this man going, that we shall not find him? Surely he is going to the dispersion among the Gentiles and will teach the Gentiles? What is this saying that he has made: ‘You will seek me and will not find me, and where I am, you cannot come’?”

On the last and great day of the festival, Jesus stood and cried out, saying: “If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink. Whoever believes in me, as Scripture says (Joel 2:28), rivers of living water will flow from his belly.”

He said this about the Spirit, which those who believed in him were to receive. For the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.

From that crowd, when they heard these words of his, some said: “This is truly the prophet.” Others said: “This is the Christ.” But some said: “Surely the Christ comes from Galilee? Does not Scripture say that the Christ comes from the offspring of David and from the village of Bethlehem, where David was (Micah 5:2)?”

Thus a division arose among the crowd because of him. Some of them wanted to seize him, but no one laid hands on him.

The officers therefore came to the chief priests and Pharisees, and they said to them: “Why did you not bring him?”

The officers answered: “No one has ever spoken as this man speaks.”

The Pharisees therefore answered them: “Have you also been led astray? Has any one of the rulers believed in him, or any of the Pharisees? But this crowd, which does not know the law, is accursed.”

Nicodemus said to them—the one who had come to him by night, who was one of them: “Does our law judge a man unless it first hears him and learns what he does?” (Deuteronomy 17:8; 19:15)

They answered and said to him: “Are you also from Galilee? Search and see: no prophet arises from Galilee.”

[Note: The current text indeed reads Greek ἐρεύνησον καὶ ἴδε, “search and see.” The Vulgate has “search the Scriptures,” as do several Greek manuscripts, including the Regius and Cantabrigiensis manuscripts, among others. Many good books, however, omit “the Scriptures,” in agreement with the Greek and Syriac. Lucas Brugensis.]

## CHAPTER CXXX. Jesus asks the Pharisees whose son the Christ is

[Col. 0321C] **Matthew 22:41–46; Luke 20:40–44**

When the Pharisees had gathered, Jesus questioned them, saying: “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?”

They said to him: “David’s.”

He said to them: “How then does David, in the book of Psalms, call him Lord, saying:

> ‘The Lord said to my Lord:  
> Sit at my right hand,  
> until I place your enemies  
> as a footstool for your feet’  
> (Psalm 109:1)?

“If therefore David calls him Lord in the Spirit, how is he his son?”

And no one was able to answer him a word, nor did anyone from that day dare to question him any further.

## CHAPTER CXXXI. Jesus teaches: “I am the light of the world”

**John 8:12–19**

Again, therefore, Jesus spoke to them, saying: “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness but will have the light of life.”

The Pharisees therefore said to him: “You testify about yourself; your testimony is not true.”

Jesus answered and said to them: “Even if I testify about myself, my testimony is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I come from or where I am going. You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one. And if I do judge, my judgment is true, because I am not alone, but I and the Father who sent me.

“And in your law it is written that the testimony of two men is true (Deuteronomy 17:6; 19:15). I am the one who testifies about myself, and the Father who sent me testifies about me.”

They therefore said to him: “Where is your father?”

Jesus answered: “You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, perhaps you would also know my Father.”

### John 8:21–59

“I am going away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come.”

The Jews therefore said: “Surely he will not kill himself, since he says: ‘Where I am going, you cannot come’?”

And he said to them: “You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world. Therefore I told you that you will die in your sins. For if you do not believe that I am, you will die in your sin.”

They therefore said to him: “Who are you?”

Jesus said to them: “The beginning—who is also speaking to you.” He has much to say and judge concerning you, but he who sent me is truthful; and what I heard from my Father, I speak in the world.

And they did not understand that he was calling his Father God.

[Note: The same reading occurs in the Vulgate, where, however, we read “Patrem ejus d. D.” Hence I suspect that Victor wrote: “he was speaking to them of the Father,” in accordance with the Greek, τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῖς ἔλεγεν. Lucas Brugensis makes many learned observations on this passage, both in his commentary, vol. II, pp. 1052, 1087, and in his more extensive notes, p. 385.]

[Note: The translator may have expressed this for explanatory purposes. For the Greek has παρ’ αὐτοῦ, “from him.” The Vulgate likewise has ab eo, “from him.”]

Therefore Jesus said to them: “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am, and that I do nothing of myself, but just as the Father taught me, so I speak. And he who sent me is with me; he has not left me alone, because I always do what pleases him.”

As he was saying these things, many believed in him.

Jesus therefore said to those who had believed in him [Note: I would regard this reading as due to a copyist’s error, perhaps arising because some manuscripts have “from among the Jews.” But “the Jews” should be read with the Vulgate translator, who adheres to the letter of the text.]: “O Jews, if you remain in my word, you will truly be my disciples, and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”

They answered him: “We are Abraham’s offspring and have never been enslaved to anyone. How can you say: ‘You will be free’?”

Jesus answered them: “Amen, amen, I say to you: everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin. A slave does not remain in the house forever; the son remains forever. Therefore, if the Son sets you free, you will truly be free.

“I know that you are Abraham’s children; yet you are seeking to kill me, because my word finds no place in you. I speak what I have seen with the Father, and you do what you have seen with your father.”

They answered and said to him: “Our father is Abraham.”

Jesus said to them: “If you are Abraham’s children, do the works of Abraham. But now you are seeking to kill me, a man who has spoken to you the truth that I heard from my Father. Abraham did not do this. You do the works of your father.”

They therefore said to him: “We were not born of fornication; we have one Father, God.”

Jesus therefore said to them: “If God were your Father, you would certainly love me, for I proceeded from God and came. For I did not come of myself; he sent me. Why do you not recognize my speech? Because you cannot hear my word.

“You are from the father, the devil, and you wish to do the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own resources, because he is a liar and its father.

“But because I speak the truth, you do not believe me. Which of you will convict me of sin? If I speak the truth, why do you not believe me?”

[Note: The Greek has εἰ δὲ ἀλήθειαν λέγω, “but if I speak the truth.” The Vulgate adds “to you” and omits the following “you.”]

“Whoever is from God hears the words of God. For this reason you do not hear, because you are not from God.”

The Jews therefore answered and said to him: “Are we not right in saying that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?”

Jesus answered: “I do not have a demon; rather, I honor my Father, and you have dishonored me. But I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks it and judges.

“Amen [Note: Perhaps another amen has dropped out; it is found in the Greek and the Vulgate.] I say to you: if anyone keeps my word, he will never see death.”

The Jews therefore said to him: “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham died, and the prophets, and you say: ‘If anyone keeps my word, he will never taste death.’ Surely you are not greater than our father Abraham, who died? And the prophets died. Whom do you make yourself?”

Jesus answered: “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, whom you say is your God. Yet you have not known him, but I know him. And if I said that I did not know him, I would be like you, a liar. But I know him and keep his word.

“Your father Abraham rejoiced that he might see my day; he saw it and was glad.”

[Note: The text reproduces καὶ εἶδε καὶ ἐχάρη, “and he saw and rejoiced.” Our ancient manuscripts, and not a few other Latin books, place the conjunction *et* before the word *vidit* as well, just as do the Greek and Syriac. Lucas Brugensis.]

The Jews therefore said to him: “You are not yet fifty years old, and have you seen Abraham?”

Jesus said to them: “Amen, amen, I say to you: before Abraham came to be, I am.”

Therefore they picked up stones to throw at him. But Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple.

## CHAPTER CXXXII. Jesus makes clay from spittle, places it on the eyes of a man born blind, and heals him

[Col. 0323D] **John 9:1–34**

As he passed by, he saw a man blind from birth. And his disciples asked him: “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he should be born blind?”

Jesus answered: “Neither this man sinned nor his parents, but that the works of God might be manifested in him. I must work the works of him who sent me while it is day; night is coming, when no one can work. As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”

When he had said these things, he spat on the ground and made clay from the spittle. He spread the clay over his eyes and said to him: “Go and wash in the pool of Siloam,” which is interpreted as “Sent.”

Therefore he went and washed, and came back seeing. And so the neighbors and those who saw him before, because he was a beggar, were saying: “Is this not the man who used to sit and beg?”

Some said: “This is he.” But others said: “No, but he is like him.”

He himself was saying: “I am he.”

Therefore they said to him: “How were your eyes opened?”

He answered: “The man who is called Jesus made clay, anointed my eyes, and said to me: ‘Go to the pool of Siloam and wash.’ I went, washed, and I see.”

They said to him: “Where is he?”

He said: “I do not know.”

They brought to the Pharisees the man who had been blind. Now it was the Sabbath when Jesus made the clay and opened his eyes. Again the Pharisees asked him how he had come to see.

But he said to them: “He put clay on my eyes, and I washed, and I see.”

Therefore some of the Pharisees said: “This man is not from God, for he does not keep the Sabbath.”

Others said: “How can a sinful man perform such signs?”

And there was a division among them.

[Note: Our manuscripts, in conformity with the Greek, omit the conjunction “but,” which other books add in agreement with the Syriac. Shortly afterward: “there was a schism among them,” following the Greek ἐν αὐτοῖς, “among them,” closely. A little later, the printed editions read: “he is like him.”]

Therefore they said again to the blind man: “What do you say about him who opened your eyes?”

But he said: “He is a prophet.”

The Jews therefore did not believe that he had been blind, * until they called his parents—of him who had seen [the printed wording *qui viderat* is uncertain].

And they questioned them, saying: “Is this your son, whom you say was born blind? How then does he now see?”

His parents answered and said: “We know that this is our son and that he was born blind. But how he now sees we do not know; nor do we know who opened his eyes. Ask him; he is of age. Let him speak for himself.”

His parents said these things because they feared the Jews. For the Jews had already agreed that if anyone confessed him to be the Christ, he would be expelled from the synagogue. Therefore his parents said: “He is of age; ask him.”

Therefore they called again the man who had been blind and said to him: “Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.”

He therefore said: “Whether he is a sinner, I do not know. One thing I know: though I was blind, now I see.”

They therefore said to him: “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?”

He answered them: “I have already told you, and you heard. Why do you want to hear it again? Surely you also want to become his disciples?”

They * reviled him and said: “You are his disciple; but we are disciples of Moses. We know that God spoke to Moses; but as for this man, we do not know where he is from.”

That man answered and said to them: “This is astonishing: you do not know where he is from, and yet he opened my eyes. We know that God does not hear sinners; but if anyone worships God and does his will, he hears him. From the beginning of time it has not been heard that anyone opened the eyes of one born blind. If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.”

They answered and said to him: “You were born entirely in sins, and you are teaching us?”

And they cast him out.

[Note: The Vulgate has “in sins,” agreeing with the Greek ἐν ἁμαρτίαις.]

## CHAPTER CXXXIII. Jesus makes himself known to the same blind man and disputes at length with the Jews

**John 9:35–41**

Jesus heard that they had cast him out. When he found him, he said to him: “Do you believe in the Son of God?”

He answered and said: “Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?”

And Jesus said to him: “You have both seen him, and the one speaking with you is he.”

* He said: “I believe, Lord.” And falling down, he worshiped him.

Jesus said to him [Note: The Vulgate has “And Jesus said.” Nor is it otherwise in the Greek. We omit noting the remaining textual variants from this point onward, content to indicate them all by this one sign *]:

“I have come into this world for judgment: so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind.”

Those of the Pharisees who were with him heard this and said to him: “Are we also blind?”

Jesus said to them: “If you were blind, you would not have sin. But now, * because you say, ‘We see,’ your sin remains.”

### John 10:1–21

“Amen * I say to you: whoever does not enter the sheepfold through the gate, but climbs in by another way, is a thief and a robber. But whoever enters through the gate is the shepherd of the sheep. The gatekeeper opens to him, and the sheep hear his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.

“When he has brought out his own sheep, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice. They do not follow a stranger, but flee from him, because they do not know the voice of strangers.”

Jesus spoke this proverb to them, but they did not understand what he was saying to them.

Therefore Jesus said * again: “Amen * I say to you: I am the gate of the sheep. All who came are thieves and robbers, * but the sheep did not listen to them. I am the gate. If anyone enters through me, (he will be saved), and he will go in and out and find pasture. The thief comes only to steal, slaughter, and destroy. I came so that they may have life (and have it more abundantly).

“I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd gives his life for the sheep *. The hired man, who is not the shepherd and whose sheep are not his own, sees the wolf coming, abandons the sheep, and flees. And the wolf seizes and scatters the sheep. The hired man flees because he is a hired man and has no concern for the sheep.

“I am the good shepherd. I know my own, and my own know me, just as the Father knows me and I know the Father. And I lay down my life for my sheep. I have other sheep that are not of this fold; I must bring them also, and they will hear my voice. And there will be one flock and one shepherd.

“For this reason the Father loves me, because I lay down my life (that I may take it up again). No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of myself. * I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it up again. I received this commandment from my Father.”

Again a division arose among the Jews because of these words. Many of them were saying: “He has a demon and is insane. Why do you listen to him?”

Others said: “These words are not those of one who has a demon. Surely a demon can open the eyes of the blind?”

## CHAPTER CXXXIV. The Jews ask Jesus: “If you are the Christ, tell us openly”

**John 10:22–42**

The Feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem, and it was winter. Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon’s portico. Therefore the Jews surrounded him and said to him: “How long will you keep us in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.”

Jesus answered them: “I speak to you, and you do not believe. The works that I do in my Father’s name testify about me; but you do not believe, because you are not among my sheep. My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them from my hand. My Father, that which he has given me, is greater than all, and no one can snatch it from the hand of my Father. I and the Father are one.”

The Jews * picked up stones to stone him.

Jesus answered them: “I have shown you many good works from my Father. For which of these works are you stoning me?”

The Jews answered him: “We are not stoning you for a good work, but for blasphemy, and because, although you are a man, you make yourself God.”

Jesus answered them: “Is it not written in your law: ‘I said, you are gods’ (Psalm 81:6)? If he called those gods to whom the word of God came—and Scripture cannot be broken—do you say to the one whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, ‘You blaspheme,’ because I said, ‘I am the Son of God’?

“If I do not perform the works of my Father, do not believe me. But if I do them, even if you do not wish to believe me, believe the works, so that you may know and believe that the Father is in me and I am in the Father.”

Therefore they were seeking * to seize him, but he escaped from their hands.

And he went away again across the Jordan, to the place where John had first been baptizing, and he remained there. Many came to him and said: “John indeed performed no sign, but everything John said about this man was true.”

And many believed in him.

## CHAPTER CXXXV. Jesus raises Lazarus from the dead; the chief priests and leaders hold a council to kill him

[Col. 0326D]

## JOHN 11:1–56

There was a certain man who was ill, Lazarus of Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha. Mary was the one who anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair; her brother Lazarus was ill. So the sisters sent to him, saying: “Lord, behold, the one whom you love is ill.”

When Jesus heard this, he said to them: “This illness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.” Jesus [Col. 0327A] loved Martha and her sister Mary and Lazarus. When he therefore heard that he was ill, he then remained in the same place for two days. After this he said to his disciples: “Let us go again into Judea.” The disciples said to him: “Rabbi, * are you going into Judea? Now the Jews were seeking to stone you, and are you going there again?”

Jesus answered: “Are there not twelve hours of the day? If anyone walks during the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world; but if he walks during the night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him.” He said these things, and afterward said to them: “Lazarus, our friend, is sleeping; but I am going to awaken him from sleep.” His disciples therefore said: “Lord, if he is sleeping, he will be safe.” But Jesus had spoken of his death, while they thought that he was speaking about ordinary sleep. Then Jesus said [Col. 0327B] to them plainly: “Lazarus is dead; and I rejoice for your sake, so that you may believe, because I was not there. But let us go to him.”

Then Thomas, who is called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples: “Let us also go, so that we may die with him.” Jesus therefore came and found that he had already been four days in the tomb *.

Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stades away. Many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them concerning their brother. When Martha heard that Jesus had come, she went out to meet him; but Mary remained sitting at home. Martha therefore said to Jesus: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died. But even now I know that whatever you ask of God, God will give you.”

Jesus said to her: “Your brother will rise again.” Martha * therefore said: “I know that he will rise in the resurrection [Col. 0327C], on the last day.” Jesus said to her: “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, even if he has died, will live. And everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”

She said to him: “Indeed, Lord. I have believed that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God, who has come into this world.”

When she had said this, she went away and quietly called her sister Mary, saying: “The Teacher is here and is calling you.” When she heard this, she rose quickly and came to him. For Jesus had not yet entered the village, but was still in the place where Martha had met him.

The Jews who were with her in the house and were consoling her, when they saw Mary—that she had risen quickly and gone out—followed her, saying: “She is going to the tomb to weep there.” When Mary came to where Jesus was [Col. 0327D] and saw him, she fell at his feet and said to him: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.”

When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her weeping, he * groaned in spirit, troubled himself, and said: “Where have you laid him?” They said to him: “Lord, come and see.” And Jesus wept.

Then the Jews said: “See how he loved him.” But some of them said: “Could not this man, who opened the eyes of the blind *, have caused this man not to die?”

Jesus therefore, again groaning within himself, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone had been placed over it *. Jesus said: “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of the one who had died, said to him: “Lord, he already stinks, for he has been dead four days.”

Jesus said to her [Col. 0328A]: “Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?” So they took away the stone. But Jesus, lifting his eyes upward, said: “Father, I give you thanks because you have heard me. I knew, indeed, that you always hear me; but because of the crowd standing around, I said this, so that they may believe that you sent me.”

When he had said this, he cried out with a loud voice: “Lazarus, come out!” Immediately the man who had been dead came out, his feet and hands bound with wrappings, and his face bound with a cloth. Jesus said to them: “Unbind him, and let him go.”

Many therefore of the Jews who had come to Mary * and had seen what Jesus did believed in him. But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.

So the chief priests and the Pharisees convened a council and said [Col. 0328B]: “What are we to do? For this man performs many signs. If we leave him alone in this way, everyone will believe in him; and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.”

One of them, named Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them: “You know nothing at all, nor do you consider that it is expedient * for us that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation should not perish.”

He did not say this on his own authority; but, being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was going to die for the nation—and not only for the nation, but also to gather into one the children of God who were scattered abroad.

From that day, therefore, they planned to kill him. Jesus therefore no longer walked openly among the Jews, but went away to the region near the wilderness, to a city called Ephrem; and there he stayed [Col. 0328C] with his disciples.

Now the Passover of the Jews was near, and many went up to Jerusalem from the region before the Passover, to purify themselves. They were looking for Jesus and said to one another, standing in the temple: “What do you think—that he will not come to the feast?” The chief priests and the Pharisees had given orders that if anyone knew where he was, he should report it, so that they might seize him.

## CHAPTER CXXXVI. Jesus Is Not Received in a Samaritan City; John and James Say to Him: “If You Wish, Shall We Command Fire to Come Down from Heaven?”

### LUKE 9:51–56

When the days of his assumption were being fulfilled, he himself firmly set his face to go to Jerusalem. And he sent * [Col. 0328D] a messenger ahead of him. As they went, they entered a city of the Samaritans to make preparations for him. But they did not receive him, because his face was set toward Jerusalem.

When his disciples James and John saw this, they said: “Lord, do you want us to say that fire should come down from heaven and consume them?” But he turned and rebuked them, saying: “You do not know what spirit you are of. The Son of man did not come to destroy souls, but to save them.” And they went to another village.

## CHAPTER CXXXVII. Jesus Comes to Bethany; Many of the Jews, Going There Because of Lazarus, Believe in Him

### JOHN 12:1–9–19; MATTHEW 26:6

Jesus therefore, six days before the Passover, came to Bethany, where Lazarus had died, whom Jesus had raised [Col. 0329A] from the dead. And when he was in the house of Simon the leper, a great crowd of the Jews learned that he was there; and they came not only because of Jesus, but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.

The Pharisees therefore said among themselves: “You see that we are accomplishing nothing? Behold, the whole world has gone after him.” But the chief priests planned to kill Lazarus also, because many of the Jews were going away because of him and * believed in Jesus.

They made him a supper there, and Martha served; Lazarus, meanwhile, was one of those reclining at table with him.

## CHAPTER CXXXVIII. Mary Pours an Alabaster Jar of Ointment on Jesus’ Head; and Jesus Rebukes the Pharisee

[Col. 0329B]

### JOHN 12:3–8; MARK 14:3–9; MATTHEW 26:6–13

Mary therefore, having an alabaster jar of precious spikenard ointment, broke the alabaster jar and poured it over his head as he reclined, and anointed his feet and wiped them with her hair; and the house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.

Then one of his disciples, Judas * Iscariot, who was going to betray him, said: “Why was this ointment not sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?” He said this not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief and, having the money box, carried away what was put into it.

Some, however, were indignant among themselves and said: “Why has this waste of ointment been made?” But Jesus, knowing this, said to them: “Why do you trouble this woman? She has performed a good work for me. For you will always have the poor [Col. 0329C] * with you, and whenever you wish, you can do good to them; but you will not always * have me. For by putting this ointment on my body, she has done it for my burial. Truly I say to you: Wherever this Gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”

### LUKE 7:39–50

When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said within himself: “If this man were a prophet, he would certainly know what kind of * woman this is who is touching him, because she is a sinner.”

And Jesus, answering, said to him: “Simon, I have something to say to you.” He said: “Teacher, speak.”

“There were two debtors to a certain moneylender: one owed five hundred denarii, * the other fifty. [Col. 0329D] Since they had nothing with which to repay, he forgave both of them. Which of them, then, will love him more *?”

Simon answered: “I suppose the one to whom he forgave more.” And he said to him: “You have judged correctly.”

Then turning toward the woman, he said: “* Simon, do you see this woman? I entered your house; you did not give me water for my feet, but she has washed my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair. You did not give me a kiss, but she, from the moment I * entered, has not ceased kissing my feet. You did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment.

“Therefore I say to you: * Many sins will be forgiven her, because she loved much. But the one to whom little is forgiven loves little.”

Then he said to her [Col. 0330A]: “Your sins are forgiven.” And those reclining at table with him began to say among themselves: “Who is this, who even forgives sins?”

But he said to the woman: “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”

### LUKE 19:28

When he had said these things, he went away, ascending to Jerusalem.

## CHAPTER CXXXIX. In Jerusalem the Greeks Wish to See Jesus

### JOHN 12:20–36

There were certain gentiles among those who had gone up to worship on the feast day. These therefore approached Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying: “Lord, we wish to see Jesus.”

Philip came and told Andrew. Andrew in turn and Philip * told Jesus. But Jesus answered them, saying: “The hour has come for the Son of man to be glorified.

“Truly, truly, I say to you: Unless a grain of wheat, falling into the ground, dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it produces much [Col. 0330B] fruit. Whoever loves his life will lose it; and whoever hates his life in this world preserves it for eternal life.

“If anyone serves me, let him follow me; and where I am, there my servant also will be. If anyone serves me, my Father will honor him.

“Now my soul is troubled. And what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour. But for this reason I have come to this hour. Father, glorify your name.”

Then a voice came from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.”

The crowd therefore that stood by and heard it said that * it had been thunder. Others said: “An angel has spoken to him.”

Jesus answered and said: “This voice did not come for my sake, but for yours. Now is the judgment of the world; now the prince of this world will be cast out. And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw everything [Col. 0330C] to myself.”

He said this signifying by what death he was going to die. The crowd answered him: “We have heard from the Law that the Christ remains forever (Psalm 109:4; 116:25; Isaiah 40:8; Ezekiel 37:25). And how do you say, ‘The Son of man must be lifted up’?”

Jesus therefore said to them: “The light is with you for a little while longer. Walk while you have the light, so that darkness may not seize you. Whoever walks in darkness does not know where he is going. While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may be sons of light.”

## CHAPTER CXL. The Pharisees Ask Jesus When the Kingdom of God Will Come

### LUKE 17:20–21; 21:37–38

When he was asked [Col. 0330D] by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God would come, he answered them and said: “The kingdom of God does not come with observation; nor will they say, ‘Behold, here!’ or ‘Behold, there!’ For behold, the kingdom of God is within you.”

During those days he was teaching in the temple; but at night he went out and stayed on the Mount of Olives. And all the people * kept coming to him in the temple to hear him.

### MATTHEW 23:1–36

Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his disciples, saying: “The scribes and Pharisees have sat on Moses’ seat. Therefore, whatever they tell you, observe and do; but do not act according to their works [Col. 0331A], for they say and do not do.

### LUKE 11:46

“They bind heavy and unbearable burdens and place them on people’s shoulders, but with their own finger * they are unable to move them.

### MARK 12:37–38

—and they wish to walk about in robes. For they love the first places at banquets and the chief seats in synagogues, greetings in the marketplace, and to be called rabbi. (And all the people gladly listened to him.)

“But you must not be called rabbi, for one is your teacher, and you are all brothers. And do not call anyone your father on earth, for one is your Father, who is in heaven. Nor be called teachers, because [Col. 0331B] one is your teacher, the Christ. Whoever is greater among you will be your servant. Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”

### LUKE 11:43; 20:46

“Woe to you, Pharisees, because you love the chief seats in synagogues and greetings in the marketplace.

“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocritical interpreters of the Law, because you have taken away the key of knowledge and shut the kingdom of heaven before people; you yourselves do not enter, nor do you permit those entering to enter.”

### MARK 12:39; LUKE 20:47

“Woe to you, hypocritical Pharisees, who devour widows’ houses under the pretext of lengthy prayer; you will receive the greater condemnation.

“Woe to you, scribes and hypocritical Pharisees, who travel around sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he has been made one, you make him twice as much a son of Gehenna [Col. 0331C] as yourselves.

“Woe to you, blind guides, who say: ‘Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple is bound by his oath.’ Fools and blind men, for which is greater: the gold, or the temple that sanctifies the gold?

“And whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is upon it is bound by his oath. Blind men, for which is greater: the gift, or the altar that sanctifies the gift?

“Therefore, whoever swears by the altar swears by it and by everything that is upon it. And whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by him who dwells in it. And whoever swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by him who sits upon it.”

### LUKE 11:42

“Woe to you, scribes and hypocritical Pharisees, who tithe mint and dill and cumin and rue and every herb, but have abandoned the weightier matters of the Law: [Col. 0331D] judgment and mercy and faith and the love of God. These things you ought to have done, without omitting the others. Blind guides, who strain out a gnat but swallow a camel.

### LUKE 11:39–51

“Woe to you, scribes and hypocritical Pharisees, who cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside you are full of plunder and uncleanness. Blind Pharisee, first cleanse what is inside the cup and the dish, so that what is outside may also become clean.

“Woe to you, because you are like graves that are not visible, and people walking over them do not know it.

“Woe to you, scribes and hypocritical Pharisees, because you are like whitewashed tombs, which appear beautiful to people on the outside, but inside are full of the bones of the dead and every impurity. So you also [Col. 0332A] * appear righteous to people on the outside, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.”

One of the interpreters of the Law answered and said to him: “Teacher, in saying these things you also insult us.”

But he said: “And woe to you interpreters of the Law, who load people with burdens that cannot be carried, while you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.

“Woe to you, scribes and hypocritical Pharisees, because you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous, and say: ‘If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been their partners in the blood of the prophets.’ Thus you bear witness against yourselves that you are sons of those who killed the prophets. And you—fill up the measure of your fathers!

“Serpents, offspring of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of Gehenna? Therefore the Wisdom of God also said: [Col. 0332B] ‘I will send them prophets and apostles and wise men and scribes; and some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city, so that all the righteous blood poured out upon the earth may come upon you, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah, son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the temple and the altar.’

“Truly I say to you, all these things will come upon this generation.”

### MATTHEW 23:37–39; LUKE 13:34–35

“Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which kills the prophets and stones those who are * sent to you, how often I wanted to gather your children, just as a hen gathers her chicks [Col. 0332C] under her wings *, and you were unwilling! Behold, your house will be left to you desolate. For I say to you: You will not see me from now on, until you say: ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.’”

## CHAPTER CXLIII. Many of the Rulers Believed in Him, but They Did Not Confess Him, So That They Would Not Be Expelled from the Synagogue

### JOHN 12:42–50

Nevertheless, many even of the rulers believed in him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess him, so that they would not be expelled from the synagogue. For they loved the glory of people more than the glory of God.

But Jesus cried out and said: “Whoever believes in me does not believe in me, but in him who sent me. And whoever sees me sees him who sent me. I have come into the world as light, so that everyone who believes in me may not remain in darkness [Col. 0332D].

“And if anyone hears my words and does not keep them, I do not judge him; for I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world. Whoever rejects me and does not accept my words has one who judges him. The word that I have spoken—that will judge him on the last day, because I have not spoken from myself, but the Father who sent me himself gave me a command: what I should say, * and what I should speak. And I know that his commandment is eternal life. Therefore, whatever I speak, I speak just as the Father has told me.”

### JOHN 12:36–41

Jesus said these things to them, and went away and hid himself from them. Although he had performed so many signs before them, they did not believe in him, so that the word of the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled, which he said:

“Lord, who has believed our [Col. 0333A] report, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?” (Isaiah 53:1)

Isaiah said this when he saw his glory, and he spoke about him.

## CHAPTER CXLV. While Jesus Sits on the Mount of Olives, the Disciples Ask Him: “What Will Be the Sign of Your Coming?” or “Of the Things You Have Said?” And He Speaks of the Destruction of Jerusalem and of Signs and Wonders

### MATTHEW 24:3–31; MARK 13:3–27; LUKE 21:7–28

[Col. 0333B]

When he was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, the disciples approached him privately and asked him, saying: “Teacher, tell us when these things will happen, and what will be the sign of your coming, when all these things begin to be fulfilled?”

And he said to the disciples: “Days will come when you will desire to see one day of the Son of man, and you will not see it. Take care that no one misleads you. For many will come in my name, saying: ‘I am the Christ,’ and they will mislead many.

“When you hear of battles and reports of wars and uprisings, do not be terrified. For these things must happen, but the end is not yet. [Col. 0333C] Nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom; and there will be pestilences, famines, and earthquakes in various places, and terrors from heaven, and great signs. But all these things are the beginning of sorrows.

“Then they will hand you over to tribulation and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations because of my name. And not a hair from your head will perish. By your endurance you will possess your souls.

“Therefore put it in your hearts not to prepare beforehand how you will answer; for I will give you a mouth and wisdom which all your adversaries will not be able to resist or contradict.

“Then many will stumble, and they will hand one another over and hate one another. Many false prophets will arise and mislead many. And because * iniquity will abound, the love of many will grow cold. But whoever perseveres [Col. 0333D] to the end will be saved.

“And this Gospel of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the whole world as a testimony to all nations; and then the end will come.

“Therefore, when you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by the prophet Daniel, standing in the holy place—let the reader understand—

### LUKE 21:20–24

“when you see Jerusalem surrounded by an army, then know that * its desolation will draw near. Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains; those who are in its midst, let them depart; and those who are in the countryside, let them not enter it, because these are days of vengeance, so that all the things that are written may be fulfilled.

“Woe to those who are pregnant and nursing in those days! For there will be great distress upon the earth and wrath against this people. And they will fall by the edge of the sword and [Col. 0334A] be led captive among all nations; and Jerusalem will be trampled by the nations until the times of the nations are fulfilled.

### LUKE 17:23–24

“Then if anyone says to you: ‘Behold, here is the Christ,’ or ‘There,’ do not believe it. For false Christs and false prophets will arise and will give great signs and wonders, so that, if possible, even the elect may be led astray. Behold, I have foretold it to you.

“Therefore, if they say to you: [Col. 0334B] ‘Behold, he is in the wilderness,’ do not go out; ‘Behold, he is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it. For just as lightning comes out from the east and appears even to the west, so will be the coming of the Son of man.

## CHAPTER CXLIX. Concerning the One Who Went Abroad and Distributed Talents to His Servants

### MATTHEW 25:14–30

“For it is like a man going abroad who called his servants and handed over his possessions [Col. 0336B] to them. To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one—to each according to his own ability—and immediately he went away.

“The one who had received five talents went and worked with them and gained another five. Likewise * the one who had received two gained another two. But the one who had received one went away, dug in the ground, and hid his master’s money.

“After a long time the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them. The one who had received five talents came forward and offered another five talents, saying: ‘Master, you handed over five talents to me; behold, I have gained another five.’

“His master said to him: ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! Because you were faithful over a little, I will appoint you over much. Enter into the joy of your master.’

“The one who had received two talents also came forward [Col. 0336C] and said: ‘Master, you handed over two talents to me; behold, I have gained another two.’

“His master said to him: ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! Because you were faithful over a little, I will appoint you over much. Enter into the joy of your master.’

“But the one who had received one talent came forward and said: ‘Master, I know that you are a hard man: you reap where you did not sow and gather where you did not scatter; and being afraid, I went away and hid your talent in the ground. Behold, you have what is yours.’

“His master answered and said to him: ‘Evil and lazy servant, you knew that I reap where I do not sow and gather where I did not scatter. Therefore you ought * to have entrusted my money to the bankers, and when I came I would certainly have received what was mine with interest.

### MARK 4:25; LUKE 8:18

“For to everyone who has, more will be given, and he will abound; but from the one who does not have, even what he seems to have will be taken away from him.

## CHAPTER CL. That the Loins Should Always Be Girded and the Lamps Burning

### LUKE 12:35–38

“Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning *; and be like people waiting for their master, when he will return from the wedding, so that when he comes and knocks, they may immediately open to him.

“Blessed are those servants whom, when the master comes, he finds watching. Truly I say to you, [Col. 0337A] he will gird himself, make them recline at table, and, passing by, serve them.

“And if he comes during the second watch, and if he comes during the third watch and finds them so, blessed * are those servants.”

## CHAPTER CLI. Concerning the One Who Went Abroad to Obtain a Kingdom for Himself; As He Departed, He Gave Ten Minas to His Servants

### LUKE 19:12–27

He therefore said: “A certain nobleman went to a distant region to receive a kingdom for himself and then return. Calling ten of his servants, he gave them ten minas and said to them: ‘Do business until I come.’

“But his citizens hated him and sent a delegation after him, saying: ‘We do not want this man to reign over us.’

“And it happened * that when he returned after receiving the kingdom, he ordered the servants to whom he had given the money [Col. 0337B] to be summoned, so that he might know how much each had made through business.

“The first came, saying: ‘Master, your mina has earned ten minas.’ And he said to him: ‘Well done, good servant! Because you were faithful in a very little, you will have authority over ten cities.’

“Another came, saying: ‘Master, your mina has made five minas.’ And he said to this one also: ‘And you, be over five cities.’

“Another came, saying: ‘Master, behold your mina, which I kept stored away in a cloth; * for I was afraid of you, because you are a stern man: you take up what you did not put down, and reap what you did not sow.’

“He said to him: ‘I will judge you from your own mouth, wicked servant. You knew that I am a stern man, taking up what I did not put down and reaping what I did not sow. Why, then, did you not put my money on the bank; * so that, when I came, I might have collected it with interest?’

“And he said to those standing [Col. 0337C] by: ‘Take the mina away from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.’”

They said to him: “Master, he has ten minas.”

“But I say to you: To everyone who has, more will be given *. But from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.

“Nevertheless, bring here my enemies who did not want me to reign over them, and kill them before me.”

## CHAPTER CLII. When the Son of Man Comes on the Seat of His Majesty
MATTHEW 25:31–41. But when the Son of Man comes in his majesty, and all the angels with him, then he will sit upon the seat of his majesty; and all the nations will be gathered before him. He will separate them from one another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats. And he will set the sheep at his right hand, but the goats at his left. [Col. 0337D]

Then the King will say to those who will be at his right hand: “Come, blessed of my Father; possess the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry, and you gave me food; I was thirsty, and you gave me drink; I was a stranger, and you welcomed me; naked, and you clothed me; sick, and you visited me; I was in prison, and you came to me.”

Then the righteous will answer him, saying: “Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you; thirsty and give you drink? And when did we see you a stranger and welcome you; or naked and clothe you? Or when did we see you sick, or in prison, and come to you?”

And the King, answering, will say to them: “Amen, I say to you, insofar as you did this for one of these least of my brothers, you did it for me.” [Col. 0338A]

Then he will say also to those who will be at his left: “Depart from me, accursed ones, into the eternal fire, which has been prepared for the devil and his angels. For I was hungry, and you did not give me food; I was thirsty, and you did not give me drink; I was a stranger, and you did not welcome me; naked, and you did not clothe me; sick, * and you did not visit me; and I was in prison, and you did not come to me.”

Then they themselves will answer: “Lord, when did we see you hungry and thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister to you?”

Then he will answer them, saying: “Amen, I say to you, insofar as you did not do this for one of these least, neither did you do it for me.” And these will go into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.

## CHAPTER CLIII. [Col. 0338B] Again the chief priests take counsel. And Judas goes to them.

MATTHEW 26:1–5, 14–16; MARK 14:1, 2, 10, 11; LUKE 22:1–6. And it happened that, when Jesus had finished all these sayings, he said to his disciples: “You know that after two days the Passover will take place, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”

Then the chief priests and the elders of the people gathered in the court of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas; and they took counsel to seize Jesus by deceit and kill him. But they were saying: “Not on the feast day, lest perhaps a tumult arise among the people.”

Then one of the Twelve, who * is called Judas * Iscariot, went away and spoke with the chief priests and magistrates, and said to them: “What are you willing to give [Col. 0338C] me, and I will hand him over to you?” When they heard this, they rejoiced and appointed for him thirty pieces of silver. And from then on he sought an opportunity to hand him over without the crowds.

## CHAPTER CLIV. Jesus washed the feet of his disciples.

JOHN 13:1–20. Before the feast day of Passover, Jesus, knowing that his hour had come to pass from this world to the Father, having loved his own who were in the world, loved them to the end. And when supper had taken place, the devil having already put it into the heart of Judas, the son of Simon, * Iscariot, to betray him, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come forth from God and was going to God, he rose from supper and laid aside his garments. And when he had taken a towel, he girded himself; then he poured water into a basin [Col. 0338D] and began to wash the disciples’ feet and to wipe them with the towel with which he was girded.

Therefore he came to Simon Peter. And Peter said to him: “Lord, are you washing my feet?” Jesus answered and said to him: “What I am doing, you do not know now; but afterward you will know.”

Peter said to him: “You shall never wash my feet.” Jesus answered and said: “If I do not wash you, you will have no share with me.”

Simon Peter said to him: “Lord, not only my feet, but also my hands and my head.” Jesus said to him: “One who has been washed needs only to wash his feet, but is entirely clean. And you are clean, but not all”; for he knew who it was that would betray him. Therefore he said: “You are not all clean.”

After he had washed their feet, he took his garments [Col. 0339A]; and when he had reclined again, he said to them: “Do you know what I have done for you? You call me Teacher and Lord, and you speak rightly, for so I am. If therefore I, the Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet. For I have given you an example, so that, just as I have done for you, you also may do. Amen, amen, I say to you: A servant is not greater than his master, nor is an apostle greater than the one who sent him. If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.

“I am not speaking about all of you; I know whom I have chosen. But this is so that the Scripture may be fulfilled: ‘The one who eats bread with me will lift up his heel against me’ (Psalm 40:10). From now on I tell you, before it happens, so that when it has happened you may believe that I am. Amen, amen, I say to you: Whoever receives anyone whom I send receives me [Col. 0339B]; and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me.”

## CHAPTER CLV. He sends his disciples to prepare the Passover for him. And he says to them: “One of you will betray me.”

MATTHEW 26:17–24; MARK 14:12–21; LUKE 22:7–23. On the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples approached Jesus, saying: “Where do you wish us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?”

But Jesus said: “Go into the city to a certain man; and as you enter, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house he enters, and say to the master of the house: ‘The Teacher says: My time is near; I am keeping the Passover with my disciples at your house.’ And he himself will show you a large upper room furnished; there prepare for us.”

And [Col. 0339C] his disciples went away and came into the city, and found it as he had told them; and they prepared the Passover. When evening had come, he arrived and reclined with his twelve disciples. And as they were eating, he said: “I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer. For I say to you that from now on I will not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”

—JOHN 13:21–32. When he had said these things, Jesus was troubled in spirit, and testified and said: “Amen, amen, I say to you, one of you will betray me.”

Then they began to be sorrowful and to say one by one: “Surely it is I, Lord?” He said to them: “The one who dips his hand with me into the dish will betray me. Indeed, the Son of Man goes, as it is written concerning him. But woe to that man through whom the Son of Man will be betrayed! It would have been good [Col. 0339D] for that man if he had not been born.”

The disciples looked at one another, uncertain of whom he was speaking, and asked among themselves which of them would do this. Now one of his disciples was reclining on Jesus’ breast, the one whom Jesus loved. Simon Peter therefore gestured to him and said to him: “Who is it of whom he speaks?”

When he had reclined upon Jesus’ breast, he said to him: “Lord, who is it?” Jesus answered him: “It is the one to whom I shall give the morsel after I have dipped it.” And when he had dipped the bread, he gave it to Judas, the son of Simon, * Iscariot. And after the morsel, Satan entered into him. And Jesus said to him: “What you are doing, do quickly.”

But none of those reclining knew why he had said this to him. For some thought, because Judas kept the money box, [Col. 0340A] that Jesus was saying to him: “Buy what we need for the feast”; or that he should give something to the poor.

But Judas, who betrayed him, answering, said: “Surely it is I, Rabbi?” He said to him: “You have said it.” Therefore, when he had received the morsel, he went out immediately. And it was night.

Therefore, when he had gone out, Jesus said: “Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God has been glorified in him. If God has been glorified in him, God has * glorified him in himself, and he will glorify him immediately.”

## CHAPTER CLVI. Jesus gave his disciples the sacrament of his body and blood. And he says to Peter: “Satan demanded that he might sift you.” And: “All of you will be scandalized because of me today.”

MATTHEW 26:26–35; MARK 14:26–31; LUKE 22:14–20. [Col. 0340B] While they were dining, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to his disciples, saying: “Take and eat; this is my body, which is given for you.”

And taking the cup, he gave thanks, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them, saying: “Drink from it, all of you. For this is my blood of the New Testament, which will be poured out for you and for many for the forgiveness of sins. But I say to you: From now on I will not drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I shall drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father. Do this in remembrance of me.”

—LUKE 22:31, 32. And the Lord said to Simon: “Simon, * behold, Satan demanded you, to sift you like wheat. But I prayed for you, that your faith may not fail; and you, once converted, strengthen your brothers.” [Col. 0340C]

—JOHN 13:33–38. “Little children, I am with you only a little longer. You will seek me; and as I said to the Jews, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come,’ so I say to you now. I give you a new commandment: that you love one another as I have loved you, so that you also may love one another. By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.”

Simon Peter said to him: “Lord, where are you going?” Jesus answered: “Where I am going, you cannot follow me now; but afterward you will follow.”

Then Jesus said to them: “All of you will suffer scandal because of me on this night. For it is written: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered’ (Zechariah 13:7). But after I have risen, I will go before you into Galilee.”

Peter, answering, said to him: “Even if all are scandalized [Col. 0340D] because of you, I will never be scandalized; for I am ready to go with you both into prison and into death. I will lay down my life for you.”

Jesus answered him: “Will you lay down your life for me? Amen, amen, I say to you: this night, before the cock crows, you will deny me three times.”

Peter said to him: “Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you.” Likewise all the disciples said.

## CHAPTER CLVII. He exhorts his disciples not to let their hearts be troubled.

JOHN 14:1–31. “Let not your heart be troubled. You believe in God; believe also in me. In my Father’s house are many dwelling places. If it were otherwise, I would have told you, [Col. 0341A] because I am going to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and take you to myself, so that where I am, you also may be. And you know where I am going, and you know the way.”

Thomas said to him: “Lord, we do not know where you are going; how can we know the way?”

Jesus said to him: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me. If you had known me, you would certainly have known my Father also. * Even now you will know him, and you have seen him.”

Philip said to him: “Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us.”

Jesus said to him: “Have I been with you for so long, and you have not known me, Philip? * Whoever has seen me has seen the Father also. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’? Do you not * believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? The words that I speak to you I do not speak from myself. [Col. 0341B] But the Father, remaining in me, himself does the works. Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? Otherwise, believe because of the works themselves.

“Amen, amen, I say to you: Whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do, and will do greater works than these, because I am going to the Father. And whatever you ask the Father in my name, I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son. If you ask me anything in my name, I will do it.

“If you love me, keep my commandments. And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Paraclete, to remain with you forever: the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him. But you will know him, because he will remain with you and will be in you.

“I will not leave you orphans; I will come to you. Yet a little while, and [Col. 0341C] the world will no longer see me. But you will see me, because I live, and you will live. On that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.

“Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, that is the one who loves me. And whoever loves me will be loved by my Father; and I will love him and manifest myself to him.”

Judas, not the * Iscariot, said to him: “Lord, what * will you do, because you are going to manifest yourself to us and not to the world?”

Jesus answered and said to him: “If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him; and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him. Whoever does not love me does not keep my words. And the word that you have heard is not mine, but the Father’s, who sent me.

“I have spoken these things to you while remaining with you. [Col. 0341D] But the Paraclete, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things and remind you of everything I have said to you.

“Peace I leave you; my peace I give you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid. You heard that I said to you: ‘I am going away, and I am coming to you.’ If * you love me, you would certainly rejoice because I am going to the Father, for the Father is greater than I.

“And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it has happened you may believe. I will no longer speak many things with you, for the ruler of this world is coming, and he has nothing in me. But this is so that the world may know that I love the Father, and that I do just as the Father commanded me.”

## CHAPTER CLVIII. [Col. 0342A] He says to his disciples: “Whoever has anything, let him carry it.”

LUKE 22:35–38. And he said to them: “When I sent you without a money bag, a knapsack, or sandals, did you lack anything?” They said: “Nothing.”

Therefore he said to them: “But now, whoever has a money bag, let him take it; likewise a knapsack. And whoever does not have one, let him sell his tunic and buy a sword. * But I tell you that what is still [*quod, “what”] written must be fulfilled in me: ‘And [*quod, “that”] he was reckoned among the lawless’ (Isaiah 53:12). For the things concerning me are coming to an end.”

They said: “Lord, behold, here are two swords.” But he said to them: “It is enough.”

—JOHN 14:31. “Rise, let us go from here.”

—MATTHEW 26:30; LUKE 22:39. And after singing a hymn, they went out according to custom to the Mount of Olives, and his disciples followed [Col. 0342B] him.

## CHAPTER CLIX. Jesus says: “I am the vine, and you are the branches.”

JOHN 15:1–27. He said to them: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the cultivator. Every branch in me that does not bear fruit, he will remove; and every one that bears fruit, he will prune *, so that it may bear more fruit.

“Now you are clean because of the word that I have spoken to you. Remain in me, and I in you. Just as a branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you unless you remain in me. I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever remains in me, and I in him, bears much fruit, because without me you can do nothing.

“If anyone does not remain in me, he will be cast out like a branch and will wither; and they will gather him and cast him into the [Col. 0342C] fire, and he will * burn. If you remain in me, and my words remain in you, whatever you wish, ask, and it will be done for you.

“In this my Father is glorified: that you bear very much fruit and become my disciples. As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you. Remain in my love. If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father’s commandments and remain in his love.

“I have spoken these things to you so that my joy may be in you and your joy may be complete. This is my commandment: that you love one another as I have loved you. No one has greater love than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.

“You are my friends if you do what I command you. I will no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know what his master is doing. [Col. 0342D] But I have called you friends, because everything that I heard from my Father I have made known to you.

“You did not choose me, but I chose you; and I appointed you to go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in my name, he may give you. I command you these things: that you love one another.

“If the world hates you, know that it hated me before you. If you were of the world, the world would love what was its own. But because you are not of the world, and I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you.

“Remember my word that I said to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his master.’ If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they kept my word, they will also keep yours. But they will do all these things [Col. 0343A] to you because of my name, because they do not know the one who sent me.

“If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin. Whoever hates me also hates my Father. If I had not done among them works that no one else has done, they would not have sin; but now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father.

“But this is so that the word written in their law may be fulfilled: ‘They hated me without cause’ (Psalm 24:19).

“But when the Paraclete comes, whom I will send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father—he will bear witness concerning me. And you also will bear witness, because you have been with me from the beginning.”

—JOHN 16:1–33. “I have spoken these things to you so that you may not be scandalized. They will expel you from the synagogues. But the hour is coming when everyone [Col. 0343B] who kills you will think that he is offering service to God. And they will do these things to you because they have not known the Father or me.

“But I have spoken these things to you so that, when their hour comes, you may remember that I told you. I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you. * But now I am going to the one who sent me; and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’ But because I have spoken these things to you, sorrow has filled your heart.

“But I tell you the truth: it is expedient for you that I go. For if I do not go, the Paraclete will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you. And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment: concerning sin, indeed, because it does not * believe in me; concerning righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you will no longer see me; concerning judgment *, because the ruler of this [Col. 0343C] world has been * judged.

“I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. But when that Spirit of truth comes, he will teach you all truth. For he will not speak from himself; but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will announce to you the things that are to come. He will glorify me, because he will receive from what is mine and announce it to you. Everything that the Father has is mine. Therefore I said that he will receive from what is mine and announce it to you.

“A little while, and you will no longer see me; and again a little while, and you will see me, because I am going to the Father.”

Therefore his disciples said to one another: “What is this that he says to us: ‘A little while, and you will not see me, and again a little while, and you will see me, * because I am going to the Father’?” They were saying: “What is this that he says, ‘A little while’? We do not know what he is saying.”

But Jesus [Col. 0343D] knew that they wanted to question him, and he said to them: “Are you asking among yourselves about this, because I said: ‘A little while, and you will not see me, and again a little while, and you will see me’?

“Amen, amen, I say to you: you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice; you will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will turn into joy. When a woman gives birth, she has sorrow because her hour has come; but when she has borne the child, she no longer remembers her distress, because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world.

“And so you now indeed have sorrow; but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you. On that day you will not ask me anything. Amen, amen, I say to you: if you ask the Father anything in my name, [Col. 0344A] he will give it to you. Until now you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be full.

“I have spoken these things to you in figures. The hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in figures, but will announce the Father to you openly. On that day you will ask in my name. And I do not say to you that I will ask the Father for you; for the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came forth from God.

“I came forth from the Father and came into the world; again I leave the world and go to the Father.”

His disciples said to him: “Behold, now you are speaking openly and saying no figure. Now we know that you know all things, and there is no need for anyone to question you. By this we believe that you came forth from God.”

Jesus answered them: “Do you now believe? Behold, the hour is coming—and has already come—when you will be scattered, each [Col. 0344B] one to his own, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.

“I have spoken these things to you so that you may have peace in me. In the world you will have distress; but take courage: I have conquered the world.”

—JOHN 17:1–26. Jesus spoke these things, and lifting his eyes toward heaven, he said: “Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son, so that your Son may glorify you, just as you gave him authority over all flesh, so that he may give eternal life to all whom you have given him.

“Now this is eternal life: that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent. I glorified you on earth; I completed the work that you gave me to do. And now glorify me, Father, with yourself, with the glory that I had with you before the world existed.

“I manifested your name to the human beings whom you gave me [Col. 0344C] from the world. They were yours, and you gave them to me; and they have kept your word. Now they know that everything you gave me is from you, because the words that you gave me I have given to them; and they received them and truly understood that I came forth from you, and they believed that you sent me.

“I pray for them; I do not pray for the world *, but for those whom you gave me, because they are yours. And all mine are yours, and yours are mine, and I have been glorified in them.

“And now I am no longer in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming [Col. 0344D] to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name, whom you have given me, so that they may be one, just as we are * one. When I was with them, I kept them in your name. Those whom you gave me I guarded, and none of them perished except the son of perdition, so that Scripture (Psalm 108:8) might be fulfilled.

“But now I am coming to you, and I speak these things in the world so that they may have my joy fulfilled in themselves. I have given them your word, and the world has hated them, because they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.

“I do not ask that you take them out of the world, but that you preserve them from evil. They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world. Sanctify them in truth. Your word is truth. As you sent me into the world, so I also sent them into the world; and for them I sanctify myself, so that they too may be sanctified in truth.

“I pray not only for these, but also for those who will believe in me through their word, so that all may be one, just as you, Father, are in me and I in you, so that they too may be one in us, so that the world may believe that you sent me. [Col. 0345A]

“And I have given them the glory that you gave me, so that they may be one, just as we are one. I in them and you in me, so that they may be perfected in unity, and the world may know that you sent * me and loved them as you loved me.

“Father, those whom you gave me, I desire that where I am, they also may be with me, so that they may see my glory, which you gave me, because you loved me before the foundation of the world.

“Righteous Father, the world has not known you, but I have known you; and these have known that you sent me. And I made your name known to them, and I will make it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.”

## CHAPTER CLX. Jesus comes to Gethsemane and prays to the Father that this cup be taken from him.

[Col. 0345B] MATTHEW 26:36–46. MARK 14:32–42. LUKE 22:39–46. Then Jesus came with them to a village called Gethsemane.—JOHN 18:1–2. Across the torrent of Cedron, where there was a garden into which he entered, he and his disciples. Judas, who betrayed him, also knew the place, because Jesus had often gathered there with his disciples.

And when he had reached the place, he said to his disciples: “Sit here and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation, while I go there and pray.” And taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, James and John, he began to be sorrowful and deeply distressed. Then he said to them: “My soul is sorrowful even to death; remain here and keep watch with me.”

And he went forward from them about a stone’s throw. And kneeling, he fell upon his face and prayed that, if it could [Col. 0345C] be, the hour might pass from him, saying: “Father, if it is possible—Abba, Father, all things are possible for you—my Father, if it is possible, take this cup from me; nevertheless, not what I will, but what you will.”

And when he had risen from prayer, he came to his disciples and found them sleeping. And he said to them: “Why are you sleeping? Were you not able to keep watch with me for one hour? Keep watch and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

Again, a second time, he went away and prayed.

—LUKE 22:43–45. And an angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him. And being in agony, he prayed more earnestly, saying: “My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, let your will be done.” And his sweat became like drops of blood flowing down upon the ground.

And when he had risen [Col. 0345D] from prayer, he came again to his disciples and found them sleeping from sorrow.

—MARK 14:40. For their eyes were heavy, and they did not know what to answer him.

And leaving them, he went away again and prayed a third time, saying the same words. Then he came to his disciples and said to them: “Sleep now and rest. Behold, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man will be handed over into the hands of sinners. Rise, let us go. Behold, the one who betrays me has drawn near.”

## CHAPTER CLXI. Judas comes with a crowd to seize Jesus.

MATTHEW 26:47–56; MARK 14:43–50; LUKE 22:47–54. While he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of [Col. 0346A] the Twelve, having taken a cohort, came, and with him a great crowd with lanterns, torches, weapons, swords, and clubs, sent by the chief priests, scribes, and elders of the people.

Now the one who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying: “Whomever I kiss, he is the one; seize him and lead him away carefully.” And immediately approaching Jesus, he said: “Hail, Rabbi,” and he drew near to Jesus to kiss him.

But Jesus said to him: “Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss? Friend, why have you come?” And he kissed him.

—JOHN 18:4–9. Therefore Jesus, knowing everything that was about to happen to him, went forward and said to them: “Whom are you seeking?”

They answered him: “Jesus the Nazarene.”

* Jesus said: “I am he.” And Judas, who betrayed him, was also standing with them. Therefore, when he said to them, “I am he,” they went backward and [Col. 0346B] fell to the ground.

Again, therefore, he asked them: “Whom are you seeking?”

They said: “Jesus the Nazarene.”

Jesus answered: “I told you that I am he. Therefore, if you are seeking me, let these men go,” so that the word might be fulfilled that he had spoken: “Of those whom you gave me, I have not lost any” (John 17:12).
