The Apostle praises them highly, writing to them from Athens through Tychicus the deacon and Onesimus the acolyte.

## Chapter One

Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians. Through Silvanus and Timothy, the word of God had been proclaimed not only to these people but also to the Corinthians together with the Apostle, as he himself says in the second Epistle: “By me, and Silvanus, and Timothy.”

In God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, grace to you and peace. He places the words in an inverted order, saying first “in God the Father and Christ Jesus,” and then “grace to you and peace.”

We give thanks to God always for all of you, making mention of you. “For all,” because the memory of all of you is pleasing to us.

In our prayers without ceasing. Do not allow yourselves to be hindered from praying always.

Remembering your work of faith and labor of love. Not faith alone, nor labor and love in word alone, but in deed.

And the steadfastness of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ. Every steadfastness is for the sake of hope.

Before our God and Father. Not before human beings.

Knowing, beloved brothers, your election by God. We know from this that you have truly been chosen by God: because you are genuine.

It should be noted that they are said to have been chosen rather than to have chosen.

Because our Gospel did not come to you in word only. For it is not merely heard; it also appeared in action.

But also in power and in the Holy Spirit. Whom you received.

And in great fullness. Of your perfection, or of our abundance.

Just as you know what kind of people we were among you for your sake. We even abstained from things that were permitted.

And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, receiving the word. Receiving the word through suffering, just as we and the Lord preached it.

In much tribulation. Something scarcely received in tranquillity.

With joy of the Holy Spirit. This is truly to rejoice in the Holy Spirit, like the apostles, who went away rejoicing because they had been considered worthy to suffer dishonor [Col. 0639D] for the name of Christ.

So that you became an example to all believers in Macedonia and Achaia. It belongs to the perfect to offer an example to believers; by your example everyone was stirred up.

For from you the word of God has been proclaimed. The nature of reputation is such that, whether it announces good or evil, it travels everywhere.

Not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but in every place. Thessalonica lies almost on their borders.

Your faith in God has gone forth. It has turned from idols to the Lord.

So that we do not need to say anything. Thus, when we begin to say anything about you for their edification, they themselves declare that they know it very well.

For they themselves report concerning us what kind of entrance we had [Col. 0640A] among you. The reputation both of our steadfastness and of your manner of life is known to everyone.

And how you turned to God from idols, to serve the living and true God and to await his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, Jesus. It should be noted that people are said to have turned to the Lord from idols; but believers are also often said in the prophets to need to turn from wickedness to faith in God.

Who delivered us from the coming wrath. By his grace and mercy he delivered us from the wrath of judgment [Col. 0640B], because we already possess, in hope, the freedom to be restored through baptism.

## Chapter Two

For you yourselves know, brothers, our entrance among you: it was not empty, but we first suffered and were treated shamefully. A word confirmed by the steadfastness of suffering is not empty.

As you know, at Philippi we had confidence in our Lord to speak the Gospel of God to you. Some of you saw that, although we suffered at Philippi, we were not afraid of tribulations and did not cease preaching.

With much earnest concern. Not negligently or superficially.

For our exhortation. Therefore we are not terrified.

Not from error. Anyone who thinks or teaches that the wicked reign with Christ is in error: “Do not err: neither fornicators nor adulterers,” and so forth.

Nor from impurity. Such as the teaching of Jovinianus.

Nor [Col. 0640C] in deceit. Speaking and persuading against conscience.

But just as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the Gospel, so we speak. We speak with integrity, as people approved by God, who knows the minds of all and has appointed us to this office.

Not as pleasing human beings, but God, who tests our hearts. Human beings can be deceived.

For neither at any time did we use a speech of flattery, as you know; nor an occasion for greed—God is witness—nor did we seek glory from human beings, either from you or from others. Those who please human beings grant the weak everything they desire and have no concern for their death. Everyone who flatters does so either for greed or for glory. Therefore the person is proved to speak for God who does not seek these things.

Although we could have been a burden as apostles of Christ. Although we could have burdened you with what God ordained for us.

But we became little children among you. Humbling ourselves and not seeking the honor due to us.

As if a nurse were cherishing her own children. She humbles herself and makes herself equal to the little child in everything, so that she may lead it to greater things by her example. Thus she even babbles in its language, eats little, and walks slowly with it, so that it may become accustomed.

So, longing for you, we eagerly desired to impart to you. That you might progress.

Not only the Gospel of God but also our own lives. Just as a nurse wishes to pour the sense of her perfection into the child, so that it may become like her.

Because you had become very dear to us. On account of your faith.

For you remember, brothers, our labor [Col. 0641A]. He worked with his hands at night, and with the word by day. For if he was always working, when did he teach?

And our toil, working night and day. Among these people, and among the Corinthians and Ephesians, he labored, wishing to remove from them any opportunity either to receive from him or to disparage him.

So that we would not burden any of you, we preached the Gospel of God among you. This refers to what he said above: although we could have been a burden.

You are witnesses, and God also, of how holy, just, and blameless we were. We did not give you any occasion for offense.

To you who believed, we were present. Not to unbelievers.

As you know how we exhorted each one of you, as a father does his children. He instructs the little one as a nurse, but the one who is already progressing as a father.

And comforting and testifying, we admonished you. In tribulation we comforted you with the promises [Col. 0641B] of Christ.

So that you might walk worthily of God. The person walks worthily of God who does nothing unworthy of God.

Who called you into his own kingdom and glory. This will be possessed only by believers, to whom it is said, “Come, blessed ones.”

For this reason we also give thanks to God without ceasing: because, when you received from us the word of the hearing of God. That is, the first thing you heard concerning God, or so that you might hear God.

You received it not as the word of human beings but, as it truly is, the word of God. Whoever despises it treats it as a human word; but you believed in such a way that you thought you were hearing from God himself.

Who works in you who believe. He works through inspiration, or through signs; and if you do anything good, he does it in you.

Observe that he says “in you,” not “with you,” so that glory may always be given to God, to whom belongs everything we can do, and who works in us [Col. 0641C] so that we may work, as Isaiah says in his song: “Lord our God, you will give us peace, and you have performed all our works in us.”

For you became imitators of the churches of God that are in Judea in Christ Jesus. Of whom he says: “For you even showed sympathy to those in chains and accepted with joy the seizure of your possessions.”

For you also suffered the same things. I marvel at you all the more, because you were neither instructed in the law nor stirred up by the examples of the prophets.

From your fellow citizens, just as they suffered from the Jews. “Fellow citizens” means people of the same nation.

Who killed both the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and persecuted us; they do not please God. What wonder if they persecute us, when they killed both God and the prophets?

And are hostile to all people, forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles so that they may not be saved. [Col. 0641D] Not only to their own people.

Thus they always fill up their sins. For they not only hinder the Jews but also begrudge the Gentiles, adding to the accumulation of their sins.

But the wrath of God has come upon them to the end. Either because understanding has been taken away from those who do not believe, or because punishment came prematurely upon them, and they were taken captive and scattered throughout the whole earth.

But we, brothers, having been separated from you for a time, in presence though not in heart, hastened all the more eagerly to see your face, with great desire, because we wanted to come to you.

As he says elsewhere: “Absent in body but present in spirit, I have already judged.” I, Paul, intended to come once and again, but Satan hindered us.

This means the tribulations of persecutors or the weaknesses of the infirm, not his own power.

For what is our hope [Col. 0642A], or joy, or crown of glory? Are you not this before our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming? For you are our glory and joy. Good teachers place all their hope, joy, and crown in the perfection of their students.

## Chapter Three

Therefore, when we could no longer endure it. We could no longer bear that none of us should come to you and comfort you concerning us; and for this reason we were tormented with anxiety.

We decided to remain alone in Athens. We preferred to remain alone rather than not know what you were doing.

And we sent Timothy our brother. How could he have written at the same time if he had been sent? Here he first relates what happened and then recapitulates it.

And a minister of God in the Gospel of Christ. Assistants are also commonly called ministers for disciples.

To strengthen you and exhort you concerning your faith. Since you have already received faith, you need only to be strengthened.

So that no one may be shaken by these tribulations. He does not mean everyone, but so that at least no one may be shaken.

For you yourselves know. Therefore you should neither be shaken nor surprised, knowing that we cannot pass through any other way.

That we have been appointed to this. By Christ, who said: “Behold, I am sending you like lambs among wolves,” and many other things.

For even when we were with you, we foretold to you that we would suffer tribulations, just as it happened—and you know it. For this reason, since I could no longer endure it, I sent him to learn about your faith.

So that the novelty of the event would not terrify you, but our prophecy would strengthen you; hence the Savior also foretold his own passion beforehand.

Lest the tempter should have tested you. Lest the tempter should say to you, “Behold, those in whom you hope that God is present cannot be delivered from tribulations,” and perhaps disturb your faith.

The one who tempts. He also tempted God.

And our labor should become fruitless. If through this suggestion he had implanted a scruple in you.

But now that Timothy has come to us from you and announced your faith. That you firmly believe in Christ.

And your love. Because you love us more than usual.

And that you have a good memory of us. For there is also a bad memory.

Always desiring to see us, just as we also desire to see you. Firmly.

Therefore we have been comforted, brothers, by you, in all our necessity and tribulation, through your faith. Because of the greatness of the joy produced by your steadfastness, we feel neither our necessity nor our tribulation.

For now we live, if you stand firm in the Lord. Even if we are killed, our life depends on you.

For what thanksgiving can we render to God for you, in all the joy with which we rejoice because of you before our Lord, night and day [Col. 0642D]? Your manner of life gives us a threefold reason for joy: you are progressing, the Lord is glorified through you, and you provide an example to others.

Praying more earnestly that we may see your face. He shows how much he ought to be desired by those brothers whom he himself desires so greatly. For who, upon hearing about someone’s reputation, does not wish to see him?

And complete what is lacking in your faith. If your faith lacks something in teaching: when what was lacking is completed, what was already present is not rejected; what was deficient is added, not what existed removed. He knew that they possessed right faith because they had Christ as their foundation; therefore something is added to the building, not taken away from the foundation.

Now may God himself, our Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ direct our way to you. Removing the diabolical obstacles and temptations by which our coming is hindered.

And may the Lord multiply you and make your love abound for one another. May he multiply it in the number of believers, or in faith and knowledge. It should be noted that the Lord does this, and that human frailty does not act without God.

And toward all, just as we also are toward you, so that he may strengthen your hearts without blame. So that you may love not only Christians but also people of every sect—not on account of their error, but on account of their nature—and not deny them the mercy that God presently shows them wherever they are in need.

For you to do all these things, what he said above must be understood: “May the Lord multiply you and make you abound in love,” because it is his gift that we act, just as it is his gift that we love.

In holiness before our God and Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints. Amen. Not before human beings.

## Chapter Four

Finally, therefore, brothers, we ask and exhort you in the Lord Jesus that, just as you received from us how you ought to walk and please God. You, for whom Christ is the way, walk along it with worthy steps: namely, in gentleness, love, peace, and other similar qualities.

So walk that you may abound still more. For you know what commandments I gave you through the Lord Jesus. As you advance in age and faith, you ought also to increase in progress and conduct, just as food and desire increase with the growth of the body.

For this is the will of God, your sanctification. Sanctification restrains the Christian from all lack of self-control; when Moses wished to sanctify the people, he commanded them to abstain from every woman, so that they might be worthy to receive God’s law.

That you abstain from fornication, so that each one of you may know. It should be considered that he does not write to them as he does to the Corinthians.

How to possess his own vessel in honor and sanctification. Let each person sanctify and honor his own body by keeping it chaste; or, at least, let him know his wife only for the sake of children.

Not in the passion of desire, like the Gentiles who do not know God. Do not fornicate outside lawful marriage.

And that no one transgress. The resolution of continence.

Nor defraud his brother in business. Let no one, after continence has been devotedly undertaken by mutual consent, violate his partner through some deception; or let fraud be committed in any business matter.

For the Lord is an avenger in all these things. Not only in fornication but also in the violation of a resolution, because by stirring themselves up they made illicit what had been lawful.

As we foretold and testified to you. For if he had preached chastity to the Corinthians, he had preached it all the more to these people.

For God did not call us to impurity. Excessive lack of restraint within marriage may be counted as impurity, because the body of Christ does not permit one to receive it.

But to sanctification. So that you may live according to Christ’s example.

Therefore whoever rejects these things rejects not a human being but God. He does not reject my words but the one who speaks through me; whoever despises them insults his Spirit.

Who also gave his holy Spirit in us [Col. 0644A]. He dwells only in holy people.

Concerning brotherly love, we have no need to write to you. For you yourselves have been taught by God to love one another, and indeed you do this.

Because of Christ, who said: “I give you a new commandment, that you love one another.” “New” means that we should die for one another, because the Old Testament had not commanded this.

Toward all the brothers throughout Macedonia. Without distinction of persons.

But we ask you, brothers, to abound and to make every effort. Even toward strangers or enemies, who are also to be loved.

To be quiet, to attend to your own business, and to work with your hands, as we commanded you. He recalls some people from unnecessary and worldly business dealings, which, as far as can be understood, they were undertaking for profit. It is therefore much more just to seek one’s livelihood with one’s own hands [Col. 0644B] than to become entangled in such matters and, through them, hope for some benefit from outsiders, thereby harming someone instead of helping others.

Some think that he is not reproving the office of a teacher but the vice of the nation; finally, in the second Epistle he says to them: “If anyone does not wish to work, neither should he eat.”

And to walk honorably before those who are outside, and to desire nothing belonging to anyone. So that those who seem to provide for you may not themselves condemn you.

We do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, concerning those who sleep, so that you may not grieve. The Savior said that Lazarus was sleeping, whom he knew would rise. The same applies to the others. One thing should be done by someone who travels abroad, another by someone who dies.

Who have no hope. Of future things.

For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again. If we believe this, which we equally do not see, and through his resurrection are certain that we have received forgiveness, why should we not similarly believe what the Gentiles do not believe because they do not see it?

So also God will bring with Jesus those who have fallen asleep. The one who raised the head promised to raise the remaining members also.

For this we say to you by the word of the Lord. Not by our own word.

That we who live, who remain. The sentence concerning the Gospel is left suspended, and he continually makes them regard the day of the Lord with apprehension, as though that day itself would find them in the body.

At the coming of our Lord, we will not precede those who have fallen asleep. Their resurrection will be as swift as our being taken up.

For the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a command and with the voice of an archangel. Terrible. Elijah saw the terrible coming of God [Col. 0644D].

And with the trumpet of God. And the dead who are in Christ. Not human beings generally.

Will rise first. Before those who died outside Christ.

Then we who live, who remain, will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. Sinful dead together with those who are found alive will rise for punishment and be dissolved by fire; and the righteous living, changed and made incorruptible, will in an instant be caught up with the righteous who are rising to glory. They will not be judged but will judge.

And so we shall always be with the Lord. In the same glory. We shall be wherever he is.

Therefore comfort one another. It should be noted that he says that laypeople ought to comfort one another.

With these words. So that you may not grieve.

## Chapter Five

Concerning the times and moments, brothers, [Col. 0645A] you have no need for us to write to you, for you yourselves know carefully. Clearly from the Gospel reading.

For the day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night. When it finds everyone sleeping securely.

For when they say, “Peace and security,” then sudden destruction comes upon them. It is most to be feared when no one fears it.

Like labor upon a pregnant woman. That is, childbirth.

And they will not escape. Just as a woman will not escape childbirth when the pains come upon her.

But you, brothers, are not in darkness. You are not in ignorance, because you know that you must always be prepared.

So that day may seize you like a thief. While you sleep the sleep of idleness.

For you are all sons of light and sons of day. He himself is light, and the day is knowledge and action.

We are not of night or of darkness. Just as darkness gives confidence to sin, so ignorance gives confidence to wrongdoing [Col. 0645B].

Therefore let us not sleep. In the mind.

As the others do. Who are like this.

But let us watch and be sober. Pay attention to yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down by overeating, drunkenness, and the cares of this life; cares also intoxicate.

For those who sleep. Therefore the others too are idle, because they are in darkness.

He continues the comparison. They sleep at night—in sins—and those who are drunk are drunk at night, that is, with sins.

But we who belong to the day. We who possess the day must be neither idle nor drunk.

Let us be sober. From every sin.

Having put on the breastplate of faith and love, and the helmet of the hope of salvation. Clothed with the garment of the justice of faith and love, which elsewhere he compared to a breastplate.

For God has not appointed us to wrath. That is, to destruction. Unbelievers are appointed to wrath, since they have already been judged.

But to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ. So that we may acquire salvation.

Who died for us. For whether we die or live, whether in the body or outside the body, we always live with him.

So that whether we watch or sleep, we may live together with him. Through good works.

Therefore comfort one another and build one another up, as indeed you are doing. Just as the person who builds is blessed, so the person who destroys is miserable.

But we ask you, brothers. It should be noted that he says this to laypeople, whom he admonishes to show the presbyters the duties of love.

To recognize those who labor among you. To understand their labor.

And preside over you in the Lord. According to the example of the Lord, not with earthly power; for a good teacher cannot teach or preside over others without labor.

And admonish you to hold them in even greater love. Presbyters who labor in the word are worthy of double honor, both that of love and that of office.

Because of their work; and be at peace with them. So that, when they are corrected by the priests for some reason, they may not become enemies and ungrateful.

But we ask you, brothers. He gives this command to the priests.

Correct the unruly. Different illnesses require different medicines. [Col. 0646A] Here he speaks to the presbyters; up to this point he was speaking to the people.

Comfort the fainthearted. Those who, when provoked, become discouraged.

Support the weak. Sustain those who have recently come to faith, because they are not yet firm in faith.

Be patient with everyone. Even with those who are being corrected. Whoever lacks patience does not correct but provokes.

See that no one repays anyone evil for evil. With every diligence and caution. He fears that they may repay evil whom he had thought unable to do so; now he states this generally.

But always pursue what is good for one another. Repay evil with good.

And toward everyone. Not only toward one another but also toward all people.

Rejoice always. “As sorrowful, yet always rejoicing,” that is, in hope of the future life.

Pray without ceasing. In the heart, just as it is said to Moses when he was silent, “Why do you cry out to me?”

Give thanks in everything. [Col. 0646B] In everything that happens; as with blessed Job, in all your actions let thanks be given to the Lord.

For this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you all. Just as it was fulfilled in him in every respect, so may it be fulfilled in all of you.

Do not extinguish the Spirit. Do not extinguish the Spirit who exhorts through objections and questions. It is extinguished by evil works—that is, the work of the Holy Spirit—for whatever we do under his inspiration, he does; he is the author of good work, just as the devil is the author of evil.

Do not despise prophecies. Whether they proclaim future things or explain past things, test only whether what is said is contrary to the faith; and if anything of that kind is found, reject it.

Test everything; hold fast to what is good; abstain from every appearance of evil. For there are many forms of evil.

Now may the God of peace [Col. 0646C]. He who sustains everyone, even those who blaspheme.

Sanctify you. Protecting you through continual guardianship; and those whom he justified, he also sanctified.

In every respect. So that you may be perfect in all things.

And may your spirit be whole. The grace of the spirit, whatever it may be in itself, is not whole unless it is guarded by whole people. The spirit is often understood as the rational mind itself, in which there is something like the eye of the soul; to this belong the image and recognition of God. At times “spirit” is understood as spiritual understanding.

And your soul. In thought.

And may your body be blameless. In deed.

Be preserved at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. He is faithful who called you. He said: “Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened, and I will give you rest.”

Who will also do this. So that you may persevere. He promised this when he said: [Col. 0646D] “Behold, I am with you until the consummation.”

Brothers, pray for us.

Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.

I adjure you by the Lord that this Epistle be read. To adjure is permitted; to swear an oath is not permitted.

To all the holy brothers.

The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.

We may understand “holy” to mean baptized.

# The Second Epistle to the Thessalonians

[Col. 0645]

## Chapter One

[Col. 0645D]

# The Second Epistle to the Thessalonians

## Chapter One

Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

They are holy—that is, the Church and all the baptized faithful.

We ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers, as is fitting, because he has made you such a people, and has formed such a Church from you, preparing you by the gift of mercy, so that you do not yield to such great tribulations. For your faith is growing exceedingly, and the love of each one of you for the others is increasing.

At first he believed through God’s gift; now faith is growing, and therefore praise also increases. It was right that, as their faith and love increased, his praise should likewise increase. At the same time, he foretells to them that certain people would attempt by this new argument to turn them away from the faith: they would say that Christ was soon to come, and would introduce whomever they wished in Christ’s place in order to persuade them.

Thus we ourselves boast of you in the churches of God, because of your patience and faith in all your persecutions and tribulations, which you endure. For unless you believed that these things would come about through God’s gift, you would by no means endure them.

But we give thanks to God, whose work it is that you are able to endure, as an example of God’s just judgment. You thereby provide an example of waiting for God’s just judgment, since you believe that he has come in this way.

So that you may be considered worthy of the kingdom of God. Those are worthy of the kingdom of God who, knowing its glory, consider no suffering worthy of comparison with it. For its sake you also suffer.

Unless, indeed, it is just before God to repay tribulation to those who trouble you. Here, if the phrase belongs to one who is taunting rather than doubting, the sense is: “If the source of justice can judge what is just.”

And to you who are troubled, rest with us at the revelation of the Lord from heaven, because you suffer with us, with the angels of his power, who will take vengeance.

He will give vengeance in flaming fire to those who do not know God. If the flame could touch none of the three boys, why should it not be believed that the same flame is harsher toward some and gentler toward others?

And to those who do not obey the Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ—not only to those who did not know God, but also to those who do not obey the Gospel’s instructions.

They will suffer eternal punishment leading to destruction. Punishment cannot be called eternal without someone enduring it.

They will suffer it from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of his power, from whose sight they will receive their sentence.

When he comes to be glorified in his saints. He himself will be glorified in his members, who will shine with the sun’s brilliance. Or, “he will be glorified” when he displays what he promised.

And to become marvelous in all who have believed. For the ungodly will marvel at the exaltation of the righteous, inspired by salvation [reading uncertain].

Because our testimony concerning you was believed on that day. For many of you believed our testimony concerning that day.

On account of this we also always pray for you, that our God may deem you worthy of his calling, so that you may be found worthy of what you have been called to; for those whom he called, he also justified. Certainly he was speaking here already to the baptized.

And may he fulfill every good purpose and the work of faith in power: through the daily assistance of grace and knowledge, and through the consolation of the virtues that are necessary for the work of faith.

So that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and you in him: so that Christ’s name may be renowned in your deeds, and you may be glorious in his signs and virtues.

According to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ—not according to our power, but according to God’s grace.

Consider carefully that he said “according to the grace of God,” not “according to our merits,” so that human presumption may claim nothing for itself and attribute nothing to its own merits.

## Chapter Two

We ask you, brothers, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ—which is dearer to you than anything else, as holy people—and by our gathering to him, when the elect will be gathered from the four winds of heaven, not to be quickly shaken from your understanding.

Not rashly, but rationally, according to the clearest teaching of the Gospel concerning that day. Whoever believes that it will come quickly is lighthearted and will be diminished.

Nor should you be terrified by a spirit. Let not signs terrify you that will be performed through a spirit transformed into a holy one, since the Savior also foretold this beforehand.

Nor by a word—that is, by dialectical fallacies or rhetorical persuasion.

Nor by a letter. For the devil’s cunning could also have devised this, as appears in many apocryphal writings, which are given the title of the apostles in order to establish unbelief as faith.

As though sent by us—that is, bearing a title in our name.

As though the day of the Lord were imminent—the day of judgment.

Let no one deceive you in any way, saying, “Behold, Christ is here,” or, “He is there.”

For unless he has come—unless the Antichrist has come—Christ will not come, because he himself promised this.

The apostasy first: from the truth or from his own principality; or else the withdrawal of the nations from the Roman Empire, as is shown in Daniel through the figure of the beast and the image. The devil is not improperly called “the apostasy,” because he withdrew from God.

And the man of sin is revealed—that is, the devil, who, according to the prophet Isaiah, disturbs the nations, and so forth—

The son of perdition, who opposes and exalts himself. For he will welcome him as though he had been born for him.

Above everything called God or everything worshiped, so that he sits in the temple of God, displaying himself as though he were God.

He will boast himself above eternity and omnipotence, and will claim that he is increasing the mysteries of worship. For he will also restore the temple at Jerusalem and reestablish all the ceremonial observances of the Law, solely in order to dissolve the Gospel of Christ. This will persuade the wretched Jews to receive him as Christ, although he comes in his own name and not in God’s.

Do you not remember that, when we were with you, we used to tell you these things?

“What is called God” is the Church; but “what is worshiped” is the supreme God. “So that he sits in the temple of God, displaying himself as though he were God”—that is, as though he himself were the Church. It would be like saying, “Let him sit in the temple of God, displaying himself as though he himself were God’s temple,” or, “Let him sit in God, displaying himself as though he himself were God.” This is from the Rules of Tyconius.

And now you know what restrains him: the coming of the Antichrist, so that he may be revealed in his own time—the same Antichrist.

For the mystery of iniquity is already at work in his Antichrist’s forerunners, who have gone out into the world.

Only let the one who now restrains continue to restrain—that is, the empire—until he is removed from the midst. The Roman kingdom will first be removed from the midst before the Antichrist is revealed.

And then that lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of his mouth and destroy by the manifestation of his coming, because he will flash like lightning in the world.

He whose coming is according to the activity of Satan. False prophets and false Christs will arise and give great signs, so that, if possible, even the elect may be led into error.

With every power, signs, and lying wonders—in appearance—and with every deceit of iniquity.

For there is also a deceit of truth.

For those who are perishing, because they did not receive the love of the truth so as to be saved. Those who did not love the truth will love vanity.

Therefore God will send them an activity of error, so that they may believe the lie. He permits it by abandoning them. For if God sends it, how can his coming be the activity of Satan?

So that all who did not believe may be judged; so that they may not excuse themselves for failing to believe the divine powers because of the obscurity of Christ’s incarnation, when they believed the devil deceiving them by human artifice, since he will appear in human form.

They did not believe the truth, Christ, but consented to iniquity, the Antichrist.

But we ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers beloved by God, because we have received the love of the truth and therefore are loved by God.

Because God chose you: he made you ready to believe, just as it was revealed to one who desired to go elsewhere through a vision of a Macedonian man.

As firstfruits for salvation, in sanctification of the spirit and faith in the truth, in which he also called you through our Gospel. For he made us believe first, before the nations.

For the acquisition of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ. You have been called for this purpose, so that you may acquire Christ’s glory; and we know that, when he appears, we shall be like him. Or this refers to God’s glory, since the number of believers increases.

Therefore, brothers, stand firm and hold fast to these things in faith, truth, and sanctification of the spirit:

the traditions. When he wants his own traditions to be held, he does not want others to be added to them,

which you learned either by word or by our letter: concerning the sacrament of baptism and the other practices observed throughout the world and thereby approved as apostolic.

Now may our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who has given us all these things—against the Arians, who think that the one named first is greater; here, behold, the Son is named first—

who loved us, although we were impious and did not deserve it,

and gave us eternal consolation: the promises, or else the consoling Spirit, that is, the Paraclete,

and good hope by grace—for there is also a bad hope—

comfort your hearts through virtues or revelation,

and strengthen you in every work. “Strengthen me in your words,” because if he does not strengthen, human salvation is vain,

and in a good word—not only in deed.

## Chapter Three

Finally, brothers, pray for us, as he prayed for Peter; he both gives an example of humility and provides an occasion for love, so that we may pray for one another.

That the word of the Lord may run and be glorified, as it is also among you. Let it run with abundance; let it be magnified by the progress of its hearers.

And that we may be delivered from unreasonable and evil people—those who contradict and persecute.

For not everyone has faith. Not everyone proclaims God’s Gospel purely.

But God is faithful, who will strengthen you. He will not abandon you unless you abandon him,

and will guard you from evil—from the temptations of diabolical assault.

But we have confidence in the Lord concerning you, that you are doing and will do what we commanded.

Now may the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God, by continually inspiring, governing, and assisting you, and by revealing how great are the things he has promised either to the good or to the evil.

It should also be noted that here he called the Lord the Holy Spirit; against the Arians, the Spirit is named first here. Therefore we rightly understand “Lord” here as the Holy Spirit, who will direct the hearts of the faithful into the love of God and the patience of Christ.

And into the patience of Christ, so that you may understand that you suffer nothing new for your sake which he did not first endure for your sake.

Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. In the first letter we admonished you more gently; since they were unwilling to correct themselves, let them at least be ashamed now.

Withdraw yourselves from every brother who walks disorderly. It should be noted that one is to withdraw from a Christian who does not live according to the apostolic commands,

and not according to the tradition that they received from us—dishonorably.

For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we were not disorderly among you. We were a model for believers.

Nor did we eat bread from anyone without paying, but worked in labor and weariness, night and day, so as not to burden any of you.

Behold their tradition: not as though we had no authority. For the Lord says, “The laborer is worthy of his wage.”

But we did this to give you ourselves as a model, so that you might imitate us, and so that we might provide no one with an occasion for avarice or, at any rate, fuel for disorder.

For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: we saw that some would become such people.

For if anyone does not wish to work, neither should he eat. Let this be so that they either sit quietly, or, if they are true apostles, follow us—if they walk for God’s sake and not for avarice.

We hear that some among you are walking disorderly, doing no work. They do not sit quietly, but busy themselves inquisitively, investigating what is happening in each province or city.

Now to such people we command and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ—not ceasing to admonish them even after a second correction—

that, working quietly, they should eat their own bread, with calm and tranquility, so that they do not even work in a disorderly fashion.

But you, brothers, do not grow weary in doing good.

If anyone does not obey our word through this letter, take note of that person and do not associate with him. I do not forbid giving to everyone; rather, the prohibition applies only to such people, so that you do not think I am abolishing the practice of doing good.

Let him be put to shame. And do not regard him as an enemy—not so that he may be utterly cut off,

but correct him as a brother. Correct him so that he may amend his ways; do not reject him, lest he despair. The sick person must be healed, not killed, lest the disorderly person become an apostate.

Now may the God of peace himself give you everlasting peace, so that you may all attend to things peacefully, in every place.

The Lord be with all of you, and in every place, wherever you may be.

The greeting is by the hand of Paul. This is the sign in every letter: “Thus I write,” so that you may know how to recognize false letters.

The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you. Amen.

With these words he subscribed all his letters, except that to the Galatians, which he wrote entirely in his own hand, so that afterward they would not accept even a letter addressed to themselves unless it had been written in his own hand.

# The Epistle of Paul to the Colossians

## Argument

The Colossians, like the Laodiceans, are Asians. They too had been forestalled by false apostles, and the Apostle himself did not visit them; nevertheless, he corrects them through this letter as well.

For they had heard the word from Archippus, who had also received ministry among them. Therefore the Apostle, already imprisoned, writes to them from Ephesus.

First he praises them for having heard of their great faith. Then he warns them not to be led astray by philosophy or by the ceremonial observances of the Law.

## Chapter One

Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy the brother—not by my merits, but by God’s will—

to those who are at Colossae, that is, to the Church,

holy and faithful brothers in Christ Jesus—not in the flesh.

Grace to you and peace from God our Father.

We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, always praying for you, because of your faith in Christ Jesus.

It should be noted that he always puts grace first, by which we are saved without any merits of our own,

and because of the love that you have for all the saints. Without exception in knowledge or person, you love holiness alone in everyone.

Because of the hope laid up for you—not so that you may be seen as holy by human beings—

in heaven, which you heard in the word of the truth of the Gospel, which has reached you: the word of eternal life.

As it is also in the whole world, it is bearing fruit. One bears thirtyfold, another sixtyfold, another a hundredfold.

And it is growing, as it is also among you, in the number of believers,

from the day on which you heard and came to know the grace of God in truth.

That person knows God’s grace in truth who is not ungrateful for God’s grace, who attributes nothing to his own merits but gives glory to him whose gift is everything he possesses.

As you learned from Epaphras, our most beloved fellow servant, who had explained to them that everything they could do belonged to God,

who is a faithful minister of Christ Jesus on your behalf, faithfully laboring in prayer for you and ministering according to Christ’s will,

who also made known to us your love in the spirit—the love you possess in spiritual matters.

For this reason, from the day on which we heard, we have not ceased praying and asking for you, that you may be filled with knowledge of his will, since you cannot do it otherwise.

Understanding this, the prophet said to the Lord: “Teach me to do your will, because you are my God.”

In all wisdom—that is, the wisdom of God’s Law—

and spiritual understanding, which makes both the one who understands and the one who hears spiritual.

So that you may walk worthily. He explained why he said this: how God gives the will, helps, and strengthens by inspiring and teaching wisdom, and by giving understanding through his grace; restoring and strengthening free choice by his daily grace.

Thus in the present passage he prays that they may be filled with knowledge of God’s will, in all wisdom by which they may walk worthily before God in every respect.

Worthy of God, pleasing him in every way, bearing fruit in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God.

One walks worthily of God who pleases him in every respect—that is, in every good work—so that the knowledge of God and its fruit may increase.

In all power. Power consists in overcoming the weakness of the flesh, whether through an ingrained habit of vices or in suffering.

Strengthened according to his power, so that you too may endure all things in the same way,

according to his glory, with all patience and long-suffering,

and with joy giving thanks to God the Father—not from necessity—

who made us worthy. May your calling make you rejoice more than sufferings distress you,

for a share in the lot of the saints. In Scripture we frequently find “lot” used for inheritance,

in the light—that is, in the knowledge of God rather than ignorance.

He rescued us from the power of darkness, because everyone is the servant of the one by whom he is overcome.

It should be noted that he himself rescued us, not our power or nature, by which we were children of wrath,

and transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of his love—from the kingdom of error and death, so that we might be beloved and sons.

In him we have redemption through his blood,

and the forgiveness of sins. Redeemed by his blood, through baptism he forgave sins.

He is the image of the invisible God.

According to his humanity, without sin; for according to his divinity he is not an image but the truth. Through this image the Lord revealed the Father to Philip.

This image is truth; this image is righteousness—not mute, because it is the Word of God; not insensible, because it is wisdom; not empty, because it is power; not vacant, because it is the fullness of life; not dead, because it is resurrection.

Image, equality, and likeness must be distinguished. Where there is an image, there is immediately likeness, but not immediately equality. Where there is equality, there is immediately likeness, but not immediately an image. Where there is likeness, there is not immediately an image or equality.

Thus, in a mirror there is the image of a human being because it has been formed from that person; there is also necessarily likeness, but not equality, because many things belonging to the person from whom it was formed are absent from the image.

Where there is equality, there is immediately likeness, but not immediately an image—as with two equal eggs. Since there is equality, there is also likeness: whatever is present in one is present in the other. Yet there is no image, because neither has been formed from the other.

Where there is likeness, there is not immediately an image or equality. Every egg, insofar as it is an egg, is like every other egg. But although a partridge’s egg, insofar as it is an egg, resembles a hen’s egg, it is not its image, because it was not formed from it; nor is it equal, because it is smaller and belongs to another kind of animal.

But when he says “not immediately,” he certainly means that it can sometimes be so.

There can therefore be an image in which there is also equality, as could be found in parents and children if the interval of time were absent. For the likeness of the child has been formed from the parent, so that it is rightly called an image; and it may be so great that it may rightly also be called equality, except that the parent preceded the child in time.

From this it is understood that equality can sometimes possess not only likeness but also an image, as the preceding example makes clear.

There can also sometimes be likeness and equality, although there is no image, as was said of two equal eggs.

There can also be likeness and an image without equality, as we showed in the mirror.

There can also be likeness where there are both equality and image, as we mentioned with children, except for the time by which the parents precede them.

Thus we say that one syllable is equal to another, although one precedes and the other follows.

In God, however, because the condition of time is absent—for it cannot rightly be thought that God generated the Son in time, since he created the ages through him—it follows that he is not only God’s image, because he is from him, and likeness, because he is the image, but also so fully equal that not even an interval of time is an impediment.

Another explanation: Why does an image in paintings have likeness, while people do not want to be unlike one another? Arius contends that the Son is unlike the Father and wants the Father to beget one unlike himself.

The firstborn of every creature. The first brought forth in the flesh of every rational creature. He says “firstborn,” not “first-created,” so that he may be believed to be both begotten by nature and first in perpetuity—or certainly the firstborn from the dead.

For in him all things were created in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones, dominions, principalities, or powers.

“In him,” because he is always the same, as Jude says: “Jesus delivered his people from the land of Egypt.” And: “No one has ascended into heaven except the one who descended from heaven, the Son of Man.”

All things were created through him and in him. All things were made through him, and what was made in him is life.

And he is before all creatures,

and all things hold together in him. They live.

And he is the head of the body, the Church; he is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead. In this way he is the head of the Church.

So that he himself might hold first place in everything. For this reason he rose first.

Because in him it was pleasing that all the fullness of divinity should dwell. For divinity did not dwell so fully in anyone else. In others grace was partial; in him nature was perfect.

Bodily. For divinity is not a body.

But because he calls the sacraments of the Old Testament a shadow of what was to come, he said that the fullness of divinity dwells bodily in Christ by comparison with the shadows: everything represented in those shadows is fulfilled in him, and thus, in a certain sense, he himself is the body of those shadows—that is, he himself is the truth of those figures and signs.

Another explanation: perfectly, as though he said, “in sum.”

And through him to reconcile all things to himself: earthly things with heavenly things, which had been separated from them by opposition of life. Hence the Lord teaches us to pray that God’s will may be done on earth as in heaven.

Making peace through the blood of his cross, whether the things in heaven or the things on earth. Through these things human beings have been corrected.

And you, when you were once alienated and enemies in mind through evil works. He explained our enmity with God and his ministers.

But now he has reconciled you in the body of his flesh through death, in which you were all baptized,

so that he might present you holy and immaculate. Do not make his benefit void and become enemies again.

And irreproachable. Consider how perfect he wants each believer to be,

before him, not before human beings,

if indeed you remain founded, stable, and immovable in the faith. You will then be able to be immaculate, if human examples do not deceive you, but you firmly believe the things to come.

From the hope of the Gospel that you heard. No one can hope for the hope of the Gospel unless he lives according to it,

which has been proclaimed in every creature under heaven.

It should be noted that human beings are called every creature.

Of this Gospel I, Paul, became a minister, and now rejoice in sufferings for you. He suffers for us in order to build us up. Yet Christ also suffered beforehand for him.

And I complete in my flesh what is lacking in the sufferings of Christ for his body. Christ was brought to death by the Jews alone; therefore, for his Church, Christ began the passion through the Gentiles but did not complete it. Now it is completed in his body, that is, in the Church.

Which is the Church.

Of this Church I became a minister, according to God’s stewardship that was given to me for you,

through the gift of the Holy Spirit and the Gospel teaching that he was commanded to distribute to you,

in order to fulfill the word of God: the mystery that was hidden from ages and generations.

So that through me the preaching might be fulfilled.

But now it has been manifested to his saints, at the time when he wished to reveal it.

To them God wished to make known the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, because the same God, rich toward all, did as he wished, since his will is just.

Which is Christ in you. He himself is the mystery that has been revealed to the Gentiles.

The hope of glory, whom we proclaim to you, through whom you hope for future glory.

Correcting every person and teaching every person in all wisdom—Jew and Greek, slave and free.

And this should be noted: he wishes to present all people as perfect, according to that perfection of which he says elsewhere, “Let all who are perfect think this way,” although earlier he said, “Brothers, I do not consider that I have apprehended,” and so forth.

But there is a certain imperfect perfection, whereby a person knows that he is not perfect in this life.

So that we may present every person perfect in Christ Jesus. This is said by synecdoche: the whole is spoken for the part.

For this I also labor, striving according to his activity, which he works in me in power—in signs.

## Chapter Two

For I want you to know what concern I have for you and for those who are at Laodicea: an agony—

and for all the others who have not seen my face in the flesh,

so that their hearts may be comforted, instructed in love, and in all the riches of the fullness of understanding, in the knowledge of the mystery of God the Father and of the Lord Jesus Christ.

For if they had seen me, and my love toward them, and had more fully understood the riches of God’s mystery, they would both have experienced the greater affection of my presence and been taught by me, who learned specifically from Christ, the abundance of reasoning.

In him are all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge, which were hidden, although they were present in the writings of the Law, as Isaiah says: “In the treasures is our salvation.” Christ came as wisdom and knowledge from the Lord.

These are the sevenfold treasures of the graces of the Holy Spirit.

Hidden—treasures that were covered from Moses by a veil.

Now I say this so that no one may deceive you with lofty speech. Therefore I say that it would have been better for me to instruct you in person; nevertheless, I have briefly gathered together the whole matter: that every treasure of wisdom and knowledge is in him. Thus you should not only fail to admire every word or thought that is apart from him, but also reckon it foolishness.

For although I am absent in body, I am with you in spirit. He had this grace: that, being elsewhere, he recognized what was happening elsewhere, just as Elisha saw in the spirit Gehazi running after Naaman.

Rejoicing and seeing your order. I both see it and desire, when present, to complete whatever is lacking.

And the firmness of your faith, which is in Christ. The supplement is to believe that God is true and that the human being is true—one person from two substances—for this is the foundation of faith, sufficient for you unto life, even if for the time being you possess somewhat less knowledge.

Therefore, just as you received Christ Jesus our Lord, walk in him, rooted in him, believing him to be God and human,

and built up in him. Let a strong building grow upon the strength of the foundation.

And established in the faith, just as you learned—in the things to come—

abounding in him in thanksgiving: always increasing in him and offering more abundant thanks for his gifts.

See to it that no one deceives you through philosophy and empty deceit.

He is arguing against the philosophers, whose entire discussion concerns the elements and visible creatures, and who judge God’s power from natural things. They say that nothing can be made from nothing; that the soul either has no beginning or is mortal; that a virgin cannot give birth; and that it is foolish to believe that God is born from a human being, dies, and rises again.

According to the tradition of human beings, according to the elements of the world—a seduction—

and not according to Christ. Whoever thinks according to Christ thinks soundly.

Because in him all the fullness of divinity dwells. The fullness of divine power dwells bodily in his body,

and you are in him substantially and truly,

filled in him, who is the head of every principality and power.

If you are taught the knowledge of him who gave a beginning even to invisible creation, what will those contribute to you who understand nothing beyond what they see?

In him you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made by hand. Here he censures the Jews and the false apostles, so that you may not be led astray by them either.

In the stripping off of the body of flesh, but in the circumcision of Jesus Christ, through which you stripped off the whole old human being.

Buried with him, having died with him, in baptism.

This is Christ’s circumcision.

In him you also rose through faith in the activity of God, who raised him from the dead. You rose into a new life, believing and understanding that this was his activity.

And when you were dead in transgressions and in the foreskin of your flesh—when you were not only uncircumcised but were likewise subject to eternal death—

although you were therefore unworthy in two ways, you were made sharers in the sons.

He made you alive together with him, forgiving you all transgressions,

blotting out what stood against us, removing the causes of the death of sin.

The bond of the decree, which was voided and was contrary to us.

Some say that the bond is like a written record of sins kept with God. Hence he says in the Canticle: “Are not these things gathered up with me and sealed in my treasures?” And in Jeremiah: “The sin of Judah is written with an adamantine stylus.”

These things were therefore erased on the cross. In forgiving sins, he also abolished the memory of transgressions.

Christ redeemed us from the curse of the Law, having become a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.”

And he himself removed it from the midst, fastening it to the cross. He not only mortified sins on the cross, but also bestowed incorruption and rewards through an undeserved death.

Stripping principalities and powers: so that through death he might destroy the one who held the dominion of death, offering himself to death on behalf of the guilty.

He led them forth boldly, taking sins upon himself and absolving sinners while fastening them to the cross.

Triumphing over them openly—publicly crucified—

in himself. He disregarded shame, not by killing but by dying, not by using force but by enduring, in order to give us an example after all pride in conquering had been broken.

Therefore let no one judge you in food or drink. There is no judgment in this matter, because, since it was a shadow, it ceased when the body came; nor is an image needed when the truth is present.

Or concerning a portion of a festival day: the Calends or the new moon,

or the new moon, or Sabbaths. The new moon had the figure of a new life or a second life; the Sabbath, the rest of the life to come.

These are a shadow of things to come. The Law was the shadow; the body is Christ.

But the body of Christ. These things were future, but are now present.

Let no one deceive you, wishing to do so in humility and the worship of angels, dwelling on things he has not seen, vainly puffed up by the disposition of his flesh.

Let no one be proud under the pretense of humility, because he falsely claims to see angels and therefore vainly exalts himself above human beings, speaking of visions from his own heart.

And not holding fast to the head—not believing in Christ, the head of all the saints—

from whom the whole body, the Church, is supplied through bonds and connections, because the members are joined together from the head to the feet.

Therefore whoever is outside this body, however much he may boast, does not live, since he has neither the head nor life.

And it is built up and grows into the increase of God—that is, into the increase of the body that is united to God.

If you have died with Christ to the elements of this world. The elements of this world can also be defined as avarice, ambition for honors, and other worldly things.

Why, as though living in the world, do you make decrees? He did not want us even to have the appearance of those who live in the world,

such as: “Do not touch, do not taste, do not handle.”

By their touch, taste, and handling—those who misuse such things in their desires and love them in place of eternal things—

all of which perish through use itself.

From the parts of the world, understand its condition: its members too must necessarily perish, so that the whole may one day be dissolved.

Therefore its elements should not be worshiped as mortal things, nor loved in place of eternal things.

According to the precepts and teachings of human beings, which indeed have an appearance of wisdom in superstition and humility, and in not sparing the body, but are not of any honor in satisfying the flesh.

Some understand the whole passage as directed against those who had believed from the Jews and said that the ceremonies of the Law ought to be observed. Therefore he calls them human teachings, because they understand the precepts carnally, saying that what is forbidden in the Law must not be eaten.

All those observances, although the commandments of the Law may seem to display a certain wisdom, are nevertheless superstitious in the honor they assign to God, because they serve to fulfill the will of a carnal observance.

Others understand the whole chapter in this way: the Apostle wished to recall us from arguments about the elements, to which philosophers persuaded us, although they may seem rational, lest through their good things we be led into evil.

Human beings too, taught by nature, handed down that the world would one day be dissolved. Therefore they worshiped the one God, whom they understood to be alone eternal—although superstitiously, nevertheless humbly—and said that the body should not be spared, nor the flesh burdened with satiety, since it too would die.

## Chapter Three
Therefore, if you have been raised with Christ. Consequently, he first says that we have died together with him and then that we have risen, and he urges us not merely to die to the earth but also to live for heaven. Seek the things that are above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God. Set your minds on the things that are above, not on those that are upon the earth. Do not pursue anything earthly; seek nothing mortal; pursue heavenly wisdom, not earthly wisdom.

For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God. You have died to earthly life through your conduct as citizens of the heavenly homeland. For when Christ, your life, appears—for since we are children of God, what we shall be has not yet appeared, but we know only this: that when he appears, we shall be like him—then you also will appear with him in glory. Therefore, do not seek your glory here and now.

Put to death, therefore. Fulfill your profession. Your members that are upon the earth. He means the members of vices, which are ours because they come from us; or else, as is customary, he calls the evil use of the members “members.” Fornication, impurity, lust. Every form of lack of self-control can be called impurity, and also lust. Evil desire. For there is also good desire; hence Daniel was called “a man of desires.” And greed, which is the service of idols. While we serve the metals from which idols are made, and venerate gold in place of God—for whoever serves God alone venerates one ineffable image.

Because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the children of unbelief. Upon Sodom and those who perished in the flood. From past events, therefore, future things are to be feared. Or, upon those who were unbelieving in the wilderness. It should be noted what we were before the grace of Christ.

Among whom you also once walked, when you lived in them. Do not walk in them now, lest you appear to have believed in vain. But now put away all these things: anger, indignation. These are what remained with us from Adam, namely, the vices that follow. Malice. Malice is inflicting upon another what you would not wish to suffer yourself. Blasphemy. Against God or his image. Shameful speech from your mouth. For if such lack of discipline is unbecoming even to human beings who have been more honorably educated, how much more is it unbecoming to God’s people?

Do not lie to one another. It is not fitting for children of truth to lie, since falsehood comes from the devil. Strip off the old human being with his deeds. The sins of our origin, or the pleasure of the flesh. And put on the new. Christ, and the virtues that come from him. The one who is renewed in knowledge according to the image of the one who created him. When he recognizes whose image he is, he ought, insofar as he can, to strive with that one’s help to become like him.

Where there is neither male nor female, gentile nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, barbarian nor Scythian, slave nor free. Before God, sex, status, lineage, and province do not count; only one’s manner of life together with right faith is required. But Christ is all and in all. All of you who were baptized have put on Christ.

Put on, therefore, as God’s chosen ones—putting away those things and putting on these—holy and beloved, compassionate hearts, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience. Since he had called the former things “members,” he therefore calls these things “hearts.” Bearing with one another. Following the example of Christ, who bore our weaknesses, both spiritual and bodily. And forgiving one another. Forgiving each other, just as Christ forgave everyone, even his persecutors.

If anyone has a complaint against another, do not demand small debts from fellow servants, lest you reclaim what has already been forgiven. Just as the Lord forgave you, so also should you. Here he explains how we ought to forgive one another: if the one who could take vengeance forgave, how much more should you, whose vengeance is either small or nonexistent, forgive?

Above all these things have love. Love is above all these things, because we bear everyone whom we love, but we do not love everyone whom we bear. Yet we must love everyone for God’s sake. Which is the bond of perfection. Love joins many members into one body.

And the peace of Christ. Of Christ, not of the world, which loves only those who love it. Let it rejoice in your hearts, in which you were also called in one body. Not with a feigned and cheerful face, or with deceitful speech. And be grateful. That is: do not imitate the Law, which repays in kind, but grace, which forgives even enemies and intercedes for them.

Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly. Here it is also shown that even lay people ought to possess the word of Christ not merely sufficiently but abundantly, and that they should admonish and teach one another. Teaching and admonishing yourselves in all wisdom. So that what is spoken may be expressed wisely and rationally.

In psalms. Of David. In hymns. Of the three youths. In songs. Of Moses and all the prophets. Spiritual songs. Not carnal songs, after the manner of the world. Singing with grace. We never read of singing without the voice. To God in your hearts. So that you sing not only with your mouth but also in your heart, so that the heart agrees with the voice, or so that you understand what you sing.

Whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him. Whether you teach or work, do nothing for your own glory, but do everything for the Lord, giving thanks to God, who has deigned to send his Son to inspire and teach these things.

Wives, be subject to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord. In those matters that accord with the Lord. Husbands, love your wives and do not be bitter toward them. Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing in the Lord. He would never exhort them concerning a natural duty unless they had begun to be continent, as has been more fully noted in the letter to the Ephesians.

Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, so that they do not become fainthearted. Do not exasperate them so that they become irritable, but let them learn patience from your example.

Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything. Because they serve the flesh, not the spirit. Not serving merely when they are watched, as people-pleasers. When your masters see you. But with sincerity of heart, fearing God.

Whatever you do, work from the heart, as for the Lord and not for human beings, knowing that you will receive the reward of an inheritance from the Lord. He sees everywhere and always, and hates every false creation. For the human eye can be deceived; therefore act so that you turn the necessity of your condition into an act of willing devotion, so that, when everyone sees you, thanks may be returned to the Lord on account of your good works, because you have made progress in the Christian life.

Serve the Lord Christ. For the one who serves a human being for Christ’s sake serves Christ himself.

For whoever does wrong will receive what he has done unjustly, and there is no partiality with God. Whether a slave who has despised his master, or a master who has treated his slave unjustly, so that he may be comforted, knowing that before God the wrong done to him is not great.

## CHAPTER IV

Masters, provide your slaves with what is just and equitable. You ought to regard yourselves more as fathers than as masters; hence you are commonly called heads of households. Knowing that you also have a Lord in heaven. Therefore, whatever sort of Lord you want to have, be such toward your fellow servants rather than toward slaves.

Devote yourselves to prayer, keeping watch in it. For a careless and drowsy petition will not be able to obtain anything even from a human being. Pray together with thanksgiving. For all the things that have been granted to you, and also amid adversities, which occur by his own dispensation. For one would not ask him in prayer unless one believed that it was granted by him, so that the door might be opened for speech—that is, so that the beginning of faith might be granted to the hearts of the hearers.

And pray for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ. What you pray for us, he will perfect in you as teaching. For how is the door of the word opened except when the understanding of the hearer is opened, so that he may believe, and, once the beginning of faith has been made, receive the things preached and discussed for the building up of saving doctrine, lest, with the heart closed through unbelief, he reject and repel what is said?

For this reason I am also imprisoned, so that I may make it manifest, as I ought to speak. So that he himself may grant what should rationally be preached, when, and to whom; for while we preach into the ears, he meanwhile works in the heart.

Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside, redeeming the time. For the days are evil. By your wisdom you will make good use of an evil time; or, if necessary, despise even some temporal thing for the sake of your repose, so that it may perish.

Let your speech always be seasoned with the salt of grace. With the reasoning of wisdom, lest our religion be judged foolish by philosophers and gentiles, so that you may know how you ought to answer each person. As Peter also says.

Always be ready to give an answer: one response to pagans, another to Jews, another to heretics, another to philosophers, another to astrologers, and another to the rest.

Tychicus, the most beloved brother, faithful minister, and fellow servant in the Lord, will make known to you everything concerning me. He wants them to be secure about him, so that they may not be overcome by sadness.

I have sent him to you for this very purpose: that he may learn about your circumstances and comfort your hearts, together with Onesimus, the beloved and faithful brother, who is one of you. They will make known to you everything that is happening here.

For us. Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you, and Mark, the cousin of Barnabas, concerning whom you received instructions. He is held with me in chains, or else shares my imprisonment through the affection of love. If he comes to you, receive him. And Jesus, who is called Justus. These are from the circumcision. They had received these instructions from him. These alone are my fellow workers for the kingdom of God, and they have been a comfort to me.

These alone are with me; or, these alone from the circumcision are fellow workers in the New Testament, through which one enters the kingdom, just as Satan is called death because he is the cause of death.

Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ Jesus, greets you. He is always concerned for you in his prayers. He is truly a servant of Christ who is found to be concerned for Christ’s body, so that you may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God. In his prayers he asks God that you may persevere in the will of God, and that the one who began the work in you may himself bring it to completion.

For I bear him witness that he has much labor on behalf of you, and of those who are in Laodicea and Hierapolis. Such were the disciples of the first age, imitators of Paul and of Christ.

Luke, the most beloved physician, greets you, and Demas.

Greet the brothers who are in Laodicea, and Nympha and the church that is in her house. When the letter has been read among you, see that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you read the one from Laodicea. For she had such people in her house as the Apostle defined a church to be.

And say to Archippus: “See to the ministry that you received in the Lord, so that you may fulfill it.” He is understood to have been a deacon, not a bishop; for a bishop would not have needed to be admonished in the church to preserve his ministry.

The greeting in my own hand, Paul’s. Remember my chains. Either pray that I may be restored to you, or remember that I suffer these things because of you, and imitate my example.

Grace be with you. Amen. Grace is truly with those who remain with it and confess that they received it freely.

# THE FIRST LETTER TO TIMOTHY

[Col. 0659]

## ARGUMENT

[Col. 0659D]

He instructs Timothy and teaches him concerning the ordering of the episcopate, the diaconate, and the whole discipline of the Church. Written from the city of Rome. Timothy was a bishop and a disciple of Paul. Through this letter Paul grants him authority to correct the whole ecclesiastical discipline and to ordain bishops and deacons. Moreover, he instructs him how to answer the false apostles who disparage Paul, giving the explanation that it is not surprising if he himself was saved from being a persecutor, since Christ came to save sinners. Finally, he warns that those who teach otherwise must be avoided and guarded against in every way.

## CHAPTER I

Paul, an apostle of Christ. He sets forth both the authority of his name and of his office. According to the command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope. Not according to my own presumption. At the same time he shows that the Father and the Son have one command.

To Timothy, my beloved son in faith. Not in the flesh. Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

As I urged you to remain in Ephesus when I was going to Macedonia, so that you might warn certain people not to teach otherwise. These are the people whom he had foretold in Acts would enter as savage wolves, not sparing the flock.

Nor to devote themselves to myths. He calls them myths from Genesis, that is, myths according to the Law, for which they are accused by the Lord while teaching human doctrines. And to endless genealogies, which produce questions rather than God’s building up, which is in faith. The genealogies of the ancients, in which they claim supreme knowledge if they enumerate the generations from the beginning: both the contradictions of their secondary elaborations and their concern with genealogies are superfluous.

But the goal of the commandment is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith. Love of God and neighbor, on which the Law and the prophets nevertheless depend. If this comes from a pure heart, it is pleasing to God, provided that nothing is loved except what ought to be loved.

He added “a good conscience” because of hope. For the person who has a prick of an evil conscience despairs of reaching what he believes and loves.

Thirdly: “And sincere faith,” he says. For if our faith is free from falsehood, so that we neither love what should not be loved nor, by living rightly, hope for it, our hope will in no way be frustrated. And he says, “a good conscience.” Let a pure conscience bear witness to love and sincere faith.

From these things some have gone astray. For there is a false faith, consisting only in words, whether that of heretics who seem to enter the Church or that of false Catholics.

They have turned aside to empty talk, desiring to be teachers of the Law. Into the empty talk of secular myths. Understanding neither what they say nor the matters about which they make assertions. It is great folly to wish to affirm things that are not understood concerning matters that are even less understood.

But we know that the Law is good. Against the Manichaeans he says to the Romans: “The Law is indeed holy, and the commandment is holy.” The Law is good as given by God according to the condition of human beings.

If anyone uses it lawfully. Knowing this: knowing for whom, why, and for how long it was given to be held spiritually.

Because the Law was not laid down for the just but for the unjust and disobedient. If this is so, Christians have no need of it, because they have been justified through Christ and have learned to avoid opportunities for sin. For why is it said to them, “You shall not kill”? They have not even been commanded to become angry, unless it is so that they may fulfill the Law spiritually.

For the ungodly and sinners, the wicked and defiled, murderers of fathers and mothers, murderers, fornicators, men who have intercourse with males, kidnappers, liars, perjurers, and anything else that is contrary to sound doctrine, which is according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God that was entrusted to me.

There are many unsound doctrines that make people unsound. The Law stands against those things that are contrary to the commandments of the gospel.
